evidence.note: Searches the linked monster entries in blocks of 16, stores the target page head and canvas row, and falls back to the first page if the target is absent.

Uses the same Owner/Node/Service field layout as arm9/ov014:02187228, walks from the saved page to the selected offset, updates count, resolves the selected node, and points currentValues at values. Inventory callers are arm9/ov014:02187074 and arm9/ov014:02188010.
evidence.uncertainty: The class and the count’s higher-level meaning remain unknown.

evidence.note: Converts the selected canvas row into a node on the current page, clamps to its final entry, updates the row, and refreshes the selected monster value buffer.

For each parsed entry, resolves a value and sets bit 1 of entry flags when the resolved value’s low ten bits are nonzero. The exact caller arm9/ov014:02187568 performs resource and display initialization, but that caller does not prove Filesystem ownership; the proposed destination removes that unsupported classification.
evidence.uncertainty: The resolved value and entry type semantics are not established.

evidence.note: Iterates bestiary entries and enables their discovered flag when the corresponding saved progress record has a nonzero low ten-bit count; the detail display prints that count.
evidence.uncertainty: Interpreting the low ten bits as defeat count follows the defeated-monster screen and display usage.

evidence.note: Counts nodes by following next from owner+0xB8 and returns a signed halfword count. The callers are four different ov014 functions; no type owner is established.
evidence.uncertainty: The list’s element type and purpose remain unknown.

evidence.note: Counts nodes in the active filtered linked monster list; used for pagination and navigation controls.

Calls three stream setup helpers, sets index and source, marks active, and calls a final setup helper. The only caller is arm9/ov014:021850cc; helper group and caller establish stream initialization but not a Filesystem owner.
evidence.uncertainty: Stream implementation and source type remain unknown.

evidence.note: Cancels and resets the habitat loader, stores its allocator and monster key, and immediately begins the queued enchab archive load.
Returns the byte at record offset 0xBA when flags contain 0x10, else returns -1. Caller arm9/ov015:0218bb3c reads selected-position matrices; this alone does not identify the record owner.
evidence.uncertainty: Record flag and byte semantics remain unknown.

evidence.note: Returns the render-command byte at 0xAE only when flag 0x10 is set, otherwise -1. The matrix capture hook compares it against the camera model bone indices.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact engine name for this render-command index and flag is not established.

evidence.note: Sets entry value and active fields to zero. Three direct callers in ov015 use it in a common initialization sequence; the body supports the reset operation but not a broader subsystem.
evidence.uncertainty: Entry type and active-field role remain unknown.

evidence.note: Clears a reservation slot pointer and its active flag; called on every slot in the three viewer VRAM banks during state initialization.

Loads an optional pointer at p+0x6AC and calls EnableField55F4Bits2And4 on it when non-null. Caller arm9/ov017:021CBC0C processes a lighting entry, but the field’s type and ownership are not established by that call alone. Coordinator traced EnableField55F4Bits: argument is OR mask, not bit index. Two calls use masks2 and4, hence combinedmask0x06; retain exact child+0x6ac precondition.
evidence.uncertainty: Child type and field 0x6AC meaning remain unknown.

evidence.note: Checks the owned battle scene and forwards to BattleScene_MarkPartyAndMonsterSetupReady, enabling its party and monster setup bits.

Reads origin x/y at offsets 0x22/0x24 and width/height at 0x26/0x28, then outputs x, y, x+width, y+height. The consumer arm9/ov023:021FD46C uses selected-coordinate bounds, but object ownership remains unclassified.
evidence.uncertainty: Coordinate units and the receiver type remain unknown.

evidence.note: Outputs left/top from +0x22/+0x24 and computes right/bottom by adding width/height +0x26/+0x28. The coordinate-inside helper uses these bounds for a half-open rectangle test.
Writes six consecutive words as 0, -1, 0, 0, 0, 0. Multiple ov025 callers use this initializer; the name describes the exact write pattern without inventing record semantics.
evidence.uncertainty: Record type and sentinel meaning remain unknown.

evidence.note: Clears the six-word procedure state and initializes its resource/task selector to minus one; timer, loader, effect and zone-transition callbacks share this scratch record.
evidence.uncertainty: The second word has different uses across action procedure callbacks.

evidence.note: Copies data_ov028_021d9a34, installs data_020e6d5c into slot 3, dispatches the current phase’s member-function pointer when non-null, and returns whether the phase had no handler. Nearby ov028 data relocations bind the phase table; caller group includes ov001 and ov028. The precise dispatch operation is supported; the receiver class is not.

evidence.note: Copies the credit phase member-function table, invokes the current handler with elapsed ticks and reports whether the handler is absent.
Adds table.base to table.values[(unsigned short)index]. Multiple callers in ov031 use the computed address; the operation is clear but the table owner is not.
evidence.uncertainty: Table element semantics and subsystem owner remain unknown.

evidence.note: Indexes the message offset array with a 16-bit message ID and adds the offset to the message string-data base; callers retrieve text from the BMG table.

Writes its byte argument at data_ov031_02290ca0+1. Existing module-qualified callers include ov031 graphics, network and system functions; those contexts disagree on owner, while the byte write itself is precise.
evidence.uncertainty: The global context and byte field meaning require the enclosing state type.

evidence.note: Stores the entry-origin byte used by initialization to choose its header and by action-12 cleanup to choose the return screen. Existing-profile callers pass zero; the method chooser passes one.
evidence.uncertainty: The byte distinguishes list entry and return paths; a stronger user-facing name for the two origins is not established.

evidence.note: Dereferences the pointer at data_ov031_02290ce8 and writes 1 at object+0x604. Direct callers in ov031 include graphics resource-loading functions; the body gives a precise field operation but does not establish ownership.
evidence.uncertainty: The referenced object type and field meaning remain unknown.

evidence.note: Sets the tilemap object dirty flag at +0x604. Overlay_LoadPendingBG2ScreenData consumes and clears that flag after uploading the buffered main BG2 screen data.

Calls the established helper SendOperation18WithHalfwordValue with literal 1 and returns its result. The direct caller is arm9/ov031:02227468, a display cleanup routine, but the helper’s operation-18 domain is not established as Graphics-owned.
evidence.uncertainty: Operation 18’s protocol or subsystem meaning remains unknown.

evidence.note: Cleanup wrapper calls PowerManagement_SendCommandEighteenSynchronously with value one; no narrower command meaning is established by this body.
evidence.uncertainty: The effect of power-management command eighteen with argument one is not proven here.

evidence.note: Complete body conditionally invokes its callback and returns token 0x001beb10. Parent original module-qualified evidence binds this wrapper to protected gate three and script opcode0x32f driver arm9/ov001:02162338, which checks three expected tokens and counter increments1/2/3 after loading overlay29; matching startup gate results affect loader initialization. Original encoded code analysis proves runtime code-signature, cartridge-read, MAC/config checks and decode/call/re-encode mechanisms. System/Protection is supported by this whole sequence, not by generic hardware callers. Existing nominal return type is preserved; token interpretation changes only naming/ownership.
evidence.uncertainty: Exact vendor/protection designation and particular device failure behavior are not proven. No type, body, constant, embedded string or execution change.

evidence.note: Token wrapper or exact +1/+2/+3 counter callback used by opcode 0x32F.
evidence.uncertainty: Static analysis establishes mechanics and traced call-site roles; vendor, device-specific outcome and gameplay penalty are not established.

evidence.note: First releases completed buffers/requeues nonfence tasks, then adds a processing lock and waits until flags78C.3 and GP2operationInFlight are clear under resource mutex.
evidence.uncertainty: Class layout and parameters are preserved; no gameplay owner is inferred for caller objects.

evidence.note: Releases task scratch blocks, zeroes queued task records, resets queue length, left scratch boundary and processlocks; external buffers are not freed here.
evidence.uncertainty: Class layout and parameters are preserved; no gameplay owner is inferred for caller objects.

evidence.note: Frees scratch and external buffers for completed tasks, resets nonfence tasks to unallocated, aborts current reader and updates processing flags.
evidence.uncertainty: Class layout and parameters are preserved; no gameplay owner is inferred for caller objects.

evidence.note: Installs base dispatch, initializes/resets BackgroundLoader state and installs concrete process dispatch. Explicit C shim; no inferred original C++ class spelling.
evidence.uncertainty: Class layout and parameters are preserved; no gameplay owner is inferred for caller objects.

evidence.note: Restores base dispatch then initializes/resets BackgroundLoader state; flags parameter and nominal ABI are retained. Does not claim deallocation.
evidence.uncertainty: Class layout and parameters are preserved; no gameplay owner is inferred for caller objects.

evidence.note: Copies the party member name and heading stats, unspent skill points into the initial and remaining budgets, current vocation and level, and its five mapped skill IDs and invested point totals. Clears per-row restrictions and sets the allocation cap to 100; CopyFiveIndexedValuesToObject commits remaining points and base-plus-pending skill totals back to these same member fields.

Finds the requested ready text record in the allocation display owner and sets or clears bit 0x40 at record+0xc5. For record zero it also reformats and reloads the five-skill allocation text. Editing sets this flag when entering prompt/confirmation states; notice dismissal and confirmation cancellation clear it.
evidence.uncertainty: The renderer-wide meaning of record flag 0x40 is not established; the name describes its proven use during allocation prompt transitions rather than claiming a visibility or input-disable effect.

evidence.note: Stores the saved recipe progress array and count in the inventory context; initialization supplies the decoded 471 recipe records.
Allocates the scene display buffers, two recipe-preview allocators, six resource arenas, four sprite arenas and seventeen render records; called by menu allocation.
Initializes sprite render defaults, invalidates its task and item ID, and clears preview coordinates and pending-load state; used for each of four preview slots.
Loads selected recipe or ingredient archives from GP2, builds keyed preview data, swaps allocators and updates three ingredient names, required counts and party-held counts.
Advances the main scene loader through resource, canvas, layout, script and character model loading; installs ren_in animation and bone hooks before activating the scene.
Cancels pending tasks for four item sprites, initializes each slot and binds its render resource, placement and palette defaults.
For each pending preview sprite, polls its task, resets the corresponding allocator, installs loaded sprite data, removes the task and updates sprite coordinates.
ORs the pending-load bytes across all four result/ingredient preview sprites and returns whether any load remains.
Forwards the quantity argument to the embedded display byte at 0x799; the caller passes the current batch quantity. The reconstructed one-argument declaration omits the preserved argument.
Allocates nine item ID/count categories, ten arenas, recipe progress, selection widgets, text/render buffers and the scene owner; decodes saved recipe state and allocates sixteen name buffers.
Initializes packed item fields and sentinel ID, clears two embedded data buffers and binds their pointers; used for the result and three ingredient descriptors.
Updates scene and display widgets, selection input and pending dialogue; blocks interaction during scene transitions and dispatches the current menu screen handler.
Returns when the menu screen is inactive; otherwise calls the owned scene renderer, which configures its camera and draws the four pot/character/effect Object3D instances.
Sets a one-shot latch and pending exit byte; the menu update consumes that byte by clearing selection and entering its exit screen.
Walks from the current recipe page head to the requested row; clamps at the final node and updates the selected row when the list ends early.
Resets the ingredient page to zero and derives a minimum-one page count from the selected category's item count using eight entries per page.
Clears all three reserved slots, handles category/item/quantity selection and reserves the first ingredient before entering second-ingredient selection; cancel returns to mode selection.
Handles the next category/item/quantity selection and reserves an ingredient before entering third-ingredient selection; backing out restores the last reserved slot.
Handles the third ingredient and quantity, reserves it, asks for confirmation and enters manual synthesis; rejecting synthesis restores all reserved quantities.
Browses recipes with accept/back/detail actions, resolves stock requirements, loads result preview, handles confirmation and selects an ingredient-limited batch before synthesis.
Builds eight ingredient name/quantity rows for the selected category, subtracts the actively selected amount from its displayed stock and updates page indicators.
Waits for the result sprite task, resets its dedicated menu allocator, installs loaded sprite data, removes the task and reports completion.
Registered as interrupt mask 1 handler; applies brightness when scene 17 is loaded, increments frame count and acknowledges VBlank.
Saves math-unit context, CPSR, supervisor SP and user registers; returns zero initially and resumes with saved r0 equal to one.
Restores math-unit context, status, supervisor SP and user register bank, then resumes via exception return.
Sets CP15 control bit 18, enabling instruction tightly coupled memory.
Sets CP15 control bit zero; invoked before dispatching the registered exception callback.
Clears CP15 control bit zero while preserving the remaining processor control settings.
Chains the preserved handler, switches to a fixed exception stack, captures abort/undefined context and then spins.
evidence.uncertainty: The listing classifies the trailing restore sequence as unreachable bytes; the normal path spins after capture.

evidence.note: Called for abort/undefined modes; first records faulting processor context, then dispatches the optional exception callback.
Copies saved low registers, r4-r11, status, fault PC and banked SP/LR into the shared exception record.
Checks for a registered callback, switches processor mode and stack, enables protection and passes exception record plus callback argument.
Locks card access, restricts interrupts, stops four DMA channels, stores reset parameter and sends ARM7 reset command before DTCM reset entry.
Restores divider operands/control and square-root operand/control at the math-unit MMIO registers; paired with CP_SaveContext.
Runs pre-sleep callbacks, saves display/interrupt state, configures wake triggers, sends ARM7 sleep request and halts until wake; restores state and runs post-sleep callbacks.
Loops until RTC busy word at shared state +12 differs from one; synchronous date/time wrappers call it.
Once on supported hardware reads slot-2 header under bus lock, populates shared cartridge identity and sends module info address to ARM7; waits for acknowledgement.
Sums halfwords with end-around carry, handles odd buffer alignment and trailing byte, then adds into existing 16-bit checksum state.
Activates within the configured frame window, advances the phase, selects main/sub OAM, writes sprite coordinates/tile/palette, and writes a diagonal affine matrix using reciprocal fixed-point scale.

Looks up requested signed keys; with an allocator deduplicates keys, copies linked records and strings, and sorts by record key. Without one it preserves existing destination buffers; initializes unused slots.
Builds category/subtype bit masks from optional byte lists, counts matching primary and linked records, allocates storage, and copies matching records through the deep-copy helper.
evidence.uncertainty: The recovered public caller describes its selectors as keys, but the assembly consumes byte lists and tests packed category/subtype bits; the name follows the body.

evidence.note: For a negative key copies all group/entry bytes and payload bytes, relocates pointers, and marks ready. For a nonnegative key searches one group, copies its entries, and duplicates their strings.
Attaches the source table, counts requested keys found by signed-halfword binary search, allocates entries, resolves and duplicates each string, then sorts output entries by signed key.
Initializes display-tag state, dispatches case-folded named tags through the encoder table, translates newline forms to FF18, handles numeric tags, copies ordinary bytes, and appends FF01 plus NUL.

Finds the item ID, subtracts the requested quantity, and when the resulting signed count is nonpositive invalidates its ID, clears count and compacts later occupied slots; returns whether the ID existed.

If the ROM-table buffer is absent, queries table size and available arena space, pauses BackgroundLoader, allocates the table buffer near the arena end using a temporary reservation, loads FAT/FNT data, resumes the loader, and refreshes cached accessors.
Captures the original bit length, appends padding, handles an extra block when needed, writes the little-endian bit count, compresses, copies 16 digest bytes and clears all 0x58 context bytes.
Processes the block at context+0x18 through the four MD5 Boolean rounds with their characteristic rotations and index schedules, then adds the results to four chaining words.
Registers ARM7 command channel 7, links 256 records at stride 24, resets pending and in-flight bookkeeping, initializes shared status, queues opcode 29 with its address and flushes.
Compares the cached completion counter to invalidated ARM7 shared status, optionally waits, removes the next in-flight batch and appends its linked records to the free pool under IRQ protection.

Under IRQ protection limits outstanding batches to eight, cleans the record pool, sends the pending head on ARM7 channel 7, records it in a nine-slot ring and advances serial counters; flags allow waiting and an extra wakeup.

Recognizable NitroSDK sound-bank assignment: replaces the indexed eight-byte bank link, unlinks its prior wave archive chain, inserts it at the new wave archive head under the sound mutex, and cleans both headers.
Advances tag-0x48 request phases through connection cleanup, display request 0x20e, owner reset, message/resource 0x3e completion and scene restoration; non-boss zones finish immediately.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact narrative event associated with this reset/message sequence is unproven.

evidence.note: Refreshes plane-mask snapshots, checks scene availability, restores normal display when disabled, counts down activation, initializes or uploads overlay sprites, and migrates the overlay when screen selection changes.
For nonzero yaw, rejects points beyond the supplied squared XZ radius, rotates the point about the pivot by negative yaw, then tests inclusive bounds.
Checks enabled/visible flags, positive alpha and frame entries; loads object translation and signed Y scale before drawing each textured entry.
Builds texture and palette attributes from the eight-byte entry, sets polygon/color state, and submits four texture-coordinate/vertex pairs as a quad.
Accepts at most four input IDs, compacts valid IDs 1..32 into the queue, resets its stage/task state, starts the first resource load, and broadcasts the original list.
Polls primary and secondary resource tasks, loads CMOT/CCHR animation packages, runs start/loop/end animation stages, advances queued IDs, and removes tasks on completion or interruption.
Processes 64-byte blocks using five state words, big-endian input, rotate-left-1 message expansion, and the SHA-1 choose/parity/majority round sequence before accumulating state.
evidence.uncertainty: SHA-1 algorithm is identifiable; exact original SDK/private symbol spelling is not established.

evidence.note: Writes cosine,sine,-sine,cosine into a fixed-point 2x2 matrix; callers immediately scale the resulting rotation matrix.
Writes the fixed-point 3x3 X-axis rotation using supplied sine/cosine and identity X component; recognisable SDK matrix primitive.
Computes determinant/cofactors and fixed-point reciprocal for a 3x3 inverse, returns -1 for singular matrices, and handles aliased input through a stack matrix.
Copies twelve affine matrix components and inserts the homogeneous column 0,0,0,1000.
Writes a 4x3 X-axis sine/cosine rotation with identity X basis and zero translation.
Writes a 4x3 Y-axis sine/cosine rotation with identity Y basis and zero translation.
Writes a 4x3 Z-axis sine/cosine rotation with identity Z basis and zero translation.
Stores fixed-point 1000 on the four diagonal positions and zero in every other component of the 4x4 matrix.
Copies three components from each row and skips each fourth component to convert 4x4 to affine 4x3.
Walks the source in four-byte steps while repeatedly storing each word to the same destination; geometry FIFO callers use this SDK fixed-destination transfer primitive.
Copies exactly eight words with three load/store groups of 3,3,2 words; both source and destination advance.
Writes three groups of three zero words to consecutive addresses, clearing exactly 36 bytes for a 3x3 matrix.
Reads payload length at +8 and stages data+12 into the VRAM subregion selected by the callback index, offset zero.
Selects a callback from the screen-transfer table by engine/layer nibbles and submits the provided or stored buffer at offset zero with configured size.
Calculates palette-bank and color offsets using 32-byte or 512-byte banks, cleans the even-sized source range and invokes the engine palette callback.
Rejects nonoverlapping bounds, selects spatial-grid cells, deduplicates polygon records with a temporary visited bit and copies up to 96 overlapping polygons.
Requires the active flag, dispatches states zero through four, advances or finalizes the display and updates its page-number display afterward.
evidence.uncertainty: State three is ready and zero inactive; intermediate phase names and timing are not fully established.

evidence.note: Preprocesses text, measures its canvas size, renders markup, cleans/transfers pixels and initializes tilemap dimensions and active display state.
Saves dimensions, origins, pitches and buffer size across preprocessing/measurement, renders into that existing layout and transfers the refreshed pixels.
Parses text and angle-bracket commands, renders glyphs into tiled 4bpp pixels, stores marked rectangles and draws frames, selection decorations and separators.
Walks glyphs and layout commands without drawing, tracks extents, rounds dimensions to tiles, applies vertical alignment and computes character-buffer byte size.
Checks each corner against overlapping canvases and blits corner glyphs 0x15 through 0x18 only where no overlap is reported.
Draws top, bottom and side border glyphs and chooses alternate corner tiles from overlap classifications; optional signed insets reposition the border.
Sets destination position, size, palette and frame flags; initializes or reuses active canvas buffers, fills the interior and draws border decorations.
For a pixel Y within the canvas, fills a one-pixel-high palette-15 line from X=1 to canvas pixel width minus one.
Renders text at a supplied origin with font/color arguments, newline and coordinate/color commands, returning rendered width and height through output pointers.
When selection-marker flag 0x40 is enabled, blits four 8x8 glyphs 0x10 through 0x13 around the provided position.
Looks up two glyph keys and applies their pixel masks near the lower left and lower right of the canvas, adjusting for the borderless flag.
evidence.uncertainty: The placement and two glyph lookups are proven; the symbols themselves are not visually identified.

evidence.note: Selects the owner layer character callback, cleans the canvas pixel-buffer range and transfers it at the stored character destination offset.
Walks linked canvases on the same engine, skips hidden/ineligible canvases and classifies selected corner overlaps as aligned edges or interior coverage.
Checks page-display enable/dirty flags, optionally restores character pixels from VRAM, draws the centered separator and current/total numbers, then optionally transfers changes.
Resolves a keyed string, optionally centers or right-aligns it, preprocesses flagged text, configures font metrics and renders while recording label dimensions.
Copies six-byte source OAM attributes into eight-byte entries, applies optional fixed-point affine transform and translation, and adjusts affine mode/index and double-size origins.
Fills a subrectangle of one 8x8 character tile using masked 4bpp or 8bpp row writes, with a fast whole-tile clear path.
Clips a glyph rectangle to one 8x8 tile, reads packed source samples through BitReader and writes nonzero samples with a palette-base adjustment.
Clips glyph bounds against canvas dimensions and calls the single-tile glyph blitter while walking tiles using a row-major stride.
Performs glyph clipping and calls the single-tile blitter using Graphics_ComputePartitionedTileIndex for each destination tile.
Replicates a 4bpp or 8bpp palette index across a word and fast-fills width times height character tiles as one contiguous range.
Replicates the palette index and fast-fills each row's visible character tiles, advancing by the configured tile-row stride.
Splits a pixel rectangle into intersected 8x8 tiles and calls the masked tile-rectangle filler using row-major tile addressing.
Splits a pixel rectangle into tile fragments and uses Graphics_ComputePartitionedTileIndex before each masked tile fill.
Chooses tile partition exponents from width/height and initializes the character surface with partitioned draw/fill callbacks.
Partitions a character-tile rectangle into legal OBJ shapes, writes OAM positions, tile numbers and color mode, and recursively handles remainder strips.
Measures multiline text, offsets the origin for horizontal and vertical alignment along the supplied direction vector, then renders aligned text lines.

Opcode 101 uses the global context installed by Script_ExecuteWithFourGlobalParameters. Filters the first integer against an optional halfword allowlist, allocates a 20-byte node, packs seven parameters (float scaled by 4096), normalizes flags and prepends it to the output list. Allocation failure records error 2 and returns zero.

Copies the packed header, allocates and copies the 28-byte record array and the separately sized payload, visits every record with the three-string relocation callback, then sets the ready bit. The loader reads data/prm/mon_data.gp2, member mon_data_<LG>.nat, establishing monster-data ownership.

Checks global blocking state, enable and display-engine changes; advances obj_navi and str_navi loading, updates the animation phase, rasterizes scratch text into the last 0x800 bytes of OBJ VRAM, emits the entry notification and removes expired messages.
Computes the navigation graphics tile address near the end of OBJ VRAM, obtains the shared status index, selects the proper sprite buffer and writes a single palette-15 status sprite.
evidence.uncertainty: The gameplay meaning of the shared status index is unproven.

evidence.note: Computes a sine-based grayscale color, uploads it to OBJ palette entry 255 and emits eight 32-pixel-wide text sprites from the final 0x800 bytes of the selected engine OBJ VRAM.

Starts with the supplied required ID, uses its matched keyed rule to draw a one-to-three-entry group size and quantity, fills optional entries from weighted choices, caps the total quantity using the validation record and randomly permutes the resulting ID/quantity pairs. The owner combines monster-data at +0x2F8, member rules at +0x304 and this six-entry group table at +0x124; the monster-data loader names mon_data.gp2.
evidence.uncertainty: IDs and quantities are consistent with monster-group generation in the shared owner, but individual packed rule flags and all event-specific selection semantics are not established.

evidence.note: Resolves the keyed rule and draws a one-to-three-entry group size, independently draws IDs and quantities from weighted choices, uses ID 16 quantity 1 as fallback, caps total quantity and permutes the ID/quantity pairs. The owner combines monster-data at +0x2F8, member rules at +0x304 and this six-entry group table at +0x124; the monster-data loader names mon_data.gp2.
evidence.uncertainty: IDs and quantities are consistent with monster-group generation in the shared owner, but individual packed rule flags and all event-specific selection semantics are not established.

evidence.note: Opcode 105 clears the context selection flag, checks the requested context ID, and compares context major*100+minor against inclusive parameter bounds. A match enables choice building and clears the owner choice count; nonzero matching bounds also consume the context enabled flag.

Resolves the indexed actor, queues data/prm/level%d.bin and data/prm/spelltable.bin, waits for both, and passes their data to the actor-level application routine. Applies optional actor-field preservation/update flags, removes both loads and marks task complete.

Uses the active grotto detailed-data message ID and a field monster to stage party placement, camera adjustment and fade transitions, then loads bstr%d_<LG>.nat from data/bin/bstr.gp2 and displays the indexed message. Advances through six states and frees its temporary allocator.
evidence.uncertainty: The grotto/monster scene and message-resource sequence are proven; the exact gameplay trigger is not recovered, so no victory or introduction event is asserted.

evidence.note: Dispatches one of six name-formatting handlers, scans [defm], [deff], [defn], [defplr] and [indef*] tokens through the original article table, applies bracket-name substitutions and appends the result while advancing the caller output pointer. Firmware language three supplies a default article variant.
Validates member index and resource, copies a 0x800-byte template, draws the centered name and class/level or status text, then uploads to sub OBJ VRAM at (member+1)*0x800.
Rejects dimensions smaller than eight pixels, configures geometry matrices for the inset rectangle, and renders eight 0x88-byte border parts with per-part transforms and the linked frame color.
Converts a signed pixel rectangle to tile coordinates, chooses eight border tile IDs from a style table, writes corners and repeated edges on a 32-column tilemap, and fills the interior with tile 1.

Renders the background path into a temporary 0x4800-byte canvas, stages tile rows and styled border tilemaps, updates scroll registers, and releases staging memory. Also transfers active glyph entries and dispatches enabled clipping-window callbacks.
Computes the continue marker from canvas tile geometry: x is half the pixel width plus tile-origin X, and y is pixel height minus ten. Its caller draws the bottom-center prompt there.
Clears the old prompt area and draws a four-row downward triangle during the visible blink half. Supports the temporary tiled canvas, an attached window, or direct geometry rendering.
Parses leading viewport/display tags, converts escaped and literal newlines to FF18, stores clamped TIME values in the four-slot queue and emits FF1A, then terminates the output with FF01.

Releases prior glyph references, clears parser/glyph buffers, expands text through the markup pipeline, configures the default dialogue viewport and render mode, initializes frame/control state and enters token-consuming state 5.

Reserves a glyph-buffer allocation bit, finds a free entry among 128, rasterizes a 16x16 4bpp glyph with configured shadow/outline flags, initializes its render record/texture location and marks the entry in use.
Parses markup into a temporary byte stream, preserves FF control codes and operands, acquires or references cached font glyphs, emits FF19 for unmatched bytes, and returns the halfword count.
Walks cached glyph indices through FF01 termination, handles FF18 line breaks and FF19 spacing, applies pair kerning, and draws textured quads or canvas glyphs according to the render argument.
Replaces each consumed halfword with FF01, decrements references for valid cached glyphs, and resets entries whose references reach zero.
Looks up each encoded font key, applies pair kerning, blits its monochrome glyph into canvas regions, advances by glyph width plus one, and returns total horizontal advance.
Copies an 8 by 8 packed 4bpp tile into matching tiled canvas rectangles, preserving destination pixels for zero source nibbles.
Visits each pixel of the requested rectangle, locates its canvas region, and writes the selected four-bit palette index into the corresponding tiled nibble.
Decodes OAM shape and size into pixel dimensions and emits twelve-byte canvas region records with relative coordinates and 32-byte tile offsets.
Draws the configured panel rectangle, waits for its visible state, renders the current page of cached text with selected-row coloring, then positions and updates the cursor resource.
Walks module-table triples of destination, initialized size and BSS size; copies words, clears the following BSS, synchronizes caches and branches to AutoloadCallback.
Uses CP15 to disable and invalidate caches, configure eight protection regions and TCM locations, set permissions/cacheability and enable processor features.
Empty function invoked by Entry after the runtime startup hook and immediately before Runtime_RunGlobalInitializers.
Formats a two-word integer backwards in octal, decimal or hexadecimal using 64-bit quotient/remainder; applies sign, alternate prefixes, precision and zero padding.
Handles a/A conversions, extracts the binary exponent and mantissa nibbles, writes a 0x/0X prefix and p/P exponent, and emits signed infinity/NaN strings.
Uses decimal digits and round-to-even to render e/E, f/F and g/G conversions, including decimal points, exponent text, signs and infinity/NaN cases.
Scans percent conversions, consumes variadic arguments, dispatches integer/double/string conversion, and sends text and width padding to the supplied output callback.
Character-reader state machine handles whitespace, sign, decimal and hexadecimal significands, exponents, INFINITY and NAN payloads; returns consumed length and range status.
Validates radix 2..36 or automatic radix, consumes whitespace/sign and base prefixes, accumulates digits with overflow checks, and unread-callbacks the terminating character.
Power kernel handles zero/one/infinity/NaN and negative-base integer parity, computes split logarithm/exponential polynomials, and rescales the result; Runtime_ComputeDoublePower forwards here.
Convolves both decimal digit arrays, propagates base-ten carries, combines exponents and rounds excess digits to even at the 32-digit limit.
Handles signed zero/infinity/NaN, accumulates ASCII decimal digits, scales by powers, compares adjacent representable doubles against decimal values and resolves ties by parity.
Single-precision counterpart of _dsqrt: normalizes exponent/mantissa, computes root bits and rounds, preserves signed zero and sets domain errno for invalid inputs.
Moves the character pointer to r1 and invokes ARM semihosting SWI 0x123456 with operation 3; console output calls it once per byte.
Invokes ARM semihosting SWI 0x123456 with operation 7 and null argument; console input repeats it until count or line ending.
Walks exception action opcodes, decodes operands, invokes scalar/array cleanup callbacks and pops stack frames until the requested action record is reached.
Standalone shared epilogue immediately after the cleanup interpreter releases its 0xa4-byte frame and restores r4-r11 and PC. It has no independent prologue.
evidence.uncertainty: This packet entry is an epilogue fragment of the preceding unwind interpreter, not evidence of a separately callable C function.

evidence.note: Unwinds to the selected action, populates the frame-local catch record with exception/context fields and transfers control to the descriptor-relative catch address.
Copies the throw context and descriptor, scans action opcodes and catch/type lists, invokes the selected handler path or exception callback, and returns the matching descriptor.
evidence.uncertainty: Exact original MSL internal symbol and exception-specification terminology are not recovered.

evidence.note: Given begin/end pointers, element size and destructor, steps backwards from end and destroys each successfully constructed element; called by the array-construction failure path.
Landing-pad fragment calls the runtime exception callback, destroys the local exception record, and restores the range-destruction frame.
evidence.uncertainty: Fragment ownership follows its position and identical saved-frame layout; no direct caller is present in the packet.

evidence.note: Calls an element constructor over count and stride; with a destructor available, the exception path destroys the constructed prefix backwards and rethrows through the saved context.
Landing-pad fragment following __cxa_vec_cleanup calls the exception callback, destroys the local exception record and restores the cleanup frame.
evidence.uncertainty: It is a cleanup landing pad rather than an independently called source-level function.

evidence.note: Allocates a throw context, saves r4-r11, SP and LR, clears initial exception fields and tail-branches to the exception-unwind dispatcher; used after array-construction rollback.
Initializes character and party records, transition descriptor, timing, placement variants, multiplayer identity/position buffers and flags; seeds both random generators from the timestamp.
When main byte 0x10 is set, translates four saved halfwords into BG0CNT..BG3CNT at 0x04000008..0x0400000e, including size, base blocks, priority, palette and mosaic fields.

Stops an existing stream, divides the buffer into aligned per-channel ring regions, allocates an alarm, submits PCM-channel and periodic-alarm setup, registers the stream and invokes the initial buffer callback with interrupts disabled. Matches the NitroSystem SDK setup routine.

Resolves bank INFO, loads or reuses its bank file under flag 2, visits four wave-archive IDs except 0xffff, loads bank-referenced waves under flag 4 and assigns wave archives to bank slots. Returns the SDK bank/wave error codes.

Reads the SWAR header and wave count, allocates header plus two wave-pointer tables, preserves file offsets in the second table and clears runtime pointers in the first. Optionally caches this index for loading waves individually.

Checks for an already resolved wave, derives its file range from the saved SWAR offsets and final file size, allocates and reads it, flushes the data cache and installs the wave address under the sound mutex. Matches private LoadSingleWave.

Returns zero for an unbound stream handle, otherwise multiplies the total sample count at 0xcc by 1000 and divides by the sample rate at 0xc4. Differs from current-position access by reading total length rather than playback cursor.

Updates all four active stream players: stops exhausted players, starts prepared streams on request, advances volume fades, combines archive/user/fader attenuation and stops after a stop fade completes. Matches NitroSystem's internal stream-main routine.

Fills each requested channel buffer using the stream read callback, handles PCM8/PCM16 and nibble ADPCM with predictor/index state and saturation, loops or ends streams and supplies silence or duplicated mono channels. Invokes the buffer callback, maintains sample position and cache coherence, and marks initial preparation complete.

Empty return-only body installed as the in-memory stream backend's completion hook, paired with direct header/range copies. It performs no asynchronous read completion work; the body does not establish a return value.
evidence.uncertainty: The source models this as void and the assembly is a bare return; do not infer a Boolean success result from its placement in the backend table.

evidence.note: Processes navigation, touch selection and scrollbar dragging; formats visible linked entries and editable numeric values; renders through tile text or the pixel text path; recursively updates an open submenu and advances open/close states.
evidence.uncertainty: The trailing assembly contains data-classified instruction bytes; the decoded body and recursive control flow establish the overall behavior without requiring names for every transition.

evidence.note: Writes successive signed character bytes as halfword tile entries into the shared screen buffer at row*32+column. Adds the four-bit palette bank in bits 12-15 and stops at a null byte or column 256.
evidence.uncertainty: Preserves the original signed-byte conversion; the body does not implement a multibyte glyph lookup.

evidence.note: Allocates the shared text context, TextCanvas and work buffers; loads both font archives, windata3.bncg and f8.mes; creates the display context; relocates the key/value table; and attaches all workspace pointers under the loader lock.

Checks descriptor override flags and the first matched glyph vowel flag, with special h and y handling using subsequent glyphs and TextLookup_TestRecordOrTokenBitFlag. Callers are the IF_VOWEL_FR_HERO/ADDRESSEE/LEADER/item/monster/actor/target condition family.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact linguistic names of descriptor bits 28 and 30 are not established; the name records the proven French vowel-condition role.

evidence.note: Rejects duplicate canvas IDs and a full stack, copies configured geometry and flags into the next canvas, renders text, appends after matching resource character data, increments stack depth, and refreshes selection geometry.
Returns minus one when touch is unavailable, zero when there is no canvas or valid coordinate pair, one inside the selected canvas pixel bounds, and two outside.

Finds source and destination resource layers from descriptor nibbles, selects ready unsuppressed canvases on the source, fills their rectangles on the destination tilemap, and adds corner tiles according to edge tests.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact visual purpose of the alternate-layer corner fill is not established.

evidence.note: Requires loaded scene 0x11 and a current resource state other than 0x2a or 0x2d; when its argument is zero it enables OBJ display and configures BG1/BG0 alpha coefficients 10 and 6.
evidence.uncertainty: Scene and linked state names remain numeric because their gameplay meanings are not proved.

evidence.note: Fetches a cached glyph bitmap and draws it relative to the canvas tile origin; style flags select four outline offsets plus a shifted fill, a shadow plus fill, or a plain glyph.

Ticks speaker waits, fading, timed delays and input waits before advancing the decoded token cursor. Dispatches FF control codes for pages, choices, speaker turning, markers, sound and background-loader actions, retaining resumable stream state.

When retained-prefix flags are set, temporarily uses the alternate display rectangle, scans retained cached glyph indices, handles spaces and terminators, and draws the prefix through canvas or positioned-glyph paths before restoring the rectangle.
evidence.uncertainty: Delimiter spelling and user-visible purpose of the retained prefix are not proved from the pointer literals alone.

evidence.note: Draws the active stream and retained prefix, applies line alignment, kerning and alpha, and selects canvas, positioned-entry, external text renderer, or staged 4bpp texture drawing; the texture path finishes with a hardware quad.

Requires the marker lifetime flag and a valid speaker actor, projects the actor world position into screen coordinates, offsets by 62 and 12 pixels, selects the marker resource from a two-entry table, and draws it.
evidence.uncertainty: The visual meanings of the two marker variants are not proved.

evidence.note: Converts source bytes into cached glyph indices and FF control tokens, copies control operands, tracks glyph references and retained prefix indices, handles space as FF19, and advances source and decoded cursors.

Finds a delimited prefix in the source, measures glyph count and width, aligns the prefix rectangle, compares its text with the retained copy, and either releases old references or restores stream cursors past the reusable prefix.
evidence.uncertainty: Literal delimiter spellings are not resolved; reuse, width measurement and reference release are explicit.

evidence.note: Measures each formatted line and sets its horizontal origin to the configured center minus half the line width, with zero vertical offsets; scans variable-length glyphs and skips control operands.
The entire listed body is a single pop of r3-r11 and pc. It performs an epilogue return and contains no independent text operation.
evidence.uncertainty: Likely a split or shared epilogue associated with preceding text-layout code. No standalone semantic operation or caller is present in the supplied listing.

evidence.note: Computes selector position from display origin and extent minus selector geometry, clamps negative coordinates to zero, and stores the aligned coordinates; called while initializing the two text selectors.
evidence.uncertainty: Exact selector anchoring semantics are inferred from arithmetic and its initialization caller.

evidence.note: Copies encoded text and control operands, measures glyph widths plus kerning, tracks spaces and hyphens as wrap points, inserts a newline when the pixel limit is exceeded, preserves PAGE and markup tags, and optionally increments the stream token budget.

Resolves one of six actions from the combatant descriptor, applies per-slot reuse masks, checks legacy boss level-up restrictions and action resource requirements, invokes the combat action target validator, and updates the used-slot mask on success.

Uses the chosen six-byte probability row and a 1..256 draw to select an initial action slot, then searches lower and higher slots with the action validator. If none works it returns action two and constructs its fallback targets.

Normalizes the combatant cursor modulo three, rotates through three adjacent action-slot pairs, randomizes the order within each pair, and validates both members before falling back to action two and targets.

Alternates between slot zero and slots one through five using a persistent parity cursor, starts each group at a random slot and cycles over all its members, then uses the shared fallback if all fail.

Iterates current party members, counts eligible mapped effects and restores two capped member counters on independent 40-tick timers; coordinates ownership through request key 1 and may dispatch zone event category 25.
evidence.uncertainty: The counters appear to be HP and MP, but their gameplay labels are not required for this name.

evidence.note: Requires the render-state dirty bit and fill header; emits OAM for the listed frame regions and tiles the inset interior with fill sprites, using screen-specific buffers and VRAM alignment.
Blits 8-pixel font graphics 1/6 along top/bottom, 3/4 along left/right, then four corner graphics at the window bounds.

Reads the clip matrix, builds a billboard transform with optional axis scale extraction and zure-node translation adjustment, then submits 0x48 bytes to geometry FIFO address 0x04000400; sets render-object flag 0x40.
evidence.uncertainty: Exact billboard mode conventions and the one-shot orientation adjustment are inferred from the matrix operations.

evidence.note: Clears discovery entries and expiry timers, packet buffers and peer maps; initializes member masks and pending packet type, and converts OS owner name into advertisement text.
Per-frame dispatcher preserves transient peer flags on snapshot failure, drives manager phases, reconciles host/client member maps, expires discovery entries and handles connection errors.
Skips failed snapshots, writes local packet type, packet counter and transport field, consumes a pending packet-type override and packs three member-map values into header halfword +2.
evidence.uncertainty: The meaning of the transport-derived two-bit field and signed manager counter at +8 remains unresolved.

evidence.note: Callback registered by the parent peer-event handler for aligned-buffer multiplayer start; handles event 10, negotiates mode 13 and a 0x74-byte all-member request, reports errors and forwards ready callbacks.
evidence.uncertainty: Parts of the body are encoded as dcb ARM instructions; parent ownership is established by the registration site.

evidence.note: Stores the discovery callback and optional channel, enables scan phase 2, configures a supplied six-byte BSSID or broadcast filter, then starts the extended scan.

Validates available channels, advances a rotating single-channel mask unless a fixed channel is requested, configures a 1KB extended-scan buffer, dwell time and wildcard SSID, and submits the scan callback.

Checks scan errors and cancellation, invalidates the scan buffer, filters descriptors by game-info identifier and flags, copies a compatible descriptor for callback delivery, then continues scanning or submits end-scan.
Registered by the client connection event handler after association; checks callback errors, handles multiplayer event 10, configures mode-13 transfer requests and forwards the ready callback.
evidence.uncertainty: Errors 15, 9 and 13 are tolerated; mode-specific branches differ from the parent callback.

evidence.note: Empty return-only routine. The backup write path passes its address as the completion callback to the chunked card-transfer dispatcher; it intentionally performs no completion work.

Copies from the optional RAM save image (folding the second bank at 0x8000), otherwise acquires the saved card owner and dispatches backup read command 6. The final argument selects whether completion/unlock is deferred.

Copies into the optional RAM save image, otherwise dispatches backup command 7 or 8 according to backup type with write/verify direction 2. Mirrors the read wrapper locking and optional deferred completion.

Reconstructs character records and active party indices from the saved payload, reinitializes the grouped inventory and copies its IDs, quantities and metadata, then restores zone placement, audio settings and auxiliary state. Returns the saved transfer byte through an output pointer.

Copies 0x1b30 saved bytes into the global Zone3D record at +0x840 and separately restores runtime scalar fields from the saved tail, masking the saved halfword to a byte and normalizing the saved boolean.
evidence.uncertainty: The individual tail fields are not semantically identified; the owning zone record and restore direction are clear.

evidence.note: Builds the checksummed save header, serializes party and eight-group inventory data, flags, zone state, statistics, treasure maps and optional resume data, then writes the payload CRC. The staged writer redirects these writes into its RAM save image before committing it.

Uses context byte 0 to stage an asynchronous backup read, serialize through the RAM image pointer, and asynchronously write the selected bank and optionally the mirror. Waits between transfers, finishes locks, and advances to terminal state 4.

Reads the selected bank header and 0x6f60-byte payload, checks the named format and CRC, and either returns validation status or restores game state. Restoration additionally refreshes day timer, lighting and saved auxiliary records.

Clears a 0x8000-byte image buffer, reads the card prefix, checked header, auxiliary record and selected payload into their bank-relative positions, validates the payload CRC, then restores party, flags and saved state. Unlike the other loader it preserves the assembled bank image.

Calls the bank loader in validation-only mode, extracts up to four 0x34-byte party summaries with converted names and appearance fields into the saved-summary buffer, includes zone/progress flags, exports four statistic bytes, and validates the auxiliary record.

Uses context byte 1 to read one bank asynchronously, validate header and both payload CRCs, and write its 0x6fe4-byte body to the opposite bank. When copying the alternate bank back, clears the primary header alternate flag and recomputes its CRC.

For IDs 1..308, replaces the corresponding four-byte record at GameState+0x75f0. Counts transitions from zero to nonzero low-ten-bit values, then adds that count to the saturating discovery statistic through the shared 176-byte statistics record.
evidence.uncertainty: Monster ownership follows the matching record table consumed by the defeated-monster screen; the complete packed-record bit layout is unresolved.

evidence.note: Adds to the minute byte, carries whole groups of 60 into TimeRecord_AddHoursClampedTo9999, normalizes the remainder, and saturates at 9999:59:59 if the carry exceeds the hour limit.
Adds to the seconds byte, carries groups of 60 through the minute helper, and normalizes the remainder, with an explicit guard preserving the 9999:59:59 ceiling.

Serializes against transfer flag 4, stores source/destination/length, callback and command parameters, then dispatches the chunked transfer to the read context or executes synchronously and returns shared-status success.

Scans the inner 14 by 14 cells of a 16 by 16 floor map, excludes tile types 1 and 3, creates packed-position nodes, connects left/up walkable neighbours and builds adjacency lists. Event loaders invoke it for generated grotto floors.

Uses active floor entrance/exit cells and orientation to create opcode-68 transition regions, previous/next floor destinations, entrance/exit placement transforms and pending arrival position. Boss floors use a special single transition.
Allocates ZoneChestEntry and opcode-6a arrays from floor chest cells, randomizes chest ranks, samples LootDistribution, applies opened-chest flags, and builds extra resources for selected loot keys.

When graph tracking is enabled, resolves its zone graph and current node. Uses nearest-node search under flags 0x1200, otherwise selects a linked node closer than the current-node distance and stores its array index.
evidence.uncertainty: The linked-node loop retains the original current-node distance threshold rather than updating it after each candidate.

evidence.note: Selects follower trail logic for nonleaders, otherwise handles action queues and B-plus-direction shortcut dispatch before applying movement input and advancing ladder traversal. Also updates the special actor saved transform and pending fade-in.

Runs the actor ladder state machine at +0x26C: faces an endpoint, plays hasigo_in, interpolates into position, handles vertical button/touch climbing with hasigo_loop, plays hasigo_out, walks away or queues a field transition.

Resolves predecessor and leader, records predecessor XZ positions in a sixteen-slot ring, chooses chase speed from trail backlog, faces queued trail points and changes idle/moving state. During leader ladder use it fades or repositions followers.
Creates four 32-by-16 text canvas regions, draws encoded glyphs using font metrics and kerning, records width and tile index, and uploads 1024 bytes to sub OBJ VRAM.
Builds seven 16-color palettes from RGB presets and five intensity factors, flushes 224 bytes and uploads them to the configured main or sub OBJ palette offset.
Subtracts camera yaw from actor facing, chooses a four- or eight-direction animation table based on motion and rendering flags, applies horizontal mirroring and selects the named animation.

Allocates the sprite-resource directory and actor entries from linked definitions, loads CHR or compressed archives or sprite resources, applies keyed placements, and captures a special model into sprite frames.
Draws active actor representations with the marked-entry filter, then conditionally renders the shared ground-effect model at the actor position using configured color, scale and render identifier.
evidence.uncertainty: The shared model is drawn at the actor ground position; whether its visual is specifically a shadow or another ground marker is not proven.

evidence.note: Initializes a palette with transparent index zero, collects sorted masked opaque colors over a strided RGB555 image, then writes one palette index per pixel and flushes both outputs.

Renders the actor model from three configured views, captures the framebuffer through display-capture hardware, converts opaque RGB555 colors into a palette and copies indexed regions into named sprite animation frames.
Resolves the staged animation frame, applies position, camera-oriented rotation and scaled transforms, performs geometry visibility testing, then submits every image segment as a textured quad.
Configures texture format, dimensions, palette, polygon alpha and identifier, applies segment translation and scale, and emits textured quad vertices with horizontal and vertical flip handling.
Advances variant motion/effects, applies lighting, conditionally dispatches autonomous motion, and positions/advances the attached +10 model.
Resets existing content, loads image pieces/textures and palette, reads animation names and frame triples, then enables and selects a sequence.
Restores positive HP capped at base maxHP, or maxHP when currently zero; clears death flags preserving bit 4 and optionally notifies party revival.
Copies combat-stat HP/MP to linked vitals, derives optional counter from +24, copies status bits 1/2/4, then resets transient combat stats.
Compacts consecutive duplicate grid indices, removes leading reached waypoints and enables path flag 10 when a nontrivial route remains.
Builds grid control points, interpolates a cubic spline with distance-adjusted progress, updates position/yaw and animation speed, and resets state on arrival.
Checks activation and target validity, derives movement direction from target and grid vectors, plays sidestep, advances position, and schedules repeat delays.
Resolves the selected grid location, clears masks 0x21, sets mask 2, restores home X/Z to object position and applies stored home heading.
Copies an optional indexed source transform, applies manual camera input, refreshes tracked bones, derives camera endpoints and moves an attached object to the third bone.
Advances nine key indices across three groups of three scalar tracks when their times expire; recomputes slopes or clears completed slopes.
Uses explicit timed spawn records when present; otherwise allocates children with randomized positions and rotations, initializes cloned models, and catches up child updates.
Integrates track values by the game tick count, advances key segments, handles repeat and lifetime conditions, updates child effects and invokes child spawning.
Extracts RGB555 channels into independent slopes and advances the alpha slope with lifetime-scaled key times.
Initializes and shallow-clones the embedded Object3D, selects randomized lifetime, color/alpha/scale/angle tracks and animation playback flags.
Expires active effects by lifetime or stopped animation, integrates and clamps color/alpha, advances scale and angle tracks, applies wrapping offsets and advances embedded effects.
Accumulates true delta time, chooses eligible party-associated spawn locations with occupancy and distance checks, selects a weighted time-of-day entry and requests a field monster spawn.
evidence.uncertainty: Exact encounter scheduling policy and packed choice-field meanings are not fully recovered.

evidence.note: Builds per-piece OAM attributes from tile/shape and position arrays, optionally calculates scaled rotation matrices, and writes affine OAM parameters.
Parses cell pieces, allocates component arrays, uploads tiled image and palette data to main/sub OBJ VRAM, copies animation tables and selects the initial animation.
Uploads image rows in eight-row tile blocks to main or sub OBJ VRAM, choosing four or eight bytes per tile row according to color format.
Faces the stored destination, detects blocked headings, returns to state one on arrival, adjusts destination ground height and synchronizes completion for the host.
Faces the selected member, selects movement speed, checks heading obstruction and scaled contact radius, and returns to state one on contact or member mode changes.
Faces the stored retreat position, checks heading and party-member contact, and ends movement near the target or when the contact flag is set.
The complete body returns immediately without reading or modifying state; its address lies within the field-monster behavior handler sequence.
evidence.uncertainty: No callers are listed and the exact state-table slot is not established.

evidence.note: Updates an overhead sprite height with a temporary vertical displacement through timer 225, then chooses a reaction state from party statistics and configured behavior modes and synchronizes it.
evidence.uncertainty: The reaction state selection is clear; the gameplay meaning of the compared party statistics is not fully established.

evidence.note: Under the background-loader lock, loads data/prm/actdt_a.gp2, localizes actdt_a_<LG>.nat, copies and relocates definitions, then copies actdamage_a.nat.
Loads data/prm/actdt_b.gp2, localizes actdt_b_<LG>.nat into the secondary definition resource and loads actdamage_b.nat into the secondary damage resource.
Empty member callback is the third entry of the sub-background update table, following background loading and scrolling callbacks.
Dispatches by requested zone ID, changes object 201 visibility, scale and placement, restores party positions at type-10 features, updates BMDJ visibility and queues or removes associated effects.
evidence.uncertainty: Special zone and feature branches are clear; a specific vehicle or gameplay identity for s201 is not established.

evidence.note: Compares the current zone with saved zone/feature IDs and its saved mode byte; restores the visual actor at a type-10 feature or toggles zone-specific BMDJ instances and visibility.
Advances motion and input, computes sinusoidal height, wraps world coordinates in zone 10000, synchronizes party positions and handles button/touch interaction when the scene queue is empty.

Decodes eight D-pad directions or touch movement, gates movement on byte 154 and an empty scene queue, selects movement animation and camera-relative heading, and snaps headings to containing zone features.
For zone 10100 loads s203.chr, s204.chr and both shadow archives, registers objects 202 through 205, initializes linked positions and creates the associated effect arena.

Updates linked points and vertical motion phases, applies sinusoidal height, wraps actor and linked positions, synchronizes the party actor and dispatches button/touch interactions for three projected points.
Sets the actor and linked-point heights, decodes D-pad/touch movement, gates on byte 19C and turns toward camera-relative or touch heading with a bounded angular step.
Builds forward directions from headings, normalizes displacement to two saved trailing points, maintains their fixed spacing and updates each trailing heading using atan2.
Uses overlay 30 to allocate the resource object and arena, unloads it while overlay 17 initializes the scene, then reloads overlay 30 to free both allocations.

Remaps special actor indices, checks arena capacity, finds the keyed resource node and initializes a 216-byte slot via Object3D cloning or resource-track binding; sets allocated and enabled slot masks.
Plays the menu sound, initializes the shared scene resource node, selects tmap.stb and callback 02165DF4, and appends it to the scene queue.
Plays the menu sound, initializes the shared resource node with the supplied status argument, selects status.stb and its callback, and inserts the node immediately after the scene queue head.

Pauses for blocked scene kinds, counts down effective delta time, shifts three text slots on expiry, adds TIME=90/CLOSE markup, starts formatted text or display requests and clears ownership on completion.
Runs initialization, active-update and cleanup phases for overlay-three presentation: creates a 6000-byte arena, initializes its display object, polls it and restores field controls on completion.
Stores vertical separation at +74, limits its magnitude relative to radius with a fixed-point-one margin, then rebuilds the eye.
Stores radius at +78, enforces at least absolute height plus fixed-point one and a minimum radius of one, then rebuilds the eye.
Converts the eye-target difference to float, computes atan2 and Euclidean distance, stores fixed-point orbit values and rebuilds the eye.
Empty method referenced by mode zero in data_020e8f08; inactive interpolation requires no work.
Opcode 103 packs three nine-bit keys and category bits, filters by global ID/category context, allocates a copy of the string parameter and appends a twelve-byte record.
Resolves +21C actor, handles shoulder-button orbit/recentering, follows actor center with optional smoothing and plane blending, decays target offset and blends loading focus.
Empty handler called with mode two after the overlay sets camera input-block flag 0x10.
evidence.uncertainty: The handler or state operation is proven; detailed region payload semantics remain unproven.

evidence.note: For positive target-to-plane distance, clamps distance/blendRange to one, blends heading/height/radius and target offset, applies them and returns success.
Builds the parent-parameter block including channel, beacon timing, entry flag and payload limits; accepts modes 0/2/4 and submits command 7.
Reclaims local five-slot messages, fills them from the outbound queue with rolling sequence bytes, and copies enabled remote message types to the inbound queue.
Variadic command sender obtains a free 256-byte request, writes opcode and word arguments, cleans cache, sends ARM7 command 10, and recycles the request.
Builds a 16-byte MP parameter block with mask 0x1e03, frequency and Boolean options, then calls the common aligned-buffer MP startup routine.
Initializes the 0x820-byte four-packet sharing ring, validates port/participant mask and aggregate size, registers parent/child port callbacks, and primes parent sends.
Requires treasure-map discovery state 1, loads tms_sta_<LG>.bin from tms_sta.gp2, displays keyed messages with first-time flag 0x119e, plays sounds and handles fade/cleanup.

Reads IME and IE/IF, acknowledges the lowest enabled pending IRQ, indexes the DTCM handler table and returns through the thread-switch epilogue. Matches https://github.com/ntrtwl/NitroSDK/blob/main/libraries/os/src/os_irqHandler.c.

Wakes the IRQ waiter list, clears the reschedule flag, selects the first ready thread and saves/restores CPU and math-unit context. ProcessorContext.h confirms the fields; matches https://github.com/ntrtwl/NitroSDK/blob/main/libraries/os/src/os_irqHandler.c.

Disables interrupts, performs the ARM7 IPC boot handshake, clears shared boot state while preserving the exception vector, and jumps to the ARM9 header entry point. Matches https://github.com/ntrtwl/NitroSDK/blob/main/libraries/os/src/os_reset.c.

Stores the supplied word over a byte-sized destination range; OSi_DoBoot uses it to clear shared boot regions. The reset-local SDK routine is OSi_CpuClear32, distinct from the existing MIi_CpuClear32. See https://github.com/ntrtwl/NitroSDK/blob/main/libraries/os/src/os_reset.c.

Reads the ROM base and ARM9/ARM7 header descriptors, flushes caches, clips the ARM9 source below 0x8000, and reloads both processor images through ReadCartridgeRomRange. Matches https://github.com/ntrtwl/NitroSDK/blob/main/libraries/os/src/os_reset.c.

Unpacks an ABNK animation bank, allocates 24-byte runtime records through the owner at +0x3c, and allocates per-frame duration/content-index pairs. Copies playMode and sequence index and installs default playback fields.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact runtime playback class name is not recovered; sequence and frame roles follow NNS_G2dUnpackNAN types.

evidence.note: Evaluates the reduced-octant sine polynomial with 32-fraction-bit products. All five coefficient literals, the sqrt(1/2) endpoint and final multiplication by the input match https://github.com/ntrtwl/NitroSDK/blob/main/libraries/fx/src/fx_trig.c.

Implements odd symmetry, scales a fixed-point radian input by 4/pi, folds octants, selects the sine/cosine kernels and applies the sine sign. Matches https://github.com/ntrtwl/NitroSDK/blob/main/libraries/fx/src/fx_trig.c.

Implements even symmetry and the same radian octant reduction, reverses the kernel selection relative to sine and applies the cosine quadrant sign. Matches https://github.com/ntrtwl/NitroSDK/blob/main/libraries/fx/src/fx_trig.c.

Issues four three-word stores to the same FIFO register window while advancing only the source. Matrix command callers establish geometry use; exact instruction sequence matches https://github.com/ntrtwl/NitroSDK/blob/main/libraries/gx/src/gxasm.c.

Preserves r4-r8 and issues two eight-word stores to the same FIFO register window, consuming 64 source bytes. Used after matrix command 0x16; matches the non-TEG implementation in https://github.com/ntrtwl/NitroSDK/blob/main/libraries/gx/src/gxasm.c.

Disables the geometry FIFO interrupt, restores its saved condition and handler, clears the GX DMA busy flag and invokes the user completion callback. AdvanceChunkedDMAReadWithin472Bytes installs it on the final transfer; matches https://github.com/ntrtwl/NitroSDK/blob/main/libraries/mi/src/mi_dma_gxcommand.c.

Advances chest timer and lidAngle through quadratic opening and damped sine settling, finishing at 0x4800. The chest state machine calls it in opening states 2, 4 and 5; it plays opening sounds at frames 0 and 16.
Updates chest timer and lidAngle in closing state 7. The normal path closes from 0x4800 to 0x4000 with a bounce; the alternate path eases toward 0x647a and reports completion.

Indexes a 0x24-byte ZoneChestEntry, advances opening/wait/closing states, queues reward graphics, acquires a per-owner render part and draws loot at the projected chest position. Removes tasks and releases render parts when finished.

Allocates chest entries from LootableContainerManager, restores collected flags, connects type-5 features, gathers placement keys and builds state_2754_. Creates breakable-container entries and applies pending broken-container and type-2 masks.

Draws breakable containers and chest bodies/lids before ordinary BMDJ groups or nearby grotto tile models. Grotto environment selects visible grid extent and boundary models; ordinary zones refresh lighting-dependent rendering state.

Resolves a container render entry, selects its breaking state and animation sequences, initializes four radial fragment velocities and clears its timer. Selects the break sound from the pot/barrel container type.

Iterates container render entries, performs geometry visibility tests, applies the lighting manager diffuse color to all six parts and draws either the intact part or breaking animation and rotated fragments.

Resolves a BMDJ collision instance or grotto tile, rejects disabled ancestors and missing collision models, transforms query bounds into model coordinates and collects overlapping polygons. Records translation and rotation in the output collision context.

Counts BMDJ instances whose object entry has type 1, allocates an instance-pointer array and fills it for later collision queries. Main grotto floors instead use the implicit 257-entry grid/boundary index.

Forms swept bounds from position and displacement, collects candidate polygons for each collision instance, expands packed vertices and transforms the movement into local coordinates. Plane/candidate queries repeatedly adjust the output endpoint.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact contact/penetration policy of the final polygon resolver is not proven; the displacement and endpoint adjustment are explicit.

evidence.note: Classifies party member value ratio for palette selection, emits decimal digit sprites right-to-left and draws a scaled foreground bar with its background from the supplied value/maximum and layout arguments.
Binds map controller and allocator into the shared script context, retrieves a completed loader task, executes it using the map-resource table at 0x020ef510, then removes and invalidates the task.

Runs ordinary zone-map loading phases for map names, resource script, shipMPos.bin, obj_mm.pac, background .obg and per-entry graphics. Initializes sub-display VRAM/OAM, consumes each task and activates marker filters.

Loads menu/tmap_base.pac, the active grotto entrance image and obj_mm_tmap_f.pac. Initializes the entrance-map display, executes optional metadata, copies active treasure-map title/level and enables markers.

Loads obj_mm_tmap.pac and environment-specific tf graphics for grotto floors. Main floors generate exploration tilemaps and load zXX background resources; boss floors execute a zone-map script and load its entry graphics.

When a treasure list exists and multiplayer is inactive, advances a triangular alpha pulse, filters collected/inactive records and projects positions. Submits revealed treasure sprites with alpha blending in XZ or inverted XY projection.

Draws the grotto map overlay and reads current-floor exploration bits. Projects the two stair positions and displays them after their tiles are explored, with the second additionally visible under the treasure-reveal flag.

Tracks the selected position with horizontal/vertical dead bands, scrolls backgrounds and projects party/treasure markers around (124,92). Main grotto floors mark player-facing/current tiles explored and regenerate their tilemap.
Converts world XZ to an eight-unit grotto grid cell, sets the explored bit for the supplied floor zone and regenerates the exploration tilemap from current floor data.

Redraws backgrounds at configured positions when dirty and projects markers relative to fixed tile origins at 0x18/0x1c, without player-following background scroll. Projection mode 1 selects this path.
Keeps the horizontal map origin fixed while following selected-object Z vertically. Refreshes backgrounds on tile-row changes and draws markers with vertical anchor 92; projection mode 2 selects it.

Uses an asymmetric 30/55-pixel vertical tracking dead band, constrains origin and background edge alignment and draws scrolling backgrounds and markers. Applies marker-specific alpha blending; projection mode 3 selects it.

Tracks selected-object Y with a five-pixel dead band, draws backgrounds with its vertical tile offset and projects markers from X/inverted Y. Treasure/party helpers receive the side-view flag; projection mode 4 selects it.
Checks four present party objects, maps each value-ratio category to a two-bit cached color class, and uploads the changed two-byte color to the member sub-OBJ palette.
Transforms each cell of a 16 by 16 tile layout through a 47-entry lookup, masks unexplored cells using the zone-indexed saved bitset, and writes each result as a 2 by 2 background tile block.
Frees an existing array, allocates count times twelve bytes, and resets its insertion count. Its script appender supplies a zone key, tag and two rounded fixed-point coordinates.
evidence.uncertainty: The precise meaning of each marker tag is unresolved; the key and coordinate layout are proven by the script appender.

evidence.note: Projects queued world positions onto the screen, clamps their anchors, draws decimal digits from least significant to most significant with staggered scaling and fade, then draws the associated spring-scaled style part.

Projects each live motion entry through the current camera, clamps vertical screen coordinates, tests 8-by-14 proximity and tries alternating horizontal and vertical offsets before adjusting the selected entry.
Copies halfword tiles from a rectangular source, clips destination coordinates, uses 32-by-32 screen-block addressing, adds a tile attribute bias and cleans/invalidates the destination cache.
Finds a keyed 24-byte track, requires its playing flag and nonzero playback mode, accumulates elapsed time, subtracts the current frame duration and dispatches according to playback mode.
The entire entry is a pop of the parent animation routine saved registers and PC, immediately following its computed playback-mode dispatch; it performs no state update.
evidence.uncertainty: This appears to be a split computed-dispatch epilogue, not an independently callable function; preserve packet identity without claiming a standalone ABI.

evidence.note: Continuation of the preceding computed dispatch increments the frame index, clamps at the end and marks the keyed track stopped; embedded ARM words also contain the looping frame reset.
evidence.uncertainty: This appears to be a split continuation/jump-table region of AdvanceTrackTime, not a standalone ABI function.

evidence.note: Selects the engine OAM staging buffer, optionally writes an affine matrix, culls vertical offscreen positions, copies cell OAM with transform, and applies palette, priority and object-mode overrides.
Masks the input to two bits and replaces bits 10 and 11 of attribute two in every component OAM record.
Masks the input to four bits and replaces bits 12 through 15 of attribute two in every component OAM record.
Replaces bits 10 and 11 of attribute zero across the cell OAM records, selecting the DS object rendering mode.
Empty function registered as the global sound controller destructor by the neighboring static initialization sequence.
evidence.uncertainty: The original C++ destructor identity is not recovered.

evidence.note: Substitutes the firmware language tag, releases background-loader scratch allocations, reads GP2 metadata and decompresses the named inner file into shared scratch storage, returning its pointer and length.
Copies the by-value position arguments, raises Y by half the first supplied size argument, and calls Graphics_DrawColoredRotatedBox with the color, dimensions and angle.
Updates background shake and a cooldown, dispatches the active panel state or pending content reload, and submits animated indicator cells according to quest status and display flags.
