Advances a six-stage content load: reads localized quest messages and optional quest-order script, loads the selected quest message background, selects status-dependent text and counters, renders it, and clears the reload flag.

Advances opening substates: requests display context, snapshots sub-screen registers, fades out, allocates background/cell resources, loads localized oq2 and str_que assets, renders quest content, configures priorities and fades in before state one.

Rejects disabled entries, tests either inverse-yaw box bounds or a vertical cylinder, then updates entered/exited latch bits in entry flags. Callers use the result to select or activate nearby features.

Captures press origin/current coordinates, waits for release before rearming, suppresses edge presses and suspended sampling, updates held indication and invokes the direction calculation for an active drag.
evidence.uncertainty: The precise interpretation of input inhibit bytes is limited to their branch behavior.

evidence.note: Converts the touch displacement to Q12, normalizes it and the shared view vector, subtracts their atan2 headings, normalizes the angle and stores sin/zero/cos as the movement vector.
evidence.uncertainty: Camera-relative orientation is supported by the shared view vector and movement consumer; its owning camera class is unresolved.

evidence.note: Builds geometry from touch origin/current coordinates and drag length, uses the protagonist heading for a short active drag, submits a Z rotation and draws the arrow render parts with scaled shaft and tip.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact artistic role of each of the four arrow resources is not needed for the renderer name.

evidence.note: Copies the mon_list packed header, allocates and copies 32-byte entries and trailing text, resolves both text offsets per entry, marks ownership, sets the head and excludes duplicate/nonpositive display indices.
Binary-searches the 32-byte entry array by the signed monster identifier at +0xc. Bestiary_MarkListedMonstersAfterPrerequisiteOnce uses returned +0x1a as the display-index mapping.
ROM registers this callback as opcode 100 for data/bin/vrambank.bin. It matches the current configuration mode, reads bank masks, saves/disables selected mappings and applies the requested mappings.

Checks current/previous special-zone ranges, updates entry status and instance flags according to the mode tier, then resets an allocator and creates character resource/state contexts for eligible interior zones.
evidence.uncertainty: The special-zone gameplay category and tier meanings are not established; no invented location name is used.

evidence.note: For selected unfinished party members, applies configured X/Z translation and heading increments. On completion it clears the motion flag, marks the member done, aligns followers to the leader, queues position/state records and clears system mask 0x402.
evidence.uncertainty: Completion depends on signed member +0xac becoming zero; the field name itself is not established.

evidence.note: Wraps serialized monster override data, binary-searches encounter-group IDs, allocates/copies matching 64-byte records, then sorts the selected records by their leading unsigned monster ID.
evidence.uncertainty: Copies override records only; it does not copy the trailing payload. The caller collects unique monster IDs from six weighted encounter groups.

evidence.note: Queues data/menu/tmap_base.pac and localized tmuo animation data, waits for both tasks and brightness, initializes sprite/animation records, snapshots sub-object VRAM, stages backgrounds, removes the task and completes its two-phase load.
Walks the linked commands at result+0x30, dispatches halfword command kinds, prepares pending field transitions and queued scene work, then applies deferred position and loader updates.
Copies the packed file header, allocates count*132 record storage plus the header-encoded auxiliary payload, copies both regions and marks the table initialized. The loader supplies mon_btldata.nat.
Builds a view over serialized input, searches each requested signed-halfword ID, allocates and copies matching records, then sorts them by their low-15-bit ID.
Filters the first parameter against the optional allowed-ID array, initializes a 32-byte record, decodes optional halfwords and packed nibble/10-bit fields, then appends it.
Resolves the party member and equipment slot, gets the selected palette parameter, then applies a palette slice or three slices to the corresponding equipment model according to slot.

The zone-change caller passes Zone3D+0x23ec, matching ActiveGrottoClass. When the requested zone is a grotto and the current zone is outside both grotto and 30000..39999 ranges, clears overallMapData_ and exports persistent activeMapData using temporarily loaded language resources; updates the client map level and grotto flags. The reverse transition adjusts persistent entry state and clears the shared 512-byte range.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact meanings of the persistent grotto flag bytes, ActiveGrottoClass+0x260, and the 512-byte range are not established.

evidence.note: Called after zone and placement loading with the embedded ActiveGrottoClass. Detects entry from a non-grotto/non-30000..39999 zone. For parent/offline play, queues type-four events 0x5105 or 0x51c3 when the stored suffix is 6 or the environment is ruins, gated by progress bits and request status; marks the corresponding once-only bits. Otherwise conditionally queues a type-0x34 record; a pending flag also queues this record and is consumed.
evidence.uncertainty: The event text and the purpose of the type-0x34 record are unproven; the name describes queuing without inventing a quest or popup identity.

evidence.note: Updates the 0x3c-byte controller allocated by the scene caller and also embedded by the menu caller. Resets once when a client detects host disconnection, decrements and clamps the message countdown, displays any queued protagonist/member-formatted message, and advances the pending display request. Unless that request remains pending, invokes the member handler indexed by the mode byte and reports completion when the handler is null. Sibling handlers coordinate party placement and resource-reset choices.
evidence.uncertainty: The controller class name is unrecovered; GameState describes the established owner of the party-transition state rather than attributing this shared controller to grotto generation.

evidence.note: Finds source and destination background layers by their descriptor layer nibble. Fills rectangles of active visible source-layer canvases on the destination, adding uncovered corner tiles when needed.
Uses touch coordinates to hit-test entries in the current group, or follows the current entry directional links for button input. Writes the resulting selection and returns direction and edge flags.
Renders the group to obtain entry heights, sorts members by y, and redistributes vertical gaps inside group height with centered end margins before resetting the canvas.
Loads data/scenario/questorder3.bin under the background-loader lock and executes it into global order state using the current map and saved scenario time parameters.
Loads questorder3.bin with the opcode table whose command 102 allocates unconditional conditional-list nodes, clears the condition-list head and executes using the supplied allocator.
Requires allocator, code and size, resets the payload-request list and opcode result selector, then executes supplied bytecode with the request/order opcode table and caller mode byte.

Filters order-condition nodes by the supplied actor byte, unlock and multiplayer flags; evaluates predicates, activates an eligible status as one and returns its quest ID. Failed conditions reset statuses other than two and three.
evidence.uncertainty: Actor association is inferred from the placement descriptor supplied by the field-event caller; status names beyond their tested values remain provisional.

evidence.note: Walks all order conditions, checks unlock and multiplayer gates and optional saved-time thresholds, evaluates conditions for the current map, and sets eligible statuses to one.
Requires the selected identifier and inclusive major*1000+minor progress range to match, allocates a group, decodes condition/action parameter lists, and appends it by event kind.

Dispatches on the condition halfword, tests context arguments, progress flags, indexed states, party attributes and time, and recursively evaluates compound conditions. Group selection applies it to every condition node.

Dispatches action IDs beginning at 100, updates progress and game state, queues output actions and spatial regions, modifies party/time state, and recursively executes composite commands. The group action walker stops on failure.

Resets the trigger allocator and group/region lists, derives the trigger filename suffix from the zone record, loads data/scenario/trigger%s.bin under the background-loader lock, executes it with current progress, and refreshes request state.
Reads the name string at linked actor state+0x3c and compares the supplied bytes for its length. Alternate Shift-JIS trail-byte differences are accepted with +0x5e/+0x5f folding.
evidence.uncertainty: The comparison permits kana-like Shift-JIS folding; the exact actor name field ownership is inferred from its linked state.

evidence.note: Selects a node by key and current serial, allocates a 24-byte bounds node, converts four float parameters to 12-bit fixed point, stores its integer selector, and appends it to the node bounds list.
Finds the key/current-serial node, stores four float parameters scaled by 4096 at +0x24..+0x30, and sets the associated mode byte at +0x1f to 7.
evidence.uncertainty: The four fixed-point values and mode 7 are proven; the geometry represented by these descriptor fields is unresolved.

evidence.note: Finds the node by key and current serial, then stores the second integer parameter into its option byte at +0x0b.
evidence.uncertainty: The option byte meaning is unresolved; +0x0b identifies the particular motion option.

evidence.note: Updates the selected nibble’s low state bits while preserving its upper flags. When parent/offline and index >=174 it emits connection-value command 7 with the index and state.

Rejects negative IDs; scans the 0x23c records at +0xf80 for the signed six-bit slot ID, marks the match invalid and decrements +0x2c8c. It then shifts following records into the hole using the serialized-character copier and invalidates each vacated header.

Reserves a 0x800 scratch allocator, looks up character template ID input+7, initializes a serialized record and live scratch character, copies identity/equipment data, derives stats, loads spelltable.bin and marks learned spells. Appends the record with header flags (1,0), updates the bounded auxiliary counter and returns success.
evidence.uncertainty: The scripted template index meaning and auxiliary counter label remain unknown; no named NPC identity is inferred.

evidence.note: Scans every halfword key in every group, writes a group pointer for each match and returns the match count. GameObject_CollectBattleLinkedRecordsByKey forwards its target list and output array here.
evidence.uncertainty: The capacity comparison only exits the current group scan; it does not terminate outer traversal. Duplicate matching keys can emit a group more than once. The name does not promise a globally bounded collection.

evidence.note: Opcode 0x01 allocates and initializes a group, converts all arguments to halfword action keys and appends it to the shared group list, making it the current command destination. If key 1 appears, keys 2 and 0xDB are appended too.
evidence.uncertainty: The operational meanings of the extra action-key aliases are not established.

evidence.note: The complete body returns 1 without side effects. The ROM Script::OpcodeLookupEntry table at 0x02183B5C binds this callback to opcode 0x02.

Creates opcode 0x09 with a required integer selector and optional second halfword defaulting to zero. Remaining arguments are partitioned by type: integers become halfwords, floats become words scaled by 4096, and string-type entries are skipped.
evidence.uncertainty: The opcode purpose and optional argument meanings are unproven. The body does not initialize every optional payload field.

evidence.note: The complete body returns 1 without side effects. The ROM Script::OpcodeLookupEntry table at 0x02183B5C binds this callback to opcode 0x0D.
The complete body returns 1 without side effects. The ROM Script::OpcodeLookupEntry table at 0x02183B5C binds this callback to opcode 0x0F.

Opcode 0x10 initializes a group with the three action keys 1, 2 and 0xDB, appends it to the shared group chain and selects it for subsequent command enqueueing. This matches the aliases added by opcode 0x01.
evidence.uncertainty: The gameplay meaning of the default key set is unproven.

evidence.note: The complete body returns 1 without side effects. The ROM Script::OpcodeLookupEntry table at 0x02183B5C binds this callback to opcode 0x11.

Builds a shared opcode 0x15 command from an explicit integer/selector/string form, an integer index shifted by 100, or a fixed-point float followed by that index. Copies optional text and a short vector, supplies default options and supports two optional boolean flags.
evidence.uncertainty: The underlying presentation effect and meanings of the selector-minus-26 and index-plus-100 encodings are unproven. Invalid input forms return 0.

evidence.note: Script opcode 0x36 emits the same command opcode 0x15 as the overloaded builder. It reads an explicit integer, a selector minus 26, optional copied text and an optional byte defaulting to 1; it zeroes the vector and fixed scalar and sets the flag at +26 to 1.
evidence.uncertainty: The presentation effect is unproven. The name identifies emitted command 0x15 rather than assuming the script opcode 0x36 is also stored; the last flag at +27 is not initialized by this body.

evidence.note: Rejects a full eight-entry array and duplicate IDs, uses an ordered search to insert a sixteen-byte record, sets the corresponding saved progress nibble to state two, and increments count.
Converts maplist9.bin parameters into a packed sixteen-byte entry, including zone ID, flags and a seven-byte map short name. Rejects a null name and calls the capacity-bounded append routine.
Compares count with allocated capacity, increments count when space remains, and copies the packed zone ID, secondary ID, flags and seven-byte map short name into the next entry.
Gets model TEX0, selects a configured two-, four- or eight-color row for kinds 1, 2 or 4, copies that slice to the requested palette offset, flushes the palette cache range and stages palette upload.
evidence.uncertainty: The original loop repeats copying to the same palette destination while decrementing a length counter; do not infer advancement to each palette bank.

evidence.note: Reads the low twelve-bit count and record pointer, then binary-searches forty-four-byte records using their signed halfword key at +0x28. Returns null when absent. The event caller uses equipped-item keys to copy matching records into eight character slots.
Converts nine integer parameters into an eleven-bit skill ID, kind, point threshold, secondary key and packed attributes, then appends through the 287-entry skill-table routine.
Builds the same packed skill entry as the full-table handler, but skips entries whose attribute byte in bits 12..19 is zero and otherwise appends through the 116-entry bound.

Visits twenty-six groups of eleven skill entries, compares each threshold against the character indexed skill value at +0x464, sets previously clear learned-ID bits at +0x8ec and writes newly learned IDs to the output array.
The body is empty. Static-initializer relocation at 0x020e6414 references it as the destructor associated with the global controller initialized just before it.
evidence.uncertainty: The empty destructor performs no cleanup.

evidence.note: Resolves the active quest record and filter context, adds the filtered result count at +0x98 to the record progress halfword at +0x0a, and writes it only when the sum is below 65535.

Caller gates execution on zone 0x1644 and flag 0x384. Updates four actors at quarter-turn intervals using sine/cosine and randomized bounded angular speed; during the checked fade state restores saved positions/yaws when the BMDJ phase is zero.

Assembly parses printf flags, width/precision and integer length modifiers, formats strings/characters and base-8/10/16 integers, supports count output, and returns the logical length while terminating within capacity.
evidence.uncertainty: No exact SDK identity is proven; the two-byte lead-byte handling is explicit in the body.

evidence.note: Converts nineteen script parameters, including a copied name, packed flags and three packed triples, then appends a 36-byte entry to the bound five-entry NPC-attribute table.

Loads or accepts data/prm/level%d.bin and spelltable.bin, executes the level script, updates the selected vocation, its level and experience, copies growth stats/weights and applies eligible spell identifiers. Optionally recalculates stats, restores current HP/MP to new maxima and invokes multiplayer synchronization.
evidence.uncertainty: The final overlay synchronization callback is referenced by absolute address; its full transport behaviour is outside this routine.

evidence.note: Uses the linked character's current vocation and its level to select learning entries whose thresholds exceed the supplied previous level, sets their learned bits at 0x910, and emits spell IDs.
Scans the selected vocation learning list, emitting byte spell IDs whose required level is at most the supplied level; character-template creation installs these as learned spells.

Maps one of nine presentation presets to palette loader arguments, then applies Graphics_LoadPartyZonePaletteToSelectedBank to either the selected member or all four members when the index is negative.

Repeatedly finds queued character records, takes an empty active party slot, initializes its indexed state, spawns the field actor, transfers the queued record, assigns leader/follower relationships and name, and consumes the queue record.

Returns a bitmask for absent/invalid equipment, missing member, unsupported kind, protagonist-only use, weapon-category or vocation incompatibility, insufficient vocation rank, and sex restrictions. Kind zero or one uses mapped learned/vocation weapon categories.
evidence.uncertainty: The 0x4680 equipped-item exception bypasses one sex restriction; its named item is not established.

evidence.note: Initializes a pooled command and actor snapshot, then one target and descriptor-result node per supplied combatant; appends each supplied message key and advances the four pool cursors.
Loads current HP and MP from the combatant descriptor and forwards them with the caller value, auxiliary pointers and flags to the common result-population routine.
Collects eligible enemy-group indices and compares home-position X coordinates, returning the selected combatant index or -1.
evidence.uncertainty: The implementation treats a selected index <=0 as uninitialized; enemy indices normally start at 192.

evidence.note: Resets all combat record pools, clears a byte in each of three enemy-group records, then invalidates descriptor link indices 0x2a and 0x2c on collected combatants.

Recalculates six combat statistics, sorts randomized agility scores, builds player and AI commands, reorders them, executes effect calculations and follow-up records, and frees temporary command/actor/target pools.

Clears per-turn actor markers and packed descriptor flags, performs post-turn processing, sets outcome 2 when no eligible party remains or 1 when the enemy count is zero, and increments the turn counter.
evidence.uncertainty: Special encounter modes suppress the ordinary outcome value.

evidence.note: Walks one selected 24-byte enemy group, excludes absent and descriptor-0x2000 combatants, optionally rejects dead combatants, and returns bounded indices.

Resolves each group species in monster battle data, initializes its per-enemy stat records, assigns unused labels 1 through 17 with a species bitmask, totals species membership, and suppresses a singleton label.
Resolves each enemy-group definition and copies 24 bytes from definition offsets 0x6c..0x83 into each enemy stat record at 0x3e..0x55.
evidence.uncertainty: The copied block is a per-enemy attribute table; individual attribute meanings are not established.

evidence.note: Moves eligible party actions and three action categories to the front, moves another category to the end, and applies special-encounter command swaps and opening-turn substitutions.
Copies command IDs, indices, count/flag bytes, actor and target list heads, and seven payload halfwords; leaves padding and the final bytes outside the copied fields untouched.
Chooses action 0xdb or a random action from four side-dependent candidates; fewer than two living allies forces the candidate branch, with an optional fifth enemy candidate.
evidence.uncertainty: Specific gameplay names for the action IDs are not established.

evidence.note: Rejects scripted encounters and species 0x26..0x28, accepts favorable opening conditions or a threefold party agility advantage, otherwise rolls against party-derived and attempt-indexed chances and increments the attempt counter.
evidence.uncertainty: The party field contributing five percent to the chance is not independently identified.

evidence.note: Compacts the pending party slot stack, discarding every occurrence of the supplied byte while preserving other entries and replacing the count.
For each selected party member, locates the HUD slot, refreshes changed current HP and MP, and copies base maximum HP/MP; resets the display when a zero-HP slot becomes living.
When scene flags permit updates, resolves the received selection owner among twelve HUD slots and forwards received command, mode, index and tag data to the HUD selection updater.

Collects combatants, updates flagged motion activation, then for each living combatant clears its animation-mode nibble and applies descriptor flags and packed stages through the shared status-appearance routine.

Combines descriptor status flags and supplied bitsets/stages to choose animation mode and status resource key; disables a dead actor resource, adjusts idle suppression, and refreshes animation when required.
Sets the pending selection flag at 0x6e24 and stores the two bytes and halfword produced by GetTreasureMapTypeFromItemID; caller validates the request owner before invoking it.
When override-active bit 3 is set, compares saved parity with scene counter parity unless forced; restores Zone3D BMDJ flag-4 overrides and clears the active bit.
Empty return-only function called by the field party-removal path when the removed identifier matches the active party context.
evidence.uncertainty: The notification role comes from its caller; the function itself has no effects.

evidence.note: Checks enemy index range 192..199, resolves its monster object, and recognizes exactly species 0x1fd, 0x1fe and 0x308..0x30b.
evidence.uncertainty: The common gameplay meaning of these six monster IDs is unresolved.

evidence.note: For an assigned HUD slot, advances phase by 0.2 times a positive delta while selected flag 8 is set, caps the phase at pi, and resets phase when unselected.

Chooses ratio-based label palette, applies selected-slot coordinate offsets, refreshes cached priority-status text when flags change, and submits the label/icon sprites under mode-specific visibility rules.

In menu state 13, positions a status icon at the marked text rectangle for a flagged combatant, animates two colors with sine or thresholded alternation, uploads sub-OBJ palette entries and submits OAM.
Processes highlight/reset flags, advances and wraps a sine phase, calculates RGB555 highlight color, and uploads the last color of the slot sub-BG palette; reset restores white.

Updates window selection with temporary input gating, advances slot animations/highlights, synchronizes selected party records and multiplayer notifications, and releases pending background work when no active menu record remains.
Clears and renders the four party panels with current HP/MP numbers, proportional bars, labels and status icons, choosing compact or expanded layouts before flushing graphics buffers.
Clamps the requested bar length to its maximum, computes inverse fixed-point horizontal scale with a minimum drawable scale, sets position/palette/priority fields and submits the bar cell to OAM.
Finds the party display record, scans the ordered status masks at 02183460, handles the 0x80000 override, and submits the selected status cell at the supplied coordinates.
Advances each valid party record flash phase, uploads its animated color when flagged, then advances a sixteen-tick cycle used to select shared panel shake offsets.
Classifies current HP relative to maximum HP for each party display record and uploads one of four colors to palette entry 10 for that slot.
Counts transitions between consecutive enemy group keys, starting with a -1 sentinel; grouped target menu builders use this as their grid entry count.
Scans consecutive enemy group keys through the requested target position and returns its zero-based group index for the grouped target selection grid.
When the menu cursor flag is enabled, obtains the selected text canvas, derives its pixel position, advances sprite-animation track zero, places it beside the window, and submits its frames.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact visual shape of the animated cursor is not established.

evidence.note: Maps the four party members' vocation values through the thirteen-entry action table, deduplicates choices, appends the default action, selects the protagonist, and opens menu state 23.
evidence.uncertainty: The specific gameplay command represented by this vocation-dependent menu is not proven.

evidence.note: For the protagonist owner, groups party action IDs by frequency, selects a target from the unique largest group, or restores saved individual actions on a tie, then queues each party action with enemy group and object IDs.
Finds two active canvases, right-aligns both to a 32-tile screen, puts the second below the first, and moves it upward if the combined bottom exceeds 24 tiles.
Locates the currently selected party record, updates its command state, dispatches the associated command-window builder, configures scrolling where needed, and refreshes its menu labels.
For command states 14 and 25, compares the target-member selection with the grouped grid; updates the group cursor or selects the first member of the newly chosen group.
Reads the requested page change, advances the wrapped action-list grid, synchronizes its paired grid, and preserves separate selected indices for menu states 6 and 7.
Scans mapped party records for enabled, listed, unblocked, unexpanded records with unfinished commands, additionally requiring manual-control mode 5 when a party object exists.
Resets the current eligible party command when encountered; otherwise remembers completed enabled manual-control records and returns the last such party index for backward navigation.
Counts mapped records with party IDs 0..3, active-list membership, nonzero current HP, and an enabled display panel.
evidence.uncertainty: The count describes these observed eligibility conditions; no turn-order interpretation is assumed.

evidence.note: Sets pending-input bit 1 for one matching party or all valid panels; in the all-party path, zero-HP members are marked complete and their input/expansion bits are cleared.
Writes the active-list membership byte at +0x87 on all mapped party records for a negative selector, or the record matching a specific party index.
Runs the multi-phase UI transition: initializes panel layout, closes spacing, slides panels or seven allocated window segments into place, waits, then moves them offscreen with staggered delays.
evidence.uncertainty: Specific artwork and gameplay labels for the three transition flag variants are not established.

evidence.note: Refreshes the header screen strip, submits the sliding header cell using its animated X coordinate, and draws a count-dependent marker when the network session and menu flag permit it.
evidence.uncertainty: The precise labels represented by the two sprite cells are unproven.

evidence.note: Draws per-party command and target details using command completion, control mode, and status; resolves party-name or grouped enemy text sprites and copies the matching command tilemap region.
Repeatedly divides a nonnegative value by ten, submits the remainder digit cell, and moves the X position left by the supplied digit spacing until no quotient remains.
Reads the first primary or secondary linked record target ID, classifies it as party 0..3 or enemy 192..199, collects the requested same or opposing side, and widens halfword IDs into output words.
Requires a primary linked record, collects eligible party IDs followed by enabled enemy IDs with a combined limit of sixteen, and widens them to output words.
Walks secondary linked records, deduplicates target IDs, includes continuation targets only for types 6..8, and expands a party-range target into the eligible-party list before returning.
Selects firmware-language sprite suffixes, loads eleven or thirteen bt_combo%s.spr resources from the archive into render parts, and sets the initial three part flags.
Uses current and previous combo tiers, display and exit timers, and firmware language to animate and draw combo-number, line, and localized damage render parts with sliding positions and alpha fades.
Registers the active scene, initializes its embedded Zone3D and camera, resets the battle menu, five allocator handles, monster objects, tracking records, and asynchronous animation queue.
Restores a saved sound heap when active, resets the battle Zone3D, clears alternate action tables and display entries, releases optional scene resources, and destroys five owned allocators.
Updates battle zone, menu and effect animation, handles disconnected participants, dispatches the scene phase, restores timed game speed, and restores the sound heap when its countdown expires.
Requests scene phase 18 and queues overlay 24 through BackgroundLoader, retaining its task ID. Overlay 24 is the adjacent battle formula and AI overlay.
Requests scene phase 19, queues overlay 25 and stores the task ID, then sets secondary selection 4. The turn-processing caller uses it to begin action playback.
Resets scene command 0x26, configures a formation camera, and optionally offsets its orbit height and distance and starts orbit interpolation when the combat mode allows it.
evidence.uncertainty: The caller flag identifies the optional introductory framing variant; its gameplay label is unproven.

evidence.note: Adds the embedded menu-controller offset and calls the four-slot party command lookup. Battle entry uses the returned record to bind party control state.

Finds a loaded monster prototype, chooses or creates a monster group and unused instance suffix, reactivates a reusable monster or builds a new indexed object, initializes its stats, and updates group counts. Returns the combatant index or -1.
Checks the group suffix-use bitmask at +4, advancing the suffix byte and wrapping at 18 until an unused suffix is found. Monster construction stores that suffix for display-name generation.
The complete body is a single return instruction with no reads, writes or calls; no packet callers are recorded.
evidence.uncertainty: The intended hook contract and any unused parameters are unknown.

evidence.note: Finds the existing monster prototype by species ID, resets and rebinds the indexed monster while preserving group and name suffix, copies its definition record, assigns palette data and removes stale linked group objects.

Looks up replacement monster battle and model definitions, rewrites the monster group species and instance accounting, resets stats and name suffix, and preserves the existing object height and radius.

Clears encounter group and suffix records, selects species and counts from preset tables, creates or reuses indexed monsters, initializes statistics and display-name suffixes, and rebuilds packed group counts.
Waits for background tasks and the shared queue to drain, prepares VRAM, snapshots field state, loads party, monsters, battle zone and menu resources, then advances the scene phase.

Waits for participant and scene readiness flags, creates monster instances, activates party and monster formations, resets menu state, initializes battle UI summaries, and requests the active encounter phase.
Locks staged texture copying, remaps texture and sub-screen VRAM banks, snapshots the previous allocation state, initializes OAM and text palettes, and reserves battle image and palette space.

Saves party positions and headings and the previous camera, pauses or removes field monsters, sets battle rendering flags, creates scene allocators, binds party tracking records and the battle camera, and updates encounter statistics.
Initializes enabled party combat stats and buffs, makes them visible, builds party and monster home and grid formations, applies combatant transforms, and sets the scene draw-ready flag.

Loads actdef.nsarc/default.bact and party battle front/back packages from chara_mp.gp2 or special character files, parses .bact data, binds animation state, and selects stand before loading battle display resources.

Loads mon_btldata.nat and localized mon_data, expands species dependencies from battle actions, applies zone and legacy-boss overrides, trims species to allocator capacity, and loads each remaining monster prototype.

Copies a complete 24-byte roster group record, including species ID, eight member slots, packed counts and secondary member slots. The definition loader uses it to swap monster groups into priority order.
Formats the species .mon archive name, decompresses .cchr and .cmot members, parses optional .bact data, creates the model prototype, binds species resources and stores it in the prototype table.

Walks encounter groups, instantiates each monster from its loaded prototype, preserves the synchronized monster ordering when required, shuffles appearance order and assigns staggered appearance delays.

Validates IDs 192 through 199, finds the matching species prototype, initializes and clones the destination object, binds its stats and instance name, assigns its palette and registers the indexed combatant.
Destroys monster objects 192 through 199, clears the four prototype pointers, resets the monster allocator and snapshots the resulting texture and palette allocation bounds.
Loads btarc.nsarc, registers effect models and render parts, loads own and other targeting cursor sprites, initializes floating numbers and the effect object pool, and marks display resources ready.

Loads s019f.chr and s019b.chr, creates party object 1 with linked character and combat state, initializes it from the character resource record, enables the party member and marks it for later removal.
evidence.uncertainty: The character gameplay identity is not proven by the archive names alone.

evidence.note: Checks four species IDs from a fixed table against the supplied halfword list and appends only missing species, returning the expanded count. Called before final monster definition loading.
Collects eligible party IDs, spaces their home positions at 0x1800 intervals, sets home headings and gives the camera the resulting party formation width and height.
Selects a default grid table by party count, preserves existing grid indices in the persistent mode, converts cells to XZ coordinates and configures party destination positions and headings.
Maintains ordered monster slots, computes total radius-weighted formation width and maximum height, spaces monster home positions accordingly and supplies those bounds to the camera.
Collects monster combatants, chooses default cells by monster count unless an existing grid index is present, then writes cell IDs and destination positions and headings.
Collects up to twelve combatants, reads each battle grid cell, converts it to XZ coordinates and updates the combatant destination position.
Walks the queued party animation reload records and removes both nonnegative BackgroundLoader task handles for each member.
For each pending member, fences and queues two party animation archives, waits for completion, resets and loads the front and back packages, parses .bact state and removes the completed queue entry.
Compacts the pending six-byte animation-reload records while excluding the supplied member ID, decrementing the pending count when a match was present.
Starts a brightness fade, waits for completion, disables scene drawing, releases zone, menu, display and allocator resources, restores saved display layer bits and advances the teardown phase.

Waits for pending loads, commits party battle vitals, restores party field transforms and camera, removes monster slots and the temporary member, reloads field animations and VRAM, restores lighting and sound, and sets the field-restored flag.

Seeds battle randomness from the synchronized word pair, translates party command choices, invokes ProcessCombatTurn unless already processed, resets turn allocation state and queues the playback overlay.

Restores world-space eye and target when attached, clears shot state and automatic rates, disables parent transform, optionally resets roll, projection and rotation, clears orbit interpolation and stops camera movement tracks.
Chooses party or monster formation bounds, derives camera distance from width, height and projection, applies shot offsets or saved framing, sets eye and target and stores baseline vectors.
Uses the direction and midpoint of two combatants, or a single combatant heading, to build a parent transform. Randomizes orbit side and angle and starts a slow inward distance drift.
Resets the shot, follows a single selected object or measures a group extent and height, derives orbit distance and elevation, and enables automatic heading and distance drift.
Tracks one combatant, sizes the closeup from height and projection, avoids redundant reconfiguration, sets eye and target and inward drift, and clamps outlying combatant positions to scene bounds.
Averages supplied combatant home positions, raises the target, chooses a random orbit preset based on party or monster flags and starts automatic heading drift.
Averages eligible same-zone party positions, selects a party heading, configures a rotating overview and enables proximity alpha adjustment, then optionally points the orbit toward visible monsters.
evidence.uncertainty: The UI caller implies overview framing; its exact menu phase is not established.

evidence.note: Enables tracking of source and target IDs, initializes shared acceleration and random shot state, optionally chooses an immediate pair framing and stores a baseline eye elevation.

While action-pair tracking is active, follows an offset between source and target, selects side and distance by size and separation, smooths eye target, orbit and roll, and marks the shot settled after the initial delay.

Moves orbit heading by wrapped angle distance and interpolates height and distance toward the stored desired orbit using the configured fixed-point retention factor; clears interpolation near the target.

Outside group framing mode, clamps horizontal eye radius to 0x11000, smooths its baseline elevation, enforces action-tracking minimum height and an upper height bound, and recalculates the orbit after adjustment.
Measures eye distance against combatant radius and height, hides nearby nonparticipants and restores alpha with hysteresis while protecting the tracked combatant and action participants.

Returns false for a null action record; otherwise tests whether the action halfword is in the inclusive range 9 through 11. Both pair-shot routines use this to suppress the large-target heading variation.
evidence.uncertainty: The gameplay names of these three action codes are not proven.

evidence.note: Walks the active member-index list, revives members whose base status has the death bit, restores their MP, clears a motion flag and resets animation. Optionally notifies network peers and shifts the party recovery counter, dispatches transition mode 2, handles a progress-bit exception, and clears the pending recovery byte.

Selects three templates using random draws, initializes three serialized character records, randomizes appearance and unique localized names, copies vocation levels and equipment, and increments the stored companion count. It then loads spell and equipment tables plus all thirteen level scripts to fill learned spells, experience and derived stats.
evidence.uncertainty: Initialization of default recruitable companions is supported; the exact story event invoking generation is not established.

evidence.note: Script opcode reads a threshold and packed stat fields, increments the shared breakpoint ordinal and copies qualifying records into the start/end slots of the growth-script output. It marks success when the threshold-selection branch supplies an end record.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact meanings of the two request selectors are not fully recovered; the name does not assume they are both level numbers.

evidence.note: Writes the compact character record from runtime state: vocation arrays and bonuses, learned skill/spell bitsets, flags, encoded name, packed derived stats, appearance/configuration and category. This is the inverse data path of InitializeCharacterStateFromOptionalInput and is used by save and party-update callers.

Combines base growth stats, learned passive bonuses, current-vocation stat bonuses and eleven equipment payloads; clamps resulting stats to 0..999 and caps current HP/MP. With no preview argument it updates packed stats and attribute percentages; with a preview argument it substitutes a proposed equipment descriptor and writes comparison values without permanently replacing the slot.

Looks up the action definition, computes its MP cost with the party reduction ability, skips deduction for unlimited MP or waived costs, and substitutes a failure action if MP is insufficient. Updates party MP display and action-dependent motion state.
For a present target that is dead or excluded, chooses a group with eligible members when necessary, then randomly replaces the target with a living selectable member from that group.
Traverses packed monster groups, resolves IDs as slot+0xc0, filters object group byte 0x17c against the requested group, applies exclusion/death options, and fills a bounded halfword target list.
Collects eligible party IDs and selects one randomly for action target type 2, one other than the actor for type 8, or the actor itself otherwise. Returns a singleton target count.

Uses the party combat-tracking record and action target/side fields to resolve stored individual/group selections, handles special target-mode abilities, and resamples targets for descriptor-specified repeat counts.

Builds monster action targets from stored linked targets, action target modes and side fields. Honors a valid forced target, filters disabled targets, handles special collection modes, resamples repeat targets and falls back to automatic target selection.

Looks up an action definition and chooses self, weighted party, random monster, other monster, group or full-side targets from its targeting fields; applies descriptor-controlled random repeat counts.

Returns a present living selectable target unchanged. For eligible descriptor repeat modes, collects replacements on the appropriate side or monster group and randomly chooses one; otherwise preserves the original target.

For a nonparty monster not already recorded, resolves its original or transformed monster definition, accumulates definition reward fields, and merges a bounded species/group defeat record with counts and flags.
evidence.uncertainty: Reward fields at definition+8/+0xc are inferred as battle rewards; exact individual reward labels are not needed for this name.

evidence.note: Called by lethal health subtraction. Allocates a bounded 64-byte defeat snapshot containing victim and attacker status, action ID, turn, health ratio and party attributes, and updates persistent defeat statistics.
evidence.uncertainty: The snapshot also accepts reason flags and special lethal-event cases; their full enumeration is unproven.

evidence.note: For a valid party object, computes 0.02 times current charm minus base charm plus persistent charm minus 100, using the low ten bits of each packed attribute word. The monster action-interruption roll consumes this factor.
evidence.uncertainty: Charm field identity follows PrimaryCombatStats; the formula's design rationale is not established.

evidence.note: Rejects party actors and blocked monsters, scans living party members, scales each charm factor by monster byte 0x53, rolls for an interruption, then chooses an allowed interruption mode and records the responsible party ID at status+0x28.
evidence.uncertainty: The three interruption mode labels are unproven; their chance weights, eligibility gates and recorded source are explicit.

evidence.note: Requires action flag 0x800, chooses party/monster recovery odds for either of two recoverable conditions, rolls a percent, clears both condition fields on success and returns the corresponding feedback ID.

For party actors requires a positive weapon record of type 3 and missing MP, scales damage by weapon absorption and target absorption percentage with randomness, then caps the result by target MP. Monster actors use a definition flag and a ten-percent damage term.
evidence.uncertainty: Weapon type 3 is inferred as the MP-absorbing weapon class; no particular item or skill is assumed.

evidence.note: Revalidates or replaces the selected action, resolves four-member cooperative action participants, runs monster AI and charm interruption logic, emits status-recovery or blocked-action substitutions, and links source records into the output action.

Recounts eligible monster members and selectable party members, writes ongoing/victory/defeat outcome, then applies timed status recovery and duration decrements to each source record when the battle continues and the suppression argument is clear.

Scans combatants, clears transient state, expires MP/HP regeneration and two action-kind blocking effects using timers and probability tables, updates the special-action readiness countdown and batches recovery feedback.

At action start checks three blocking conditions in priority order, decrements the corresponding recovery counter and rolls the recovery table. Success clears that condition, replaces the action with recovery feedback and removes target records.

Adds the supplied recovery feedback ID to a result record, links it into source-result category 1, increments the result-pool counter and populates a current HP/MP snapshot with an optional split-word result flag.

Gets the party member's current vocation at character-data+0x950 and searches a sentinel-terminated vocation/action pair table. Cooperative-action validation substitutes this action when four eligible party members are unavailable.

Looks up the current vocation in a sentinel-terminated pair table returning 1 or 2 for the twelve vocations. The action calculator adds equipment/action bonuses to this value and multiplies it to roll special-action readiness.
evidence.uncertainty: Whether the small returned value is a literal percentage or a base chance unit depends on caller scaling.

evidence.note: For party indices obtains character data and reads the current vocation level from the vocation-indexed halfword table. For other combatants returns the monster level with the grotto boss override, narrowed to a signed byte.

Tests a selected result flag supplied as two separate word arguments. Uses low-word shift by index through 31 and high-word shift by index minus 31 above that, preserving the engine's split-word convention.

Applies party equipment/status HP recovery, party and monster MP regeneration, and periodic max-HP/16 damage clamped to 1..999. Updates HP/MP through shared helpers and batches resulting health, MP and damage records.

For a monster with a valid forced target, marks the reaction pending, allocates action/source/target/result records with IDs 0x399 and 0x212, links the forced target and optionally records the special event counter. Invalid targets clear the status.

Scans pending forced-target actions, clears the actor's pending marker, checks actor and linked target eligibility, cancels invalid forced-target status and copies valid action headers into the active action pool while advancing the consumed cursor.

Consumes the deferred action pool populated by Combat_AppendCombatantDescriptorRecords. Requires valid source/target records and an eligible source before copying each action header to the active pool. The producer stores MP adjustment feedback 0x243.
evidence.uncertainty: The producer records MP adjustments; the exact producing equipment/skill identities are not assumed.

evidence.note: Consumes the deferred pool populated by Combat_AppendDescriptorActionForCombatant, marks the action flag 4, filters absent/dead/excluded actors, copies valid action headers into the active pool and advances its cursor.

Deduplicates final target IDs, consumes a pending-hit marker, checks action/status eligibility and rolls a stage-dependent chance to raise tension. Emits stage feedback 0x31..0x34 and an additional action when the maximum stage is reached.
evidence.uncertainty: The pending marker's exact set of triggering damage types is not established.

evidence.note: For each source record, collects pending result lists other than MP category 1 into action 0x3ae, copies the source snapshot, clears transferred lists and handles the additional completion feedback indicated by byte 0x2d.
evidence.uncertainty: The individual non-MP list categories are not all identified; the category-1 exclusion and transfer/clear behavior are explicit.

evidence.note: Examines source-result category 2 and its damage/defeat/status flags plus category 4. Transfers qualifying pending lists into a new action 0x3ae, clearing transferred source lists and building target snapshots.
evidence.uncertainty: The full category-2/category-4 enum is unproven; the exact qualifying masks 2, 4, 0x10, 0x2000 and split flags 0x22/0x25 are preserved as evidence.

evidence.note: For source records with a nonempty category-1 list, allocates action 0x3b0, copies the source snapshot, clears its original category-1 head/count and index fields, then links a current combatant target snapshot.

Scans monster combatants carrying the forced-target condition. If the linked target is missing, dead or excluded, sets the recovery marker, clears forced-target state and appends action 0x3ab with feedback 0x164.

Builds grouped result actions for HP recovery, MP recovery or periodic damage, selecting single/multiple-target feedback IDs, recording resulting HP/MP and signed deltas, attaching descriptor messages for damage/defeat and linking targets into the action.

Rejects inactive, unassigned or zero-HP member records, resolves battle state, advances the special-command phase, flushes a pending panel refresh, and dispatches the top command-history state to its input handler.
For an enabled member without the direct-control bit, displays the priority status label or the linked member tactics label from string key 0x753E plus the tactics value.
evidence.uncertainty: The control-bit label follows caller use and the protagonist flag; every multiplayer ownership case is not proven.

evidence.note: Loads the actor name, vocation and current vocation level, resets command selections while preserving HP/MP fields, copies status flags and clears entry counts and the active-command flag.

Examines action category and target mode, initializes target selections, and returns the next enemy/party/group targeting state or completion state 100. Single-target cases automatically resolve when only one eligible target exists.

Reads the selected spell from the 66-entry table, checks adjusted MP cost, pushes either an error or targeting state, stores its action ID and formats its name. Called by the spell-list confirm handler.

Validates the chosen ability from the 147-entry table, compares adjusted MP cost or the special gold cost against available resources, records its ID and pushes its targeting state and formatted name.
Stores a nonnull ability definition at a valid index below 147 and updates the cached ability count by recounting the table.
Validates the selected item key and linked action definition, advances target selection with the single-member adjustment, then expands and wraps the item name into the command TextSprite.
Copies active party slot order, fills unused slots to make a four-slot mapping, copies the protagonist-party mapping with invalid sentinels and counts eligible listed members.

Initializes allocators, item tables, selection and canvas controllers, TextSprites and four member workspaces. Binds member workspaces to shared strings and selection state, records the protagonist and lays out member rows.
Resets the external menu allocator, restores saved sub-BG VRAM mapping and both background control configurations, then restores the sub-OBJ bank mapping. Called during menu owner cleanup.

Runs the staged BackgroundLoader state machine for battle strings, item records, sprites and tiled backgrounds; allocates seven text canvases, binds selection records and enables the sub-screen display when ready.
Finds the specified party member, rejects locked or invalid records, writes command state, action kind, item key and target fields, then resolves targeting and refreshes the displayed action label.
Returns the second word of the shared menu dispatch state. The main command confirmation handler copies this result into the global selection context used by subsequent panel operations.
evidence.uncertainty: The returned word's full semantic type is not established; it is retained as an opaque shared dispatch argument.

evidence.note: For a negative selector, refreshes every assigned mapped member label; otherwise refreshes the first record whose actor index matches the selector.

Refreshes an existing member or uploads vocation-icon and level-number tiles for a new member, binds its actor and protagonist flags, initializes command data, updates the shared member count and recomputes row positions.

Refreshes slot mappings, checks whether any assigned row is expanded, then writes each member's x/y position. Rows advance by 0x48 when expanded and 0x28 otherwise, with an initial offset when none is expanded.

Pops the shared canvas stack and resets controller history, finds the first assigned living enabled member without a command-blocking status, and anchors the root canvas at its row before requesting redisplay.

Dispatches list and choice states to their panel constructors. Other states prepare contextual messages and confirmation panels, including item/equipment mutation branches, then configure and push the appropriate text canvas.
Finds a canvas by ID, temporarily derives formatting mode from its flags, sets or clears its refresh flag, dispatches the panel-specific text rebuild, and restores the previous formatting mode.

Returns when panel formatting mode is inactive; otherwise dispatches the requested panel ID to its text rebuild without the canvas lookup or temporary mode override used by the existing-panel refresher.

Builds the root option list from four configured option IDs, initializes directional/touch selection, sets root canvas ID one, formats the options, pushes the canvas and updates the associated input state.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact localized labels are referenced through standard string IDs 22 through 25; their wording is not assumed.

evidence.note: Copies the configured four option IDs, emits optional frame and cursor tags, and appends their standard-string labels with separators in display order.
evidence.uncertainty: The specific option wording is not decoded; the root panel role follows its constructor and canvas ID.

evidence.note: Emits cursor/frame tags and the labels at 0x753A through 0x753C, adding key 0x7553 for an active multiplayer session whose protagonist index is zero.
evidence.uncertainty: The option labels are not decoded, so the name identifies their session-dependent presentation role.

evidence.note: Anchors canvas ID six to the member row, configures its selection grid, formats the current page of enabled category labels and pushes the canvas with paging when needed.
evidence.uncertainty: The twelve-bit category set is not assigned a specific gameplay category vocabulary without the localized strings.

evidence.note: Formats visible item keys from the controller list through its ZoneState2754 table, substitutes the empty-choice string when needed and prefixes the currently equipped primary item with the equipped marker.
Walks the ordered party list at +0x70, colors names using each command record HP ratio, and appends one of string keys 0x7551/0x7552 from the member flag at +0x134/+0x3c bit 30.
evidence.uncertainty: The option represented by bit 30 and the two localized labels is not established.

evidence.note: Resolves the highlighted action through the actor +0x9c array, wraps its action description, appends effective/current MP values including action 0x28 handling, and creates or replaces canvas 34.
evidence.uncertainty: Spell classification is inferred from the action list and MP checks.

evidence.note: Uses the bounded page range and actor cursor +0x20 to append the visible +0x9c action names with cursor/frame markup and separators.
evidence.uncertainty: The operation is proven; spell classification follows sibling MP-cost and selection routines.

evidence.note: Resolves actor cursor +0x1e in the 147-entry +0x1a4 action array, wraps the description with effective/current MP arguments, and creates or replaces canvas 35.
evidence.uncertainty: Skill classification is inferred from the list and associated equipment compatibility test.

evidence.note: Resolves actor item cursor +0x22 through the 16-entry item array, uses its positive item ID at +0x18 to obtain description text, wraps it, and creates or replaces canvas 36.
Configures canvas 18 beside the acting record, varies its height when three allies are listed, and populates selectable ally names with HP-ratio palettes.
Indexes the action-ID table by party state +0x950, resolves that action, appends MP arguments to wrapped description text, and creates or replaces canvas 22.
evidence.uncertainty: Vocation ownership follows the class-indexed table; the exact command label is unverified.

evidence.note: Looks up the action ID selected by owner cursor +0x1d6d, uses fallback string 32 if unresolved, wraps to width 152, and creates or replaces description canvas 24.
Groups enemy identities at +0x1d1c, resolves names through +0x1d3c, chooses the group containing the global target cursor, and formats each enemy group name and count.
Finds the selected actor command record, applies ID-to-relative-position tables to seven canvases, aligns paired canvases, and refreshes window selection geometry.

Switches on the acting record command-history top, derives list/grid sizes and remembered cursors for command, target, spell, skill and item selection, and configures both input grids; unsupported states disable input.
Reads the actor six-choice command cursor, reacts to confirm by pushing command states and preparing attack/action/item branches, and on cancel closes the actor window and returns -2.
Reads the actor enemy-target cursor, expands a touch-selected enemy group to a random member, commits the command history with state 100, or restores the previous menu on cancel.
Waits for a stable +0x20 cursor, hides description canvas 34 on confirm, validates the +0x9c action, remembers the selected action at party +0x960, and restores history on cancel.
evidence.uncertainty: Spell classification follows the 66-entry action list and MP-cost description routine.

evidence.note: Waits for a stable +0x1e cursor, tests the compatibility bitset before confirming, hides description canvas 35, resolves the +0x1a4 action, and remembers it at party +0x962.
evidence.uncertainty: Skill classification follows the 147-entry action array and equipment compatibility checks.

evidence.note: Skips missing or empty entries in the actor 16-entry +0x3f0 item array, hides description canvas 36 on confirm, records the positive item ID, and advances through the item action/target path.

Resolves the ally target through the actor target-index list, handles target-list changes by returning to the originating spell/skill/item handler, and checks target status before committing its index.
Confirms the actor vocation-indexed action using the class-to-action table, stores its low-12-bit action ID, hides description canvas 22, and invokes the action target-state resolver.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact player-facing vocation action, possibly coup de grace, is not established.

evidence.note: Tests confirm/cancel keys and outside-canvas touch, clears the actor transient flag, pops actor command history, reconfigures selection, and redraws the preceding menu.
Uses the owner command-history top to derive counts, page dimensions and saved cursor for global menus, then synchronizes touch and directional grids or disables unsupported states.
Closes all canvases when no command-ready party records remain; otherwise dispatches the owner history state to its input handler, processes selection changes, and refreshes the active window.
Reads the root selection, maps it through the four-entry root command table, and dispatches to actor-command, party options or other nested branches while pushing owner menu history.

After a five-tick confirm delay, counts eligible command records and inspects party options before dispatching one of four submenu choices to member, shared action or equipment paths; cancel restores the root selection.
evidence.uncertainty: The full localized labels of all four options are not decoded.

evidence.note: Writes the selected policy to linked party state +0x94c for the selected member or all eligible members, refreshes command records, returns through menu history and queues party-state synchronization.
evidence.uncertainty: The policy is inferred as tactics from its use in automatic-command display and party-wide selection.

evidence.note: Resolves the selected party index, computes and filters its available equipment category mask, enters an error message if empty, otherwise selects that member and opens category canvas/state 6.

Maps the highlighted category through the set-bit mask, collects equipped and inventory item IDs for that category, rebuilds localized item records under a loader lock, and opens equipment item canvas/state 7.

After stable selection and a five-tick delay, resolves the chosen equipment record, evaluates Equipment_GetPartyRestrictionMask for the selected member, and pushes result/message state 32; cancel restores category selection.
Resolves the selected party member and flips bit 30 in its +0x134/+0x3c flags, redraws the current option window, and queues party-state synchronization; cancel pops history.
evidence.uncertainty: The option name represented by bit 30 and strings 0x7551/0x7552 is not decoded.

evidence.note: Runs a three-phase load/format/wait state machine for str_ex2.gp2 and str_ex2_<LG>.nat, assembles enemy-status lines with enemy and party descriptors or a fallback message, then restores menu history after dismissal.

Reads the highlighted shared action ID; a zero choice clears actions across the party, while a resolved action copies its ID and appropriate inherited target indices into each party command record and opens group targeting if required.

Visits living party members, tests existing ailments or missing/nonpositive buff stages by requested mode, appends typed status records and secondary effects, then scores single or group candidates only when useful.

Computes target-specific effect chances with attribute and status multipliers, rejects redundant ailments and stat reductions, appends effect records, and submits candidates grouped by action target mode.

Resolves an actor or target result by mode/category/index, defers it while result sequences run, then selects damage/guard/escape animations, floating numbers, sound, camera shake, effect objects and party-panel HP/MP updates.
Accepts only party indices 0 through 3, searches four panels spaced 0x448 bytes by their combatant index and returns the matching panel; callers update its HP and MP.

Initializes playback, starts each command, updates both deferred result sequences and action resources, dispatches movement/load/playback/cleanup phases, and restores game speed when the command list ends.
During movement phase 2, excludes current command actors and targets and pushes other combatants with remaining sidestep cycles away from overlapping bystanders using their radii.
Clears saved action descriptors and selected motion categories for present combatants, resets shared display activity and clears the current playback command pointer.
Examines action-script commands and actor paths, frames the actor/target pair, optionally snaps combatants into place, starts queued grid paths and advances to movement-wait or action playback.

Resets the action allocator and transient effect fields, plans combatant movement, locates an actor-specific action script or queues the spell/skill/other archive, and starts playback or advances past an empty action.
Chooses immediate playback or target-turn preparation, disables sidestep on command actors and turns eligible actors toward the first command target, with a deferred-turn option.
Waits for action resources and the camera, hides temporary objects, optionally starts the actor-to-target alpha trail and turns the target, then advances once target motion and the delay finish.
Waits for the archive task, extracts the numbered action script and prepares it for playback; falls back to the resident action table or timed generic presentation and removes the loader task.

Waits for deferred results, transient objects, motion/effect queues, temporary music and animation transitions; restores idle animation, clears presentation fields, resets camera/text and restores music.
Writes the phase byte consumed by the grouped deferred-result presentation state machine and used to gate action effects.
Returns the phase byte that gates immediate result dispatch and grouped effect playback.
Copies the five words and bypass byte unpacked by the saved-result dispatcher, excluding the queue-specific actor/target and timing fields.
Runs the five-entry result queue: stages combatants around a target, controls visibility, camera and movement commands, dispatches timed results and restores motion updates after the sequence.
Runs the target-result queue with per-target effect spawning, sound and camera changes, timed result dispatch, a final selected-target effect and restoration of combatant motion.
Selects combatants, restores their target positions and zero heading, sorts each horizontal axis and centers their radius-adjusted bounds, compressing gaps when the formation exceeds the fixed span.
Clears the coordinate key and two linkage words of the temporary sorting node before the formation routine attaches its combatant pointer.

Emits pending trail samples into a ten-entry ring with alpha 31, marks emission complete when exhausted and reduces each live sample alpha by two; the drawing routine consumes the same position/alpha pairs.
Requires a visible combatant with an eligible motion category, no motion flag 0x200 and no idle suppression; party-specific hidden/abnormal animation state further disables turning.

Restores motion fields, clears absent/inactive primary and fallback targets, selects a forthcoming command target where available and otherwise finds the nearest active combatant on the opposing side.
Collects present combatants, initializes planned cells and opponent cells, builds occupancy maps across commands, selects actor/target destinations and reserves clearance cells for earlier commands.

Builds paths toward planned cells while tracking other combatants at each step, removes redundant intermediate steps, copies the paths into motion components and configures sidestep/path flags plus shared actor-target motion state.
Recursively traverses neighbors with a delayed start and bounded depth, paints a supplied ownership value after clearance and avoids cells marked with occupied/sentinel bytes.
Converts a reference cell and each supplied candidate to planar coordinates and returns the candidate with the smallest fixed-point squared distance.

Builds clearance/distance maps around the opponent, preserves an already suitable position or chooses the nearest reachable candidate, reserves an adjacent cell and records the planned destination and primary target.
Examines neighbors at clearance depth minus one, marks them blocked and invalidates other combatants' reservations on those cells, marking their planning entries for relocation.
Uses primary motion target, then fallback motion target, then the first target index in the action command, preserving 255 when no target exists.
Marks supplied cells blocked and flags other combatants occupying or reserving them for relocation, excluding the two action participants and clearing affected reservations.
Clears the node-array pointer, node count and blocked-cell count of the path-search context before the node allocator initializes it.
Returns whether the head pointer is null; the pathfinder uses this to stop when its open list is exhausted.
Selects objects from an action descriptor, resets battle motion as needed and plays the requested animation; magic falls back to magic1 and magic_in, with associated lighting, sound and camera flags.

Uses animation configuration and frame bounds to compute an approach duration/delay, subtracts actor and target radii from travel distance, queues translation and facing commands and optionally turns the target.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact authored meaning of the two frame parameters is partly inferred from their use in timing arithmetic.
