evidence.uncertainty: The eventual external condition permitting retirement is not fully traced.

evidence.note: Writes the command halfword into embedded action-message controller +0x162. The message updater copies this default, initially 750, into remaining-time +0x160 when opening a message unless the message supplies an override.
Opcode 137 in the action command dispatch table returns one immediately, indicating command completion with no side effects.
Copies the three command words at +8 into the active battle scene vector +0x6FDC and marks its validity byte +0x6FE8.
evidence.uncertainty: The vector is an action-scene override; its exact coordinate interpretation is not proven.

evidence.note: Action setup binds level-zero allocator at +0x10 and saved texture VRAM allocation state at +0x20; push/pop and resource loaders consume these parallel tables.
Selects saved texture allocation state table +0x20 using allocator nesting level +0x30; callers restore and save texture VRAM bounds around model registration.
Stores -1 in controller +0x1C0 during battle reset; refresh processing resets the battle camera only when this field equals zero.
evidence.uncertainty: Other values and the original field type are not established.

evidence.note: Binds the action program and command chain, resets effects/messages/load state, resolves action metadata, schedules display loads, queues localized item-name data, and marks acting combatants.

Advances delayed action commands through the opcode table, consumes completed command nodes, refreshes presentation state, updates the twelve effect records, and emits attack impact effects when requested.
Consumes action refresh and result flags, dispatches action sound and opening messages once, restores actor placement, synchronizes MP results, and queues target-class presentation entries.
evidence.uncertainty: Several shared flag meanings and special result codes remain unresolved.

evidence.note: Walks primary action actor records, applies +0x24 to combatant runtime +0x0E and stats +6, and emits a positive floating value/effect/sound for negative linked +0x0C changes.
evidence.uncertainty: The paired HP updater and stats layout support MP; special redirected actor rules remain partially inferred.

evidence.note: Polls localized item-name loading, copies the selected name into message context, then either updates queued messages when ready or collects message keys and starts their resource load.
Uses flag 1 to enqueue the action opening message and selected target once, handles key 0xFA supplementary message timing, and optionally appends then clears the action extra message.
Returns the command block token at +0x57C so the matching-token command can release the action command block.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact script construct represented by the token is not proven.

evidence.note: Initializes the same four-slot display load request using two halfwords and type zero, preserving unique-key insertion through AddUniqueFourSlotRecord.
Collects selected combatants, restores saved action descriptors and runtime fields, clears alpha-restore requests after setting inherited alpha 31, and performs deferred target turns.
Clears the timed effect record fields and initializes effect/sound keys +0x20/+0x22 to -1; used on each of twelve slots and when completed records are retired.

Advances twelve scheduled records using effective delta time, dispatches effect templates and sound keys at their trigger times, queues result messages, waits for message owners, and retires completed records.
Builds timed presentation records for primary actor and target groups with linked result data, selects conditional effect/sound parameters, and appends each to the twelve-slot set.
Returns whether the twelve-record scheduler active count at +0x300 is zero; battle completion tests use it to wait for effects and result presentation.
Copies a nonnull item-name string to queue +0x16C or empties it for null; action setup and localized item-name loading supply this substitution text.
Writes a selected message duration in the parallel +0x80 array; opening message setup overrides this field, and display uses it instead of the default duration when nonzero.
Pops queued message keys, builds actor/target/action/item substitutions and numeric results, starts the shared text window, and expires active messages after their duration.
Null owners are immediately released; nonnull owners remain pending if they match the active message owner or any queued owner, allowing timed records to wait for their messages.
Takes a node from the free list at +0xE4, copies a 0x1C-byte task, and prepends it to active list +0xE0; callers supply object movement, position, and turn tasks.

Returns true when the outgoing network record queue is drained or command key 99 is absent from both the locked linked list and the five local packet slots. The command-selection loop and pending-party admission gate call this predicate.
evidence.uncertainty: The payload meaning of network command 99 is not established.

evidence.note: Obtains the shared TextContext buffer at +0x5C, clears all 0x960 bytes, formats the requested battle-string key into it, and returns that buffer. Used when assembling the encounter introduction.

Scans CameraChoices by enemy resource ID and copies the selected eye and look-target vectors to scene +0x77F4/+0x7800. Resource 0x115 has three seed-selected variants; special encounter species classification 2 enables the zero-ID preset.
Writes the supplied X, Y, and Z components into a three-word vector. Its sole caller uses it to copy the selected encounter camera eye position.

Large phase handler called by BattleScene_Update: loads skilltable.bin and spelltable.bin, builds party action menus, shows encounter text, waits for commands and multiplayer acknowledgements, resolves escape attempts, and switches into action playback. Shares scene phase +0xEAC, menu +0x3760, party selection +0x2A0, and effect staging state +0x7710 onward.

Validates a party index in 0..3 and scans four 0x448-byte entries beginning at menu-controller +0x958, comparing each entry index at +0x4C. Callers use the result for command queues, available action lists, and party entry/removal.

Collects up to eight enemy indices, computes a normalized XZ vector from each home position toward the camera depth, sets actor yaw and home heading, and optionally shuffles eligible actors and distributes their normalized animation times.

Builds a name descriptor for a party member issuing command type 6 and chooses battle message key 1, 2, or 3 from the escape result at scene +0x5950. Success also updates field tracking and hides the encounter monster; after message closure and a delay it leaves the phase or resets escape commands.

Starts when BattleMenu_CommitMatchingPartyVocationActions accepts four matching vocation commands. Loads eb0091.chr, ex3000.chr and s264_<LG>.chr, sequences screen fades and effects, fades party actors, then runs the tracked-bone party animation and restores presentation.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact player-facing name of this combined vocation action is not proven by the archive names.

evidence.note: Disables the member in the selection mask, clears synchronization/text records and pending join data, and reassigns the party owner when the departing index owned it. Optionally resets command selection and queues an ownership update when the active local party changes.

Normalizes the command-selection subphase, clears selected command bits/readiness slots, resets each active party entry and broadcasts its command summary. Restores saved scene and system flags while preserving the pending-load bit, then cancels menu background work.

Loads chara_mp.gp2, creates the mp0200sc camera-animation object and a bone-tracking camera, loads mp0200sp as staging object 207, and tracks eight placement bones. Loads selected members animation package 3 from their resource-specific CHR or s017s.chr, then restores brightness.

Resets the party command entry skill/spell lists, reconciles inventory-granted skills, maps learned skills and spells through their tables, classifies action definitions into menu lists, and populates carried/equipped item entries. Enables command input only for an active party member without the checked incapacitating statuses.

Tests bit 3 in the combatant state flags at nested +0x138/+0x14. CombatStatus_ClearRecoverableAilmentAt5C clears that exact bit and timer; action-list construction and escape eligibility reject combatants with it. The 5C qualifier follows the established unresolved ailment naming.
evidence.uncertainty: The specific gameplay ailment represented by timer 0x5C remains unproven.

evidence.note: Consumes pending party-join indices, enables the members, initializes their combat state and tracking buffers, rebuilds action lists, resets movement/rendering, and snapshots home transforms. Refreshes enemy facing and broadcasts selected-party and enemy masks when the local party owns the encounter.

Tests bit 13 of nested combat-state flags at +0x18, identical to Combat_IsCombatantExcludedFromSelection. Callers skip marked monsters when building encounter name/group displays and the multiplayer selectable-enemy mask.
evidence.uncertainty: The precise gameplay condition causing this exclusion flag is not established.

evidence.note: Aggregates escape-command state across local and network-owned party members, rejects incompatible escape decisions, filters incapacitated actors, calls Combat_RollEscapeSuccess, and returns a classified outcome. Records escape attempts and qualified successful escapes in saved statistics.

Groups enemy species, builds representative name descriptors and singular/plural arguments, counts selected party members, and chooses battle introduction keys 6..9. Adds encounter-mode text and AUTO/TIME/CLOSE markup, starts the text window, and configures its viewport.

Queries the field resources for a pending member-removal index, returns false for a negative result, otherwise dispatches the party removal/ownership repair routine and returns true. The command-selection state machine calls it while waiting on multiplayer synchronization.
evidence.uncertainty: The queue producer and exact external condition selecting the pending removal are not identified.

evidence.note: Runs during command-selection phase 7/subphase 4 with inactive special staging. Resolves each eligible party command to all, grouped, or individual enemy targets; projects enemy head positions, draws markers colored from the issuing members palette, and offsets overlapping markers with a sine animation for the selected command.

Reads signed bits 0..2 of currentStats+0x58, retains stages greater than -2, and applies weighted target-count selection. Uses the linked target from the preliminary collector when available, otherwise living party IDs.

Looks up the requested indexed actor, reads signed bits 15..17 of currentStats+0x58, and emits its ID only when the stage is below +2. The shared combat-stat layout identifies this as magical mending.

Finds the requested indexed actor and emits exactly that ID when the currentStats+0x14 mask 0x01000000 is clear. The callee body proves the flag location. The bit qualifier is retained because this exclusion flag has no proven gameplay name.

Requires an indexed actor and overlay control. For action category 12, resolves required species through the action lookup, checks their four-slot definitions, and checks existing or spare encounter groups. Emits the requested ID if the encounter count is below five, or eight for actor species 0x10a.

evidence.uncertainty: The category appears to add encounter members, but no specific summon action is asserted.

evidence.note: Collects living party IDs, retains actors with nonzero current MP at currentStats+2, and selects one retained ID randomly.
Filters living party candidates for a nonzero tension byte at currentStats+0x24, then selects one randomly. The same byte is consumed by the tension multiplier in the action-damage estimator.
Validates required species for action category 12 against the overlay four-slot table, then emits the requested actor if the encounter-header low-nibble count is below two.
evidence.uncertainty: The precise encounter count label and category-12 gameplay action remain unproven.

evidence.note: Collects living party actors, excludes those whose currentStats+0x14 mask 0x20 is set via TestDescriptorFlag20, and selects one survivor randomly.
evidence.uncertainty: The flag meaning is unresolved; the mask and random choice are proven.

evidence.note: Collects living party IDs, excludes currentStats+0x14 flag 0x100 using the reviewed callee body, and selects one survivor randomly.
evidence.uncertainty: The exclusion flag gameplay purpose is unproven.

evidence.note: The entire routine writes zero to the first word of its argument. The immediately following target-rule dispatcher treats that word as its combat context, establishing the likely object owner.
evidence.uncertainty: No relocation caller is present, so constructor or reset lifecycle is not proven.

evidence.note: Stores an action halfword and two metadata bytes in the first four bytes of a ranked-choice record. The ranked-list initializer calls it with action 0, source -1, and flags 0.
Initializes four records at stride 12 with an empty action identity and floating score -1.0. Called for the shared choice list and each category-specific four-entry ranking.
Multiplies the two input floats at +0x14/+0x18 by 1.25 and writes +0x1c/+0x20. The common dispatch context is constructed by the action-damage estimator and labels these as damage bounds.

Resets all ranked-choice lists; gathers enemy groups and available party actors, HP totals/ratios and physical-damage baselines; enumerates up to 128 usable action identities from character definitions and inventory; and initializes mode-dependent randomized scoring weights. Refreshes per-party-slot action availability once per turn.

Requires action availability flag bit 28 at definition+8. Computes adjusted MP cost for party actors and checks it against current actor MP, then rejects flag-one/two actions when the acting record has the corresponding blocking status flags.

Looks up the action damage table and computes average/lower magnitudes. For scaling category two, selects magical-might or magical-mending inputs from currentStats+0x10 and linearly interpolates between table thresholds; otherwise uses table midpoint/minimum. Clamps each result to 0..32767.
evidence.uncertainty: The second magnitude can be derived by subtracting a table variance term; it is consumed as the lower bound by healing/damage evaluators.

evidence.note: ProcessCombatTurn calls this for party actors before action expansion. When the existing action is default attack and tactics mode is below five, prepares turn state, tests usable support actions, estimates a single-target attack, and conditionally replaces the action ID and target metadata.

Enumerates prepared action identities, resolves definitions, rejects excluded or unusable actions, and stores current action/cost in shared evaluation state. Dispatches the eligible action category through the member-handler table to populate ranked choices; tactics mode four requires zero MP cost.

Aggregates typed 12-byte effect slots into capped enemy damage, party healing and support scores. Applies MP-cost and tactics weights, copies current action/target metadata into a scored choice, and inserts it into overall and category-specific four-entry rankings.

Builds and dispatches the action-specific damage-bound context, then applies tension, target-category bonuses, attribute wards, category-one/two reductions, packed damage modifiers and combo effects. Caps the adjusted bounds and returns their weighted interpolation along with both bounds.

Checks eligibility and applies a five-turn status at 0x78 with word 0x18 mask 0x200, then builds success or failure results. Action validation, MP-cost calculation and MP deduction all consult this same exemption flag. Emits the shared message once except for action 0x1FB.

Uses the monster combatant group index, resolves its MonsterBattleData entry, rejects an existing group marker or type 7, and sets group byte 0x16 after a 100-percent or 50-percent roll before building the target result.
evidence.uncertainty: The meaning of the group marker is unproven.

evidence.note: Reads tension stage at status 0x24, queues stage messages 0x31 through 0x33, sets ordinary tension to stage 3, and can enter super-high tension with message 0x34. Appends each transition and updates the result count.

Scans encounter groups through MonsterBattleData_FindEntryById and tests their word at +8; selects the descriptor success messages if any is nonzero, otherwise message 0x1F, then builds the target record.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact reward represented by the monster-table word is not established.

evidence.note: Raises defense, the modifier at packed status bits 21 through 23, and attack independently when permitted; refreshes their durations, recalculates defense and attack, and queues stage-specific messages in one result.
evidence.uncertainty: The bits-21 modifier is used as a damage reduction stage; its exact resistance category is unproven.

evidence.note: Collects eligible party members, sums current vocation levels, chooses one of four weight rows at totals 61, 121 and 201, rolls a four-way outcome, applies it to the battle scene, and builds a target result.
evidence.uncertainty: The scene mode gameplay identity is not proven.

evidence.note: Rolls among three weighted outcomes, scans monster-group records, marks group bytes 0x16 or 0x17 when the corresponding table types allow it, and chooses aggregate text from reward availability, markers and group multiplicity.
evidence.uncertainty: The two monster-group marker meanings remain unresolved.

evidence.note: Uses the descriptor restriction mode, side-dependent chance and target susceptibility at 0x4C, then calls CombatStatus_ApplyActionRestriction. Returns effect bits, adds optional mode-specific messages, and queues a tension-clear notification when required.

Uses the sign of descriptor +0x32 to choose ailment mode one or two, scales the side-specific chance by target susceptibility at 0x4D, applies the chosen ailment and returns the effect mask with a status message.

Checks eligibility and susceptibility at status 0x47, rolls the descriptor chance, applies CombatStatus_ApplyDamageRecoverableAilmentAt5D, sets effect bit 14 and queues application and tension-clear results. The offset qualifies the established ailment.

Rolls the descriptor chance against the target's Sleep susceptibility, applies the condition on success, and builds feedback/result-mask information. Flag 0x14:0x10, duration 0x5D/recovery 0x80. Combat_SelectPartyHalfwordForDescriptorMode (0x021E929C) selects actmsg_en.nat 0x41/0x92 (falls asleep/put to sleep),0x42/0x17E (deeper sleep) and 0x43 (already asleep). actdt_b_en.nat Snooze 0x35 and Kasnooze 0x36 dispatch effect8 to 0x021DBD84, which calls this field's setter. Clear handler 0x021DBF18 uses wake-up message 0x40; Combat_TryClearDamageRecoverableStatus clears Sleep on a successful damage-recovery roll.

Clamps the requested defense-stage adjustment to -2 through 2, rolls target susceptibility for decreases, refreshes the defense stage, recalculates defense, and returns effect bit 30 with the stage message.

Checks susceptibility at 0x4A and the existing ailment, rolls the descriptor chance, applies CombatStatus_ApplyDamageRecoverableAilmentAt5E, selects party-specific text and returns effect bit 23. The offset qualifies the established ailment.

Rolls the descriptor chance against the target's Confusion susceptibility, applies the condition on success, and builds feedback/result-mask information. Flag 0x14:0x20, duration 0x5E/recovery 0x81. Combat_SelectDamageRecoverableAilmentAt5EMessage emits actmsg_en.nat 0x81/0x82 (mind confused/becomes confused),0x83/0x84 (more confused),0x85 (already confused). actdt_b_en.nat Fuddle 0x33, Kafuddle 0x34 and Fuddle Dance 0x236 use effect21; Combat_TryApplyDamageRecoverableAilmentAt5E calls the same selector and setter. Damage recovery clears this state and emits 0x173 (pulls together).

Checks the recoverable ailment and susceptibility at 0x4E, handles action-specific target categories and chance overrides for 0x52 and 0x58, applies the status and returns effect bit 24. The offset qualifies the established ailment.

Rolls the descriptor chance against the target's Paralysis susceptibility, applies the condition on success, and builds feedback/result-mask information. Flag 0x14:8, duration 0x5C/recovery 0x7F. Combatant_GetPartyStateValue (0x021E9464), called by the application handler 0x021E3A34, selects actmsg_en.nat 0x1E explicitly saying paralysed; clearing handler 0x021E32F4 queues 0x1F9 explicitly saying no longer paralysed. Burning Breath 0x110 and coagulant 0x19D select effect24 in actdt_b_en.nat; its primary handler 0x021DDC80 calls the same setter. Unlike Sleep/Confusion, damage recovery does not clear Paralysis.

Clamps descriptor adjustment to -2 through 2, rolls susceptibility at status 0x52 for decreases, adjusts packed modifier bits 18 through 20, and queues messages 0xAB through 0xAF by direction and resulting stage. The offset qualifies the resistance modifier because its exact category is unproven.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact resistance category is unresolved; At58Bits18 qualifies the meaningful stage rather than a raw field operation.

evidence.note: Attempts the descriptor's signed spell-resistance stage change, applying its negative-change susceptibility roll and building stage-specific feedback. Signed 0x58 bits18-20, active flag 0x14:0x10000, duration 0x74/recovery 0x97. Combat_SelectResistanceStageChangeMessageAt58Bits18 and Combat_TryAdjustResistanceStageAt58Bits18 emit actmsg_en.nat IDs 0xAB-0xAF explicitly describing spell resistance; actdt_b_en.nat actions 0x38 Spell Checker and 0x39 Magic Barrier dispatch effect22 to 0x021DD968. Combat_UpdateTimedStatusRecovery clears this stage with message 0x1D3.
Clears the active monster reaction flag 0x1000 and sets its recovery marker, lowers ordinary or super-high tension by one stage, then queues the appropriate reaction and tension messages.
Clamps the descriptor delta, checks directional limits, refreshes magical-might duration, recalculates magical might, selects a message for direction and final stage, and returns effect bit 32.
Clamps the descriptor delta, checks agility-stage limits, refreshes the agility timer, recalculates agility, selects the agility-stage message and returns effect bit 31.

Rolls descriptor chance times susceptibility at 0x46, applies the established timed condition at 0x5F, writes its mode into status halfword 0x22 bits 6 through 8, and queues the matching message. The offset qualifies the condition with unresolved gameplay label.

Rolls the descriptor chance against the target's Dazzle susceptibility, applies the condition on success, and builds feedback/result-mask information. Flag 0x14:0x40, duration 0x5F/recovery 0x82, with source/appearance mode in 0x22 bits6-8. actdt_b_en.nat Dazzle 0x3B and Scandal Eyes 0xBF select effect19/handler 0x021DD534, with messages 0x25 (hallucinate) and 0xF5 (struck blind); Combat_UpdateTimedStatusRecovery clears this exact flag and emits actmsg_en.nat 0x1C7 explicitly saying no longer dazzled. Sand/ink/flash variants share this status and retain their mode.
Clamps the requested adjustment, checks and refreshes the magical-mending modifier, recalculates magical mending, selects its result message and returns effect bit 33.
Independently changes defense and agility by the clamped descriptor delta, recalculates both stats, appends both stage messages, builds effect bits 30 and 31, and queues one combined result.

Indexes a 23-entry member-function table by descriptor word 0x18 low five bits, remembers the current target work item in the context, and dispatches the secondary effect with source, target and applied amount.

For actions carrying flag 0x80000, reads the attacking party member special modifiers and uses a shared random roll to apply eligible target ailments, tension loss, lethal effects, or attack and defense reductions. Queues combined status messages and refresh notifications.

Reads stored damage at battle context 0x8E38, applies it from the actor to itself through the health-subtraction routine, and queues damage or defeat messages. Final-damage calculation stores one quarter of action 0xAF damage in this shared field.

Subtracts signed descriptor +0x32 from the shared carried-gold total for the protagonist or linked protagonist, otherwise from the corresponding per-combatant battle gold value. The action validator checks the same amounts before execution.

After a successful-hit gate and 50-percent roll, computes ten percent of monster data +0x0C or carried gold, capped at 100; credits or debits protagonist gold, records the amount and queues message 0x172.
evidence.uncertainty: Monster data +0x0C is interpreted as its gold value from the transfer context.

evidence.note: Checks CanRaiseTension, advances the ordinary stage or enters super-high tension at stage four, appends the appropriate effect bits and 0x31 through 0x34 message, and marks the action result.
Uses descriptor word 0x2C bits 14 through 17 to select an eleven-entry member-function table. The action resolver calls this after resolving all targets with the accumulated applied amount.

Aggregates positive damage from existing result nodes by combatant, excludes the current actor and unavailable targets, then applies one quarter of that damage back to the actor for targets with the retaliation status; a mapped modifier provides a probabilistic one-fifth alternative.
evidence.uncertainty: The named stance or equipment effect behind the retaliation status is unproven.

evidence.note: Computes (accumulated battle power + 5) times a random factor between 0.8 and 1, capped at 100, then applies target attribute susceptibility, damage statuses, category overrides and super-high-tension reduction. Used for subsequent hits of action 0x61.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact named action and accumulated-power counter are unproven.

evidence.note: Transforms base damage using tension, randomization, elemental affinity, attacker category bonuses, wards, target reduction stages, guarding and evasion, special target overrides, combo scaling and the action damage cap. Also stores recoil for action 0xAF.

Scans target work and result lists, counts party and monster outcomes, selects singular or plural success and failure messages, suppresses redundant per-target messages, and sets aggregate presentation flags and critical messages.

Checks action and target eligibility, swaps attacker and defender for reflection flags, and redirects targets for status modes four, five and nine using cached party or monster selections. Records the redirection reason and disables original-attacker tension when swapped.

Requires active fatal-damage protection and an action ID in the signed sentinel table containing 0x18 through 0x1B. Lethal-result callers then subtract current HP minus one and consume the protection.

Checks monster-group capacity, combined-party requirements, MP cost and discounts, ailment restrictions and gold availability. Preserves the original action and substitutes a failure action while clearing targets when requirements are unmet.

Initializes the action context, validates and substitutes the action, collects targets, consumes MP, resolves criticals and reflection, calculates damage and dispatches effect handlers for every target. Applies follow-up effects, finalizes messages, consumes tension and snapshots final HP/MP.
Multiplies both input damage estimates by 1.25 into the adjusted pair and returns success. The AI estimator initializes this pair and invokes it through modifier table kind 7.
Returns success without reading or writing state. The AI power-modifier dispatch table at 0x021FFDA4 references this exact callback at kind 14.
evidence.uncertainty: The ability associated with modifier kind 14 is unknown; the kind identifies a verified dispatch role, not an arbitrary numbered duplicate.

evidence.note: Doubles both damage estimates when the target has either damage-recoverable ailment at 0x5D or 0x5E. Otherwise leaves the adjusted estimates initialized by the AI caller unchanged.
Multiplies both damage estimates by 1.5 only when the target data pointer is nonnull and its halfword +0xA bits 7 through 10 equal 8. The AI caller resolves this data for the target.
evidence.uncertainty: The gameplay identity of target type 8 is unproven.

evidence.note: Scales both input damage estimates by 1.5 when target data exists and its packed four-bit type equals 5, then returns success.
evidence.uncertainty: The gameplay identity of target type 5 is unproven.

evidence.note: Writes the adjusted pair as the two input estimates multiplied by float constant 0x3FA66666, approximately 1.3. Invoked by the AI modifier dispatcher at kind 24.
Returns success without accessing the estimate context. The AI power-modifier table references this distinct callback at kind 25.
evidence.uncertainty: The ability associated with kind 25 is unknown; the kind is the verified dispatch discriminator.

evidence.note: Scales both damage estimates by 1.5 for a nonnull target-data pointer whose halfword +0xA bits 7 through 10 equal 6; otherwise preserves the initialized adjusted pair.
evidence.uncertainty: The gameplay identity of target type 6 is unproven.

evidence.note: Computes 2 times the attacker current vocation level plus 125 for the first adjusted estimate, and 85 percent of that value for the second. The AI estimation context stores the attacker pointer at +0.
Returns success without reading or mutating state. The AI modifier dispatch table references this callback at kind 31.
evidence.uncertainty: The ability associated with kind 31 is unknown; the kind distinguishes an actual dispatch role.

evidence.note: Clears response and affirmative counters at 0x4444/0x4445, invalidates the selected responder, and clears pending/result flags. TrackMemberResponsesAndDispatchGroupCompletion uses these fields for trigger group 29.

Initializes GameState resources, party objects, zone resources, queues, cameras, status UI and lighting; runs the input/update/render loop until exit or reload; then releases scene resources and clears object pointers.
Updates zones, scene commands, camera, party and actor movement, collision, messages, deferred revivals, brightness and ownership requests. Called once per iteration by the scene lifecycle.
Requires an allocator, resets any prior presentation owner, allocates and initializes a new owner at 0x4498, snapshots the zone-appropriate texture allocation, and queues data/effect/ev999992400.chr.

Scales the leader signed movement step at 0xB2 by a fixed-point factor; commits unconditionally when requested, or only when the normalized direction dot the stored movement vector is at most the threshold.
evidence.uncertainty: The precise units of the movement step at 0xB2 are not established.

evidence.note: Scans container render entries, pushes the object outside the horizontal radius when vertical proximity permits, selects the closest facing candidate, and queues an interaction descriptor of kind 5 when commands and object actions allow.

Advances one indexed party object, resolves party/container and zone collisions, restores blocked movement, adjusts heading along wall contact, suppresses tiny displacement and caps displacement to the original movement distance.

Updates the active roster through the movement/collision helper, handles unlisted local and remote followers, advances the attached effect, and updates special party member 0xCE under the same movement gates.
Filters four party members by zone, scene render flags, selection masks and special equipment exclusions, draws eligible members, then draws special member 0xCE and its shadow.

Draws a party member or its alternate model, propagates inherited alpha to equipment, renders equipment at attachment bones and child objects, draws its shadow, and restores temporary transition height.

Selects and resets a character resource context, allocates the object subtype selected by flags, registers its index and eleven equipment objects where applicable, initializes transform/collision defaults, and attaches indexed character state.
Stores the three supplied coordinates. QueuePositiveRecordAndNotifyConnection uses this leaf to snapshot member zero position into GameState action-position storage.

Cancels queued resource work, saves the member display name, invalidates its character resource context, clears the member and eleven equipment slots, compacts follower order and rebuilds roster/camera state. Client transition members reset linked state instead.

Protects the local/protagonist/leader index, clears disconnect flags, optionally removes the peer, destroys its field objects, clears ownership and acknowledgements, and releases matching field-monster selections.

Orders leader and associated followers by life state and formation slot, returns the active indices, sets predecessor/leader/order and movement-input flags, optionally resets trails and preserves formation positions, and refreshes the status portrait.

Copies the template name into linked character state, repacks base-stat percentage fields, recalculates derived stats, preserves HP for an unchanged template or restores default HP, restores MP, resets vocation/skills and learns the template spell.
evidence.uncertainty: The source template category is not conclusively identified.

evidence.note: Scans supported combatants in the protagonist zone, applies alpha/tint/polygon presets according to dirty bits 2 and 4, restores default appearance when clear, and clears each dirty bit.
evidence.uncertainty: Visual presets are proven; their gameplay status labels are not.

evidence.note: Requires a client session and an active party transition owner, then checks its 0x101, 0xF8 mask, 0xFF and phase 0xCF fields. Creation/removal/equipment paths use this to select saved-state handling.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact transition subtype is not established; the name describes the proven client-only restriction.

evidence.note: Detects contact with visible remote party members, queues eligible interactions and tracks contact bits. Host/offline updates collision for all field monsters; clients restrict collision to their assigned monster block.

Expands/scales instance triangles, rotates the object into local space, intersects floor geometry for height/contact material, resolves the collision sphere against walls, and writes corrected position and wall/floor descriptors.
Scans vertically and horizontally nearby chest entries, constructs their eight-polygon collision shape and delegates floor/wall resolution to the instance polygon solver, accumulating wall contacts.

Builds object bounds, collects zone-instance collision polygons, resolves floor/wall/chest contact and optional two-step movement, rolls back blocked movement, updates airborne/input state and slows movement near selected interaction targets.

Collects nearby zone polygons, expands and transforms triangles, probes downward for floor contact materials, writes the floor descriptor and clears the object vertical transition offset; returns the number of collected polygons.

Initializes geometry/render state, submits camera and lighting, draws the world pass with optional DMA suppression, draws marked-object/command passes in their configured order, and performs the final scene render pass.

Draws zone geometry, ground-model actors, wandering-monster shadows, unmarked display entries, controlled/linked actors, party effects, grotto entrance effects and world placements, respecting brightness and scene render flags.

Temporarily installs a fixed projection/view for marked display objects and optional scene queue drawing selected by the mode bits, then restores the saved world view/projection and submits render configuration.

Initializes orthographic geometry, processes the front action, draws text windows and interaction sprites, party overlays, background gradient, touch movement indicator, navigation messages and atmospheric effects.

Scans twelve monsters in the active tracked-zone group, checks visibility, alpha, contact and facing, handles interactive monsters and nearby unlisted party encounters, and queues the encounter action with its opening outcome.

Scans type-nine regions, tests position and facing with a short input threshold, resolves the paired type-nine entry, constructs endpoint vectors and angles, copies GameObject ladder traversal state and sets the traversal system flag.

Collects up to two containing type-two regions according to feature flags, facing and movement direction; ranks their interaction by averaged position and activates selected features after a sustained approach threshold.
Scans Zone3D chest entries, rejects height and horizontal-distance mismatches, ranks facing angles and openability, then submits a chest interaction candidate with index, pointer and approach angle.
Finds the containing type-three feature and compares it with the actor action-context pointer. Runs group five for the old region and group two for the new region, then stores the new context.

Scans type-four containment regions and applies camera action-four/action-five plane blends, recentering and orbit-input policy. Restores region input and disables blending when no applicable region remains.

With an empty action queue and no actor actions, finds a containing type-five feature, updates the directional movement vector and submits interaction kind seven with feature pointer and signed facing difference.
evidence.uncertainty: The gameplay identity of type-five features is not proven.

evidence.note: Finds a containing type-ten feature whose identifier and zone match the stored zone selection, then submits an enabled kind-eleven interaction candidate.
evidence.uncertainty: Type-ten feature gameplay identity is not proven; only the zone/identifier match is established.

evidence.note: Requires map eligibility, finds an enabled placement near the actor, accepts A or touch activation, queues synchronization, clears the placement bit, sets its progress flag, removes its world instance and queues the pickup presentation.

Checks grotto discovery state, matching zone, entrance position, brightness and session policy; registers the entrance interaction and accepts activation to queue a grotto zone transition or the undiscovered-entrance action.

Scans serialized progress-state oriented region bounds, compares the containing identifier with the previous region byte, dispatches group-five leave and group-two enter commands and updates the active identifier.

Processes selected type-two feature pointers, dispatches trigger group 17, invokes Zone3D activation, applies pending transition vectors to features and queues their transition action or resets approach state.

Reads the selected chest and index. Nonstandard chest mode dispatches trigger group 18; ordinary chests initialize the chest action, reverse its approach angle, copy chest position and queue the action.
Processes only requests addressed to this member or broadcast; rejects mismatched actor zones or interaction tokens and otherwise replies with packet 0x9a using local/requester member ordering.
evidence.uncertainty: The final response bit is described as acceptance policy without assigning a specific gameplay interaction.

evidence.note: Advances the shortcut display through string-table and layer-resource loading, configures BG1/BG2 and blending, allocates four text canvases, attaches them to the selection window and populates their assigned-action labels.
Opens the shortcut display on a B press when movement/actions permit, saves background controls and pauses movement; closes it on release or blocking actions and advances loading while active.
The complete body immediately returns without reading or modifying state; its recorded caller is field scene initialization.
evidence.uncertainty: No implemented purpose beyond an empty startup hook can be recovered.

evidence.note: Updates party overlay state, requires a fully loaded active shortcut display and no scripted action selector, refreshes the window canvases and marks the rectangle for the selected assigned action before transfers.
Configures four window canvas rectangles, looks up protagonist action-shortcut assignments, formats their labels, pushes the text canvases and clears their per-canvas auxiliary status.
Clears the HUD touch-capture byte at 0x3658. The touch handler sets it while an on-screen control holds movement input disabled, and name-entry completion clears it when restoring the display.
evidence.uncertainty: The specific HUD icon identity is not proven.

evidence.note: Projects selected NPC, party member or monster positions to place the interaction icon, tests touch bounds or A input, dispatches the callback table by selected interaction kind and consumes activation state.
Draws context-sensitive field HUD icons subject to queued actions and movement restrictions; separately projects remote members and draws status/interaction markers with a three-marker limit.

Rejects interaction lock, ladder traversal, actor restrictions and shortcut display; compares candidate facing rank, copies the winning kind/index/pointers/angles into shared state and resolves its default icon from a type table.

Under the loader lock loads chest models and NARC sprite resources, localizes the main interaction icon, creates the pickup world object, loads touch render parts and binds container render models into Zone3D.
Cancels staging for both chest models, resets touch and interaction render parts, detaches the world pickup object and resets their allocator and VRAM allocation snapshot.
Loads icon.nsarc and text-window frames; unless frame-only mode is requested, loads kanoke.nsbmd, kage.chr, obj_def.pac and bg_def.bncl into the shared resource allocator.

Initializes and queues a destination-zone transition, optionally resolves a Zoom destination, restores leader-only rendering, then queues memory2.stb or chooses a chur_messet.bin message by chapter and day/night.
evidence.uncertainty: Exact interpretation of the incoming return-reason selector and the church-message variants remains unproven.

evidence.note: Initializes the script action, selects memory2.stb with code pointer 0x021689d8 and mode four, sets execution flags and appends the reusable action to the field queue.

Skips conflicting actions and fades, handles client refresh, tests Opcode68 exit volumes, submits manual exit interactions or fills automatic requests, then queues the zone transition and dispatches zone-leave trigger group six.

Recognizes specific destination zones and zone families, revives dead members with destination-dependent HP restoration, resets death motion/flags and updates party representation and synchronization; special destinations also revive eligible followers.

Resolves source/destination zone metadata, synchronizes progress/day state, updates and revives the party, resets actor/monster resources and message usage, switches resource pools by zone category, prepares grotto transition state and calls Zone3D::SwitchZone.

Remaps special zone identifiers, updates the party member and associated follower zone/tracking identifiers, applies destination revival, clears movement/ladder state, restores alpha and refreshes client/day synchronization when applicable.

Host-only handling ensures the requested tracked zone and monster pool, chooses the nearest spawn entry, records grotto floor data and initializes or requeues its per-group type-20 load action with member and mode parameters.

Maps destination zone category to one of six pool profiles, tears down the previous profile, initializes allocator/VRAM reservations for the new profile and resets/repopulates overlay selection stacks.
Finds the tracked zone, visits its twelve monster slots and clones cached models/animations into them; rejects nonzero local member IDs in an active session.
Destination map kind and descriptor bit 7 determine camera follow-control mask 0x10 during zone switching.
evidence.uncertainty: The precise meanings of these control bits are unresolved.

evidence.note: Fades screens, changes BGM, waits for queues/network, switches zones, loads treasure and placements, executes entry events and restores party/camera state.
Empty body is the tag-3 cleanup callback in the queue release dispatcher; no resource is freed by this callback.
Requires transition flag 1, optionally revives and restores protagonist/associated members, records options and fixed zone 0x10d0 destination and optionally queues tag 3.
evidence.uncertainty: The recovery destination gameplay identity is not established.

evidence.note: Returns zero unconditionally; packet identifies its caller as a field subscreen handler.
evidence.uncertainty: The caller-specific interpretation of the false result is unresolved.

evidence.note: Frees allocation at +0x9c and creates pools 5, 12, 15 and 16 from an index/size table; the shared subscreen handler uses pool 5.
evidence.uncertainty: Individual pool purposes are not fully recovered.

evidence.note: Destroys and frees pools 0 and 7; caller selects this table-based routine for destination map kinds 2 and 3.
evidence.uncertainty: Map-kind gameplay meanings are unresolved; separate modes intentionally share pool lists.

evidence.note: Destroys and frees pools 0 and 7; caller selects this routine for kinds outside its explicit map-kind cases.
evidence.uncertainty: The default map-kind geography or gameplay meaning is unresolved.

evidence.note: Destroys and frees pools 20, 0, 7, 21 and 26 from a terminated index table; caller selects it for descriptor kind 7.
evidence.uncertainty: Map kind 7 gameplay meaning remains unresolved.

evidence.note: Destroys and frees pools 20, 0 and 7 from a terminated index table; caller selects it for descriptor kind 8.
evidence.uncertainty: Map kind 8 gameplay meaning remains unresolved.

evidence.note: Destroys and frees pools 0 and 7; caller selects this routine for destination map kind 5.
evidence.uncertainty: Map-kind gameplay meanings are unresolved; other modes also free these pools.

evidence.note: Destroys and frees pools 0 and 7; caller selects this routine for destination map kind 6.
evidence.uncertainty: Map-kind gameplay meanings are unresolved; other modes also free these pools.

evidence.note: Fades out, allocates and initializes overlay-23 screen, supplies party list for selector 3, updates/releases screen, reloads field resources and restores camera.
evidence.uncertainty: Screen selectors span multiple subscreens; a single gameplay menu identity is not proven.

evidence.note: Wraps counter above 0x7ff7 to one, rejects IDs used by forty-eight monsters or party-sync entries, returns fresh ID and advances counter.

Host updates visible active-group monsters, preserves protected flags/states 8 and 9, hides those outside all same-zone wandering-actor bounds and broadcasts removal; clients update current-zone monsters.
Selects up to seven minus same-zone party count nearest visible monsters, draws selected objects and renders shadows scaled by monster size and zone opacity.
Scans up to twelve objects from 112 plus group times twelve and returns first existing slot with negative model identifier, or -1.
Resolves monster/behavior data, acquires group slot, clones cache, applies ground placement, angle, collision, scale and behavior, assigns unique ID and publishes visible spawn.
Rejects clients, selects zone/time monster choice, computes a point ahead of a party member, replaces eligible slot if necessary and calls tracked-zone spawning.
Extracts selected monster archives from enemy.gp2, loads .cchr models into allocator, registers cache slots from index 7, saves VRAM state and refreshes clones.
Opens data/scenario/%s.npc, executes place.bin and npc.bin with zone/progress values, creates actor representations and adjusts eligible actor positions to ground.
Resets field objects, loads NPC and linked actors, partitions remaining heap, loads/shows discovered grotto entrance, loads monster cache and prepares remaining zone resources.
Returns for null nodes and switches on signed tags through 0x4e, routing queue/node to field, subscreen, interaction and network state handlers.
Checks selected actor/chest, lock and multiplayer restrictions, plays opening animations, formats/grants loot, records collection and queues special reward follow-up.
Stops movement, plays pickup motion, resolves reward, loads /data/ani/d_%c%03d.spr, displays message and floating/fading sprite and releases allocator/display state.
Queue release wrapper forwards pickup command to its sprite allocator cleanup routine.
Dispatches peer identity resolution, member activation, packet reception restrictions and failure handlers; completion clears connection-transition flag and restores display overlay.
Writes argument bit 0 to flag 0x20; load/return handlers skip replacing and restoring secondary render flags and 3D clear color.
evidence.uncertainty: Any additional behavior inside overlay 11 is unresolved.

evidence.note: Queue cleanup wrapper calls routine destroying the loot command's two allocators and restoring game resource flags.
Captures container position, rejects collected loot, formats/grants reward, records break/collection flags and broadcasts them, or restores movement and completes when empty.
For loot kind 1 selects sprite i127; otherwise extracts sprite character code and preferred attribute from serialized reward. Returns phase 2.
Disables camera/movement, allocates panel/heap, pushes overlay selection 3, initializes/updates panel, then frees it and restores camera/input/resource flags.
evidence.uncertainty: A specific inn or shop screen identity is not proven.

evidence.note: Passes the queue front to the type-22 drawing dispatcher; the scene caller installs the projection used for display objects.
Rejects null or completed records and kinds other than 22, then draws the embedded Object3D only in its ready state.
Forwards the queue front to the per-kind drawing dispatcher from the field overlay rendering pass.
Skips missing or completed records and dispatches by signed record kind to text, menu, effect and other overlay drawing hooks.
Passes the queue front to the world-object drawing dispatcher before the scene draws world geometry.
Walks every linked record via its next pointer, dispatches kind-specific cancellation or resource release, and clears both queue endpoints.
Checks presence and completion before dispatching transfer hooks, including TextWindow_RenderAndTransferDisplayBuffers and canvas transfer resets.
Resets shared interaction targets, scans actors and nearby multiplayer members, applies facing and movement restrictions, and submits an interaction descriptor.
Resolves the selected actor, activates its quest order, executes trigger group zero, or queues the actor dialogue record when no trigger succeeds.
Scans all 32 active actors, evaluates interaction rectangles or distance and facing, returns the best actor slot, and suppresses autonomous motion nearby.
Requires an idle queue and controllable protagonist, handles X to queue the party menu and Y/touch shortcuts to story.stb or the grotto-specific record.
Allocates the ov002 menu and arena, pushes overlay selections, polls menu completion, restores rendering and camera/movement control, then releases the command.
Initializes type 59, clears receive state and capacity-failure flag, and saves the supplied mode in GameState; its updater registers received treasure-map metadata.
evidence.uncertainty: The GameState mode byte meaning is not decoded.

evidence.note: Checks the 99-map capacity limit, adds received metadata or offers a follow-up choice, displays messages and dispatches trigger group 27 before restoring field control.
Empty hook reached by the queue display-transfer dispatcher for the received-map registration command.
Configures an overlay-load command for tmap.stb, inserts it at the requested queue end, fades the scene to black and blocks map fade-in.
Accepts buttons or touch while the shared text window is idle/ready, plays the confirmation sound and reports whether an advance was requested.
Collects eligible listed members, applies the associated linked-state operation, formats each member name into a message stating HP became 1, and advances until acknowledged.
Empty cancellation/release hook selected for the HP-reduced-to-one notification record by the all-command cleanup dispatcher.
Loads bg_tm and bm_rev layouts, handles the two-choice recovery prompt, fades out, invokes party revival/recovery completion and releases its display resources.
Only draws in the prompt interaction phase; copies display parts to layers, finds the selected entry position and submits the animated cursor sprite there.
Returns success without side effects. ROM opcode table at 0x021D78A4 assigns this exact callback to opcode 100 for riremito.bin.
Returns success without side effects. The same escape-script opcode table assigns this callback to opcode 101; opcode 102 chooses the destination row.
Uses grotto exit metadata or executes data/map/riremito.bin, resolves an exit destination and queues the escape effect plus the pending field transition.
Initializes kind 28, effect phase/timer, departure mode, actor mask, allocator and background-task sentinel for the em1800 departure sequence.
Loads em1800.chr, spawns effect instances at the selected party positions, times sound and visibility changes, fades out, restores control and optionally queues memory2.stb.
Loads localized htana scenario data for the zone feature, selects text by progress flags, presents it, merges associated collectible IDs and dispatches trigger group 24.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact collectible category merged by the optional reward list is not established.

evidence.note: Returns success without side effects. ROM table at 0x021D7900 maps this function to opcode 101 for the htana scenario-text reader.
Returns success without side effects. ROM table at 0x021D7900 maps this function to opcode 100, alongside the entry-population opcode 102.
Acquires GameState, network and field-resource singletons, then returns the shared text context; the command-update dispatcher calls this hook for kind 1.
evidence.uncertainty: The singleton acquisitions have no explicit mutation in this wrapper.

evidence.note: Empty overlay-draw hook reached for kind 1, whose party effects and text panel have separate drawing paths.
Sets the command completion byte; the queue-wide release dispatcher selects this hook for kind 1.
Loads one of two effect archives, spawns party-position effects, coordinates fades and field return requests, or runs the alternate rising-party/camera-shake sequence.
evidence.uncertainty: The archives and movement/fade behavior are proven; the exact spell or travel feature for every option combination is not.

evidence.note: Marks the party-effect command complete and calls the arena release helper used for its SafeAllocator at offset 8.
Cancels timed text, initializes a one-entry selection panel using standard string 31, centers it at Y=64 and starts its opening animation.
Draws the embedded selection panel at offset 0x44 with its cursor, using the standard zero draw mode.
Allocates a 0x32000 arena and ov003 screen, pushes overlay 3/secondary 1, polls the screen, restores display/camera/input state and releases the arena.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact town facility served by this ov003 screen is not established.

evidence.note: Selects equipment-descriptor/model refresh or alternate NPC appearance loading, polls asynchronous stages, binds archives and completes the member refresh command.
Waits for the equipment archive, initializes all 11 equipment descriptors, fills them from serialized records, removes the task and marks changed linked equipment stats.
Attaches the loaded item battle-parameter table, copies matching 44-byte records into eight equipment slots, removes the load task and recalculates derived stats.
Polls eleven model and three animation tasks, binds equipment models and archives with VRAM state handling, applies palettes/shared textures and restores member rendering.

Shared termination path for event phases: restores party motion and stand/ladder animations, clears scene flags, destroys nested and owned allocators, reenables movement and orbit input, and updates multiplayer completion state.
Returns the signed halfword at +14E. The completion phase fills it from the peer event record, and the event packet handler matches incoming IDs against token + 0x8005.
evidence.uncertainty: The token encoding and distinction from the peer event ID are not fully established.

evidence.note: Initializes the type-four event node, selects mode three, sets +9C, snapshots chapter/stage, and copies the zone descriptor. The loading phase uses +9C to select data/map/ineventdata3.bin; the default script name is inevent.stb.

Phase zero of the type-four event table checks conflicting actions and ladder state, switches scene overlay, disables movement/orbit input, freezes party motion, and queues the inevent, quest, LV5 or ordinary event-list script.

Phase one waits for brightness and script loading, executes the loaded script into the event descriptor, tests completion flags, synchronizes progress/daytime and prepares a map reload when required. Otherwise it selects the scene execution phase and fade behavior.

Phase ten waits for background loads, restores zone BMDJ requests and camera following, records event completion bits, processes peer acknowledgements, and chooses another event, return-map transition or normal field cleanup.

Copies packet mode/flags, two map IDs, a condition byte and four event-related halfwords into +13C..+14C, then sets +FC. Completion logic consumes these fields to coordinate client event continuation.
If the leader stats record has flag one, the parent/offline path applies and clears that status, resets motion and +B2, optionally broadcasts the change, then refreshes party resources.

Type-0x37 handler waits for display request 0x204, then prepares a return transition using zone-saved position/yaw and map 10000 or 10100, or queues a special event. Clients instead show a formatted refusal message and restore input.
evidence.uncertainty: The particular spell/menu action requesting this return is not proven.

Allocates scrolling tiles and the script arena, resets frame timing and update/upload toggle, then captures the epoch used by the elapsed-time getter.
Converts timestamp elapsed since start into 60 Hz ticks, dispatches only when elapsed ticks change, toggles the upload stage and records time since the allocation epoch.
Runs the phase handler only while phase is zero; when asynchronous display/script initialization reaches phase one, captures the scrolling start timestamp and resets elapsed ticks.
Initializes the singleton state, allocates its buffers and schedules the periodic VAlarm at scanline 215 with delay 30 and the alternating update/upload callback.
Forwards to AdvanceInitialization with the singleton staff-roll state; distinct from the state-taking helper.
Returns cached time since the buffer-allocation epoch as (delta << 6) / 33514, matching the timestamp-to-millisecond conversion in include/System/Timing.h and System timing routines.
Runs timing and graphics cleanup and returns the state pointer; registered as the singleton destructor by __sinit_ov028_021d9a54.
Reads a script integer as an unsigned-short record capacity and allocates/initializes the active credit list through the script execution context.
Sets a credit record to invalid ID -1, zero vertical spacing and formatting flags, and null text; used for both allocated slots and script-created temporary records.
Converts the script parameter to float and stores it in the active credit list speed, which the drawing and final-scroll phases multiply by elapsed ticks.
Clears the list pointer, used count and capacity and sets the staff-roll scroll speed to 1.0.
Cleanup wrapper reinitializes the credit list through InitializeRecordList; Graphics_RestoreCanvasDisplayState calls it while destroying the owning arena.
Binds the active list and allocator in a shared script context, installs the overlay opcode lookup table, loads the supplied definition bytecode and executes it to populate credits.
Rejects null input or a full list; otherwise copies ID, vertical spacing, formatting and text pointer into the next slot and increments used count.
Returns the indexed credit record only when the index is below used count; Text_DrawScrollingRecords treats null as the end of the credits.

Reads a selected font bitmap and glyph metrics, tests individual glyph bits across twelve rows, and writes the supplied 16-bit color into a framebuffer with a 256-pixel stride.
Measures and centers one or two caption lines, processes glyph advances and kerning, optionally draws a four-direction black outline, and limits rendering to the supplied progressive character count.
The concrete NitroVM adapter vtable points its deleting destructor slot here. It forwards the adapter allocation to the global SafeAllocator free thunk and returns the original pointer.
Null-safe forwarding getter for the selected compressed frame audio-block count. The playback loops use the result to bound repeated PCM block decoding.

Returns one of the two low-14-bit compressed-frame header values, selected by the active input-buffer index. Playback uses it as its PCM decode loop limit; the record-advance routine multiplies it by channel count for total audio-block tracking.

Codec-one dispatch invokes this body with per-channel state. Its internal routines unpack residual/codebook data and apply multiply-accumulate prediction; the public path alternates history buffers, saturates 128 results to signed 16-bit PCM, writes with the channel stride, and returns consumed bytes.
evidence.uncertainty: The codec-specific published algorithm name is not established locally; several internal routines are encoded as dcb words in the assembly listing.

Queues camera opcode 9; its handler advances the configured paired transition and wraps through its path.
