Validates encounter key and active scene, reconstructs four 24-bit awards, then either forwards them to the combat award routine or updates the local protagonist experience-earned statistics in both normal and compact records.
Reads context +0x44 or zero. Overlay-31 sets completion bits here; menu callers test bits 1, 2, 4 and 0x80 to select success and failure messages.
Compares the low 12-bit year first, then month/day/hour/minute fields using weights 1000000, 10000 and 100. The overlay-31 caller packs year+2000, month, day, hour and minute before calling it.
Swaps the two incoming packed words and calls IsPackedDateTimeEarlier, implementing the reverse chronological comparison.
When the shared overlay-11 canvas exists, calls the wrapper which walks its node list at +0x118 and invokes the second virtual method.
evidence.uncertainty: The lifecycle meaning of this virtual slot is not established.

evidence.note: Checks the shared canvas pointer and calls Ov011_ForwardObjectAt118, whose body forwards its node list to Object_InvokeUpdateOnLinkedNodes.

Waits for brightness and successful background loading, loads overlay 11, pushes overlay selections, allocates its 0x1E0-byte canvas, initializes SB2 script buffers and the remaining node allocator, runs the setup callback, and returns state 2.

Collects three canvas result flags, releases the overlay state and cached resources, then returns alternate states 5/6/7 or restores field camera input, zone rendering flags, resource flags and lighting clear color before returning 4.
Waits while Zone3D +0x424 reports ongoing work. On completion clears the secondary transition flag and the screen reload bit, then returns transition state 3.

Handler for 0xAA in the command dispatch table. Searches the local member list for both signed participant IDs, then routes action codes 1..8 to the field resource owner or menu-result state 2/5/6/7/8.
evidence.uncertainty: Specific gameplay actions remain unproven; membership gating and result dispatch are explicit.

evidence.note: The body immediately returns. Its pointer occupies command 0x95 in the incoming dispatch table at 021D7F98, between handlers for types 0x94 and 0x96.

Resolves the indicated party member and enables flag 0x400 plus optional control flag 0x20. The release branch visits the sender group, clears those flags and marks the corresponding sender bit when releasing control.

Compares the packed recipient against the local member ID, multiplies the chunk index by fourteen and copies the encoded byte count into serialized progress state +0x2CC, using the low-byte destination offset.

Builds type 0x9D with a two-bit recipient and byte offset, copies at most fourteen bytes from the supplied buffer while capping at 0x2E0, then queues it. The matching handler copies this into its active resource buffer.
Handler for type 0x9E copies the payload halfword into +0x24 of the transition request owned through GameResources +0x370C.
evidence.uncertainty: The field role within the transition request is unresolved.

evidence.note: The body immediately returns. The command dispatch table registers it for opcode 0x1D immediately after the inn recovery-value handler.

Phase 1 checks recipient membership, idle queues and member availability, returns flagged equipment from eligible slots to inventory, clears equipped stats/status, refreshes party state and replies with phase 2 or 3. Later phases update sender resources and menu response state.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact gameplay interaction is unresolved; equipment return and the three exchange phases are explicit.

evidence.note: For command phase 1 filters the target roster and screens, applies bounded HP/MP changes, status cures and revival, optionally formats str_tm messages, then queues success or rejected results. Phases 2/3 convert packed amounts into per-member display results; phase 4 marks rejection.
Clears the kind byte, amount halfword and auxiliary byte in a six-byte display-result record. The recovery handler invokes it for both four-element result arrays.

Requires the encoded recipient to match the local member. Copies the encoded byte count into ZoneState0840 at the packet offset; the final-chunk bit marks completion and disables incoming record type 0xB9.
Only handles the packet in a client session. Stores its byte into ZoneState0840 tier +0x1B3C (Zone3D +0x237C) and calls ResourceContext_SetActiveFlagIfIdle.
The type-0xBB dispatch-table handler copies the received payload word into the shared overlay scalar at 021D847C.
evidence.uncertainty: Only storage of the type-0xBB payload is proven. Its gameplay purpose is not established; the same base symbol is also used to address adjacent static-initializer data.

evidence.note: Saturating countdown at +0x598 returns whether a delay remains. The church dialog update at 02158e94 calls it before dispatch; its save sequence sets this timer to 15.

Queues str_rki or scenario str_in language text, bg_tm.pac, and obj_rikka.pac. Polls all three tasks, creates two canvases and sprite tracks, gathers eligible guests, computes the stay price, and enters the choice state.
Formats guest count and total price into the greeting, chooses text according to day and network role, creates the stay options, and maps confirmation or cancellation to rest/day-choice/exit states.

Checks carried gold against total price, fades out and plays the rest sequence, obtains network ownership, deducts payment, restores guest HP/MP, sets the selected day threshold, then fades in and shows the completion message.
Reformats the current choice canvas on selection changes and rebuilds the gold canvas when its dirty flag is set. The gold formatter previews the balance after payment when +0x3bb equals two.
Builds a two- or three-option list from network role and current day period, measures labels, sizes and positions the canvas, formats its cursor text, and pushes it onto the stay window.

Main update for the shared str_lui/str_lav party menu: handles interrupted network sessions and close requests, advances portrait and canvas resources, runs pending messages, processes selection input, and dispatches the menu state table.
Finds a present character-list display group, walks four marker codes at +0x468, obtains each row position, and submits the corresponding sprite with a horizontal offset of 56 pixels.
evidence.uncertainty: The marker codes derive from character flag bits; their exact visual meaning is not established.

evidence.note: Accepts confirmation keys only after the field-input cooldown, reads a visible option-window result or touch-selected canvas entry, synchronizes linked row highlights, and returns whether an entry was confirmed.
Clamps the roster expansion value at +0xf70 to four, adds the base eight slots with a twelve-slot cap, and returns both capacity and capacity minus stored-character count.

Formats the current or fallback message with party count and selected character descriptors, starts it through the shared text context, handles automatic continuation, then advances queued message keys or closes the message/menu state.
Walks active party indices, excludes the protagonist, resolves each remaining party member, and resets its follow trail before recruitment or storage changes.
Walks active roster object indices except the selected member at +0x482 and counts resolved combatants with nonzero HP. The storage menu uses zero to reject removing the last living member.

Creates the party-service choice group, dispatches selected entries to recruitment, member storage, character creation, dismissal, and related service states, and checks roster limits before those transitions.
evidence.uncertainty: Some service branches remain raw ARM bytes in the reference listing; exact dialogue meanings and the full option-label mapping are not established.

evidence.note: Builds and pages the stored-character recruitment list, updates the character preview, checks active-party capacity and special record statuses, confirms selection, then invokes the stored-character activation sequence. The extra row routes to character creation when capacity permits.

Builds the active-member list, rejects storage when no other living party member remains, checks special character statuses, resets follow trails, and routes to the storage operation or its explanatory message.

Collects the character-creation choice, calls the creation/append routine, displays the resulting stored character and checks active-party space. Confirmation activates that character, removes its serialized roster entry, and advances to the party transition.
Pages stored characters, rejects protected record status values, requests confirmation, then returns the selected character equipment to the bag and removes its roster entry.

Fades and hides party actors, waits for queued loads, starts one of two field transition tasks, restores actor visibility/positions, and queues roster presentation work before resetting menu text and character tracking.
evidence.uncertainty: The special flag-0x40 branch changes fixed scene placement and task selection; the exact destination/event is not proven.

evidence.note: Chooses the multiplayer option group according to offline/host/guest classification, processes confirmation/cancellation, and routes to discovery, hosting, departure, or explanatory dialogue while updating the selected group palette.
evidence.uncertainty: Several branch bodies are represented as raw ARM bytes; the exact text-label mapping is not established.

evidence.note: Coordinates a required save, enables peer discovery, collects and sorts up to eight advertised sessions, renders a paged selection, verifies the chosen peer address, and queues a join request with timeout/cancel and success/failure paths.

Confirms the host setup path, waits for loader idleness, performs a staged save under loader locking, starts/reset host networking through Network_ResetConnectionPoolsAndRefreshPartySlots, and presents the subsequent confirmation/exit dialogue.

Waits for confirmation and pending loads, rejects ending while other valid members remain, otherwise preserves orbit camera state around Field_EndMultiplayerSessionAndRestoreLocalParty and returns to the multiplayer menu.

Formats four active-member rows from the eligible member index list: character names, selected vocation, levels, status labels, colors and marker codes. Rebuilds the group, row markers, and selection geometry for the storage screen.

Formats four paged stored-character rows with decoded names, vocation, level, status colors and marker codes; highlights the selected slot, adds the conditional creation row, updates capacity/page labels, and rebuilds row overlays.

Formats four paged stored-character rows with names, vocation, levels, status labels, marker codes and empty-row placeholders, then updates paging/capacity labels and redraws groups used by the dismissal screen.

Renders four of eight advertised session records for the selected page, colors entries by availability and selection, displays session names and remaining party places, supplies empty placeholders, and updates the two-page indicator.

Finds the selected serialized character and a free actor slot, fades the sub-screen, initializes character state and spawns an actor, copies its name/vocation/level, links protagonist ownership, waits for field work, and synchronizes the new member over the network. Returns zero while pending, one on success, or minus one when no actor slot is free.
Tests dirty bits at +0x464, clears the layer at +0x328+0x40, fills full-screen or selected-row rectangles, and cleans its destination cache. Called during the active town-party menu redraw.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact contents of each masked region are not established.

evidence.note: Clears resource pointers, saves sub BG/OBJ VRAM bank assignments, snapshots sub background controls and display-enable bits, and initializes the requested display mode and character index.
The entire body returns without side effects. The member table at 0x0217f4f0 places this callback in display mode 1, alongside the active-character mode 2 and roster-character mode 6 handlers.
evidence.uncertainty: Mode 1 has no recovered semantic label; the mode qualifier identifies its actual table slot rather than an arbitrary duplicate suffix.

evidence.note: Resolves the indexed active GameObject, recalculates derived character statistics, fills its name/vocation summary and five skill lines, unpacks twelve numeric statistics, and configures the canvas display part.
The complete body is empty. The seven-entry member dispatch table places it at mode 3 in the shared sub-screen character-status controller.
evidence.uncertainty: Mode 3 has no recovered semantic label; the qualifier is the actual dispatch-table mode.

evidence.note: The complete body is empty. The member dispatch table places it at mode 4 in the shared sub-screen character-status controller.
evidence.uncertainty: Mode 4 has no recovered semantic label; the qualifier is the actual dispatch-table mode.

evidence.note: The complete body is empty. The member dispatch table places it at mode 5 in the shared sub-screen character-status controller.
evidence.uncertainty: Mode 5 has no recovered semantic label; the qualifier is the actual dispatch-table mode.

evidence.note: Finds a stored character by slot ID, converts its saved name, reads selected vocation and packed statistics, fills skill-line values, and configures the status canvas. This is mode 6 in the member table.
Loops over five skill lines using Vocation_GetSkillLineId, fills label and numeric canvas entries, highlights values equal to 100, and hides both entries when the vocation is zero.

Runs the asynchronous loading stages for str_bank.gp2/str_bank_<LG>.nat, bg_tm.pac and cell_inst.pac; creates backgrounds, three canvases and sprite resources before entering the initial dialog state.
Pops the transaction menu, clears the text buffer, appends the balance/farewell text and starts the message. After message completion it marks the bank dialog finished.
Configures both grids as one column of three menu choices for canvas mode 1, or four digit columns for mode 2, and restores the corresponding remembered selection index.

Initializes digit and touch-rectangle grids; handles directional edits, touch arrows and held-touch repeats; clamps against the permitted amount; and converts four digits to thousand-gold units on confirmation. Returns waiting, accepted or canceled status.
Reformats menu or numeric-entry canvas text after selection/touch changes; when the gold-change flag is set, replaces canvas 0 text using the new held-gold value and clears that flag.
Appends string key 1091 with the bank balance when +0xf68 is nonzero; otherwise appends key 1090 with the protagonist name. Both paths expand and wrap into the shared scratch buffer.

Allocates a selection controller, two background transfer records, one canvas, fifteen sprite transforms and an animation track list from the supplied arena. The Rikka inn scene wrapper calls this setup.

Loads str_rkm.gp2 localized strings, bg_tm.pac and obj_rikka.pac; initializes window, background and sprite resources; and chooses the opening service state according to scene mode and multiplayer availability.
Builds the opening message from string key 0 and the first set bit of Zone3D notification byte +0x2382, clears those notification bits, waits for messages, then enters the service menu.
evidence.uncertainty: The five notification messages are not decoded, so their individual gameplay meanings remain unproven.

evidence.note: Waits for greeting/presentation completion, initializes the four-choice localized service menu, advances its animation, accepts key/touch confirmation or cancellation, and selects the corresponding service state.

Rejects the operation when an active session has multiple members; otherwise allocates and drives the embedded selection panel at +0x410, frees it, reloads obj_rikka.pac and returns to the service prompt.
evidence.uncertainty: The panel presents the inn guest/selection list; the exact list action performed inside its separate handlers is not proven here.

evidence.note: Drives the inn communication dialog, checks multiplayer restrictions and map availability, runs guest/map exchange panels, updates inn-transfer statistics, writes staged saves and handles received legacy-boss maps and their presentation animation.
Only in the idle service-menu state with no active network session, positions sprite transform 6 beside the second marked text rectangle and submits it to OAM.
evidence.uncertainty: The marker graphic is not decoded, so its exact icon meaning is not claimed.

evidence.note: Allocates and initializes the bank dialog, disables movement/camera input, updates the dialog until completion or shutdown, then releases its resources, restores display layers and input and marks the scene task complete.

Allocates the Rikka inn service controller and its resources, supplies the launch mode, disables movement/orbit input, runs its state dispatcher and restores resources/input when finished; also handles external shutdown.
Clears control coordinates, both label pointers and flags, and sets its signed control identifier to -1; Script_BuildAndAppendLinkedStringRecord fills this same record.
Reads layout mask, width and height from script parameters, allocates width times height halfwords, fills cell identifiers and appends the grid to the shared table.
Checks signed column and row against the navigation grid dimensions and returns its signed cell identifier, or -1 outside the grid.
Resolves the current control in the active layout grid, applies directional offsets, handles wrapping and negative placeholder cells, then updates the selected control pointer.
Returns action 10 through keyboard callback table slot 6; UpdateProfileTextEditor validates and commits text for this result, and character creation advances confirmation.
Returns action 12 through keyboard callback table slot 8; UpdateTextEntrySelectionPhase handles this result by calling FormatRandomCategoryEntry.
Returns zero without a selected control; otherwise dispatches one of nine keyboard actions using control byte 0x0d and the callback table at 0x0217f3c8.
Handles D-pad movement and repeat delays, A or optional L activation, optional B deletion and touch hit testing; returns the selected action or a selection-change result.
Computes the requested string length and compares that many bytes with each non-null control label; returns the matching control without altering selection.
For lists longer than four, shows entries 0xd3 through 0xd5 and sets current page plus one and the rounded-up four-entry page count; both party-list builders call it.
Copies the complete 55-byte entry, including its final six-byte identity; the wireless party-selection caller uses it while deleting, compacting and sorting discovered party entries.
Updates the window with game ticks, obtains the touched region from its region table, records press-only activation and dispatches the guest-list state member function.
Loads gl_<LG>.pac, renders up to eight guest names and packed profile fields from the current page, draws paging labels and transfers resources to main backgrounds.
Handles initial help, B exit, left/right page wrapping, up/down row selection and touch selection; confirmation enters the selected guest's action menu.
Runs the selected guest's three-choice action menu, changes kind-nine or kind-ten guest allocation, enforces the six-entry limit, and removes a guest after confirmation.
Builds and centers the three-choice guest window from two labels, configures its selection grids and maps marked text rectangles into touch regions 22 through 24.
Returns the marked action-text rectangle's screen position during the action menu, or x=4 and the selected row's y coordinate in list states; otherwise returns zero coordinates.
Clears the fifty-entry peer cache, exchange flags and counters, initializes retry counts and resets three staged 232-byte guest records including configuration and profile defaults.
Resets wireless buffers and builds native and localized outgoing profiles from the protagonist, greeting, appearance, progress statistics, identifier and optional treasure-map metadata.
Checks host permission, starts a parent session, advertises protagonist identity, activates local membership and resets exchange completion flags with a randomized hosting interval.
Processes member disconnects, tests outgoing queue drain and receive completion, caches the exchanged peer identity and closes the host connection or advances after timeout.
evidence.uncertainty: Unlike the client poller, the timeout field is assigned the effective delta rather than accumulated; the proposal preserves this distinction without assuming intended timing.

evidence.note: Starts the scanning connection state, advertises protagonist identity, clears stale membership and exchange flags, and computes a randomized scan interval adjusted by remaining scan attempts.
Scans discovered peers until the countdown expires, rejects identities already cached, checks advertisement flags, connects to an eligible peer and copies its descriptor and identity.
The complete function returns immediately; relocation 0x0218075c places it in the guest-exchange dispatch table after the post-exchange resource handler.
evidence.uncertainty: The empty callback provides no additional semantic state identity.

evidence.note: Rejects null or all-zero six-byte identities and searches fifty eight-byte cache entries with a nonzero age byte; returns one for a matching identity.
Accumulates payload fragments for the selected member until 224 bytes arrive, normalizes names and treasure-map metadata, validates identity and stages at most three unique guest records.
Requires the guest profile's eligibility bit, then compares its six-byte identifier against all staged 232-byte records and rejects duplicates.
Measures up to two optional labels against a 256-pixel width and draws each twice with adjacent x positions and different palette values to create outlined arrival text.
Loads obj_pm and comb animation resources, renders the capped guest total, loads profstr and str_fms message scripts, then waits for display completion before entering reception state.
Monitors staged guests and new advertised flags, formats guest and title notices, handles touch or B cancellation and confirmation, and transitions the exchange controller toward shutdown.
The complete body is an immediate return; relocation 0x0217fa38 registers it in the main reception-screen state table alongside setup, resource loading and reception update.
evidence.uncertainty: The callback's state has no additional observable behavior.

evidence.note: Loads com_name.pac, renders centered guest or event labels, transfers a notice strip to sub BG0 and eases vertical background scrolling until the new notice is visible.
The complete body returns immediately; relocation 0x0217fa80 registers it in the notice-state dispatch table after the scrolling and fade handlers.
evidence.uncertainty: Its empty body does not prove a more specific lifecycle purpose.

evidence.note: Forwards the embedded object at +0x1E0 to the empty preview drawing callback; the caller invokes it in facility mode 5/submode 6.
Empty callback reached by the facility resource-refresh dispatcher for mode 5/submode 6.
Allocates six arenas, a Window, 33 sprite transforms, a DisplayLayout and storage for eight linked canvases.
Saves text and display state, initializes canvases and input, copies the protagonist party slots and removes members with the tested status nibble.
Advances layout canvases, key repeat and Window selection, handles queued messages and dispatches the current shop state member handler.
Loads shopdata1.bin, stock IDs, localized shop messages, bg_shop2 and obj_shop graphics, then builds canvases and enables the gold display.
Resolves the selected item, builds a Party stat comparison for the requested member and returns its mapped integer or float comparison pair.
Finds quantity group 9, reads the two adjustment-entry positions and submits sprites with one-pixel pressed offsets from quantity flags.
Resolves the selected item, multiplies its adjusted price by the requested quantity and compares against carried gold at inventory +0xF6C.
Rejects insufficient gold, subtracts adjusted price times selected quantity, refreshes the gold display and sets the purchase flag.
Checks party equipment restrictions, swaps the selected equipment, returns replaced pieces to grouped inventory and synchronizes active network state.
Clears the purchase flag and adds the remaining selected quantity through grouped equipment or ordinary-item inventory helpers.
Maps the selected shop category to an inventory group and resolves the positive-quantity item using page and row selection.
Asynchronously loads item-name text, sets party, price and quantity arguments, starts the transaction message and restores the queued message/state on completion.
Chooses a layout for party size, checks equipment restrictions and current equipment, then writes member names and colored before/after integer or float stats.
For ordinary items displays each member name and carried-copy count plus total party quantity; hides this panel for equipment categories.
Displays the selected item name and restriction/equipped messages for one recipient, or its colored integer/float stat comparison.
Resolves the current inventory owner and fills an eight-row item-name/price preview from member carried items, ordinary inventory or grouped equipment.
Wraps the purchase page on input flags 0x10/0x20, resets the first list entry and refreshes selected item, comparisons and quantities when needed.
Runs item selection, affordable quantity adjustment, purchase confirmation, gold deduction, recipient selection, equipment changes and remaining-item delivery.
Maps the owner-group selection to a party member or shared inventory, resets page zero and calculates the ordinary inventory page count.
Initializes owner names and item preview, rejects empty owners and enters member-item or shared-inventory sale selection on confirmation.
Handles member carried-item selection, sale eligibility and confirmation, then adds sale proceeds and removes the sold item from its owner.
Handles shared ordinary-item selection and bounded quantity adjustment, confirms sale, credits proceeds and removes selected inventory copies.
Uses five-row category-grouped inventory pages with equipment comparisons, quantity bounded by grouped stock and gold room, and confirmed sale removal.
Empty drawing callback also reached by the embedded facility preview wrapper.
Queues model and rb_ev00 preview resources, saves camera vectors and orbit heading, installs Object3D in slot 0xA0 and advances screen setup.
Fades out, frees three preview arenas and load tasks, clears layer buffers, restores saved camera state and removes preview object slot 0xA0.
Builds destinations from a 24-bit zone mask, loads obj_rikka, bg_tm and str_ev resources and sizes the six-row menu to localized destination labels.
Waits for the initial text choice and queues the facility event plus a default field transition request with destination 0xC3BC on acceptance.
evidence.uncertainty: The default field transition and event queue are proven; the specific inn service and destination label are not established.

evidence.note: Handles six-row destination selection, cancel and paging, then queues the facility event and a field transition to the chosen destination or default entry.
Formats up to six destination labels starting at page times six, centers the Window, configures paging markers and attaches selection grids.
Computes cursor position from selected canvas tile coordinates and selected row within the six-entry page, advances and submits cursor animation.
Hit-tests the bottom left/right page arrow regions, wraps the secondary grid page and synchronizes primary and secondary selection indices.
Waits for queued scene work, fades out, snapshots VRAM mappings/backgrounds/render flags, runs overlay 9 and restores field graphics, camera and input afterward.
evidence.uncertainty: The invoked overlay number is 9; the specific user-facing modal operation is not established.

evidence.note: Loads the optional modal state at +0x1C and forwards to World_DrawStageObjectAttachments when present.
Forwards optional state at +0x1C to overlay 9 rendering refresh, which resets Window transfers and refreshes selected description canvases.
Looks up the selected action definition and dispatches its primary and secondary packed effect categories through two sentinel-terminated callback tables; returns whether either effect succeeds.
For flagged kind-one actions, interpolates packed percentage bounds against the caster stat. The revival handler compares the returned value with a random integer below 100.
Checks living eligible targets and clears status mask 2 through the shared status-removal helper; records remote results and synchronizes changed party members.
evidence.uncertainty: Mask 2 is treated as poison from its relationship to the combined healing/status-removal effects; no localized ailment string is embedded in this body.

evidence.note: Clears both result banks and applies capped HP recovery in the first and status-mask-2 removal in the second, preserving deferred remote-target results and synchronization.
evidence.uncertainty: The status-removal half clears mask 2; its poison label follows the field recovery effect grouping.

evidence.note: Processes dead eligible targets: action 39 restores half maximum HP, action 38 rolls an interpolated success percentage, and the special full-revival action supplies 999; invokes GameObject_ReviveAndRestoreHP.
Passes each eligible target character state and selected action ID to the permanent stat-item routine, records its increase, recalculates derived stats and synchronizes vocation and character state.
Always returns zero without changing results; the effect-dispatch table installs this callback for category 85.
Resolves the target object, tests and clears the supplied mask in its status word, writes success status 3 and returns one only when a flag was present.
Resets allocators, descriptors, background state, display controller, twelve canvases, task IDs, party lists, menu cursors, sound settings and transfer state for the shared party-menu object.
Stores two entry options at 0x2485 and 0x2486. FieldMenu_UpdatePartyMenuOverlay supplies them after initialization; the first selects the initial menu route during resource setup.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact meaning of the second entry option is not established; both are passed from the field-menu owner.

evidence.note: Cancels background tasks, restores cached background controls, clears canvas and sprite resources, pops the secondary overlay selection and destroys the eight active menu allocators.
Stores the frame delta, refreshes party snapshots, updates selection and auxiliary controllers, handles close input and dispatches the current menu state through the state callback table.
Clears and processes menu canvas buffers, prepares transfers, positions menu sprites and cursor, updates inventory decoration and draws the two visible auxiliary windows.
Commits canvas transfers and updates visible window masks and positions, configuring alpha blending when the auxiliary controller is absent.

Initializes text backgrounds, twelve canvases and sprite resources, queues and consumes sprite/string background loads, and advances to the normal root or alternate entry menu once resources are ready.
Examines the top canvas to choose how many paired or grouped panels to pop, restores the menu state from the remaining top canvas and rebuilds its text.
Initializes four output words to minus one and copies the selectable member list at 0x1C6E up to its count at 0x1C73.
Supplies the selected item key to the protagonist status-kind-nine script lookup, dispatches returned world commands and selects feedback message 0x232A on success.
evidence.uncertainty: The script helper has a recovered status-kind-nine contract; the particular item story or event is not established.

evidence.note: Looks up the selected item, handles travel and network-restricted special items, resolves its action definition, dispatches field effects, consumes successful uses and selects target or feedback panels.
Checks the selected action cost, handles field skills such as destination selection and chest discovery, dispatches target effects, formats feedback, and charges the caster when the action succeeds.
Accepts an explicit action ID, caster and target; applies party-wide action 34 or a single-target field action in menu state 23, selects feedback and subtracts the successful action cost.
Resolves item and actor names, chooses effect-specific success or failure strings from both result banks, expands wrapped feedback into the menu buffers and marks the message ready.

Scans eight carried slots for the chosen member or all members, compacts items bearing the retain flag, transfers the others into the shared inventory, handles the special item side effect and rebuilds item sorting data.
Locates canvas 33 and positions sprite cells 7 through 10 in four rows at fixed vertical spacing relative to its tile-scaled origin.
evidence.uncertainty: The four sprite graphics are not identified; their placement on the seven-slot command assignment panel is explicit.

evidence.note: Positions heading sprite 42 on canvas 26, then uses marked text rectangles on canvas 24 to place member-specific sprites and a packed-state indicator when canvas 25 is absent.
evidence.uncertainty: The packed indicator bit at member stats word 0x3C is unlabelled; the name describes its proven member/heading placement role.

evidence.note: Reads the selected palette index, copies the final color of its 16-color palette into scratch and transfers that color to main OBJ palette offset 0x11E.
When menu cursor display is enabled and no visible auxiliary window covers it, starts and advances cursor track zero, positions it at the selected canvas cursor rectangle and submits frames.
Copies the current BGM and sound-effect volume settings from their global controllers into the menu option bytes.
Collects shared inventory and active members carried item IDs, loads the localized item-sort resource, rebuilds its catalog against the item definitions and allocates temporary item/count arrays.
Alternates the two item catalog sort routines, snapshots and rebuilds shared inventory quantities in sorted order, and optionally restores selection to the previously highlighted item.

Updates the selected canvas formatting flag, dispatches its text builder into the shared buffer, replaces canvas text and optionally refreshes linked dependent panels before clearing the dirty marker.
On a selection-change result, validates touch selection, dispatches the current state text builder and replaces active canvas text; also refreshes dependent panels when the dirty marker is set.
Configures the current panel, builds the selectable-member list through its dedicated formatter and pushes its text canvas; the caller uses it to choose a member for a field command.
Adds cursor/frame markup and a header, then appends names for the selectable member list with eligibility palette colors and separators.
Appends cursor/header markup and two inventory options, adding the third option only when TreasureMapCollection_ReadMapCount is nonzero.
Positions canvas five to the right of owner canvas four, formats that owner item list and pushes it with page behavior derived from the current page count.
Formats up to eight carried items for a selected member or paged bag item names and quantities for owner four, then updates page indicators and canvas paging flags.
Builds and selects the current target-member canvas, binds the associated resource and creates canvas eight for the highlighted target status with placement depending on action selection.
Uses the current target cursor, cached member display names and action eligibility colors; chooses the active or selectable member list according to the action target mode.

Resolves the highlighted target and selected action or item, chooses HP, MP, stat or ailment templates, applies language-dependent status text adjustment and expands numeric values into the status canvas.
Positions the current panel to the right of canvas three, formats the paged secondary inventory at index-list offset 0xE04 and pushes a canvas with page behavior.
evidence.uncertainty: The secondary inventory player-facing category is not proven; the formatter distinctly reads index-list offset 0xE04 rather than the normal bag.

evidence.note: Reads the current recipient panel bounds, binds the companion resource and opens canvas thirteen at its right edge using the recipient inventory formatter, including an empty carried slot when available.
Empty return-only body. The type-fifteen resource vtable at data_ov004_021705f8 installs it in the position setter slot +0x1c.
Empty body occupies resource vtable slot +0x3c, the mode setter invoked by WriteNodeVirtualField3CByKey.
Initializes three filters to minus one; selected node keys 26 through 29 choose all, subtype, kinds one through six, or kind seven. Nested selections resolve subtype or kind.
Returns zero. Relocation at 0x021706e4 places it in the type-fifteen resource vtable +0xec, used elsewhere to retrieve linked list data.
evidence.uncertainty: The resource object does not provide linked data; the exact base-class virtual method name is unrecovered.

evidence.note: Walks to page times sixteen in the linked list, fills sixteen two-column grid cells, exposes text only for completed records, hides missing rows, updates page labels and selected details.
Requires the catalogue grid and page text canvas to have types seven and six before invoking the catalogue page population routine.

Expands and wraps twelve selected message strings into per-entry buffers, adjusts positions for multiline text, fills a two-column grid, hides missing entries and refreshes page/category presentation.

evidence.note: Resolves a type-seven grid, reads its selected coordinates, resolves their keyed cell and returns the corresponding node.

Requires type seventeen and invokes its +0xe8 virtual getter; callers use the result to find serialized item records by key.
Rejects slot indices at or above six and returns the forty-byte saved inventory slot indexed by page times six plus the supplied slot.

For each newly displayed item, chooses one of twelve columns with height below ten, increments its height, sets a stacked position and initializes a movement record toward the corresponding visible position.

evidence.note: Resolves the selected party member and item record, maps item kind to an equipment stat, transfers new and replaced items between equipment and inventory, handles status/network updates and refreshes party resources and menu state.

Allocates and initializes the shared 0xB8 session, snapshots resource flags and zone color, packs the current date/time, disables movement, allocates scratch storage and filters the selectable party list.

evidence.note: Initializes overlay-31 request mode 1 with menu buffers, stops BGM, waits 18 ticks, then advances the request and branches on readiness and completion.
Compares the saved offer timestamp with the session timestamp through the packed-date comparator; clears text buffers for expired offers or resumes the pending-transaction route.
Writes the inventory gold word at 0xF6C to numeric widget 201 and refreshes its associated display handler.
Resolves the selected offer and item definition, updates the item preview, selects equipment comparisons versus carried-item counts by item kind, and rebuilds the detail panel navigation record.
Rejects zero stock, insufficient capacity or insufficient gold; saves the offer item, resets purchase quantity and recipient state, and enters the purchase selection flow.
Walks six page-relative offer records, supplies item names, icons, remaining stock and unit prices, hides empty rows, then refreshes the selected detail panel.

evidence.note: Resets text arguments, builds descriptors for the selected recipient and linked name, resolves the offer or protected equipped-item name, and supplies purchase total and quantity.

Builds and submits the settings canvas using the formatter that renders independent music and effects volume choices.
Renders two rows of five selectable values from the music and effects volume bytes, with active palettes and a final return option.
Prepares actor and recipient descriptors, action or localized item names, result amounts and follow-up resource text, then expands and wraps the message.
Tests the bottom corners of the active canvas for touches, advances its wrapped page, marks page text dirty and synchronizes both selection grids.
Dispatches on menu screen ID to configure orientation, entry counts, pages and saved cursor indices in both input grids; disables input for nonselectable screens.
Initializes the six-command main panel, handles confirm and cancel, and dispatches to item, member, spell and miscellaneous menu states.

Maintains item paging and the item detail panel, resolves the highlighted item, and enters item actions or confirmation on accept.
Restores the saved four-choice item-action cursor, routes accepted actions and handles network ownership responses and result messages.
Builds eligible target choices, checks target availability, remembers the target cursor and executes item or spell actions after any network ownership request completes.
Filters recipients, accepts a party member or bag, handles immediate transfer to the bag and routes member transfers through carried-item slot selection.
Builds the separate inventory list, updates its item preview on selection changes and allows cancellation without an item action confirmation.

Lists available members, skips blocked members and queues SceneMenu_InsertStatusScreen; the extra row enters the combined party summary.
Creates all present member summary panels, stages the secondary display context and brightness fades, and exits on cancellation or touch.
Checks spell and skill tables, builds each caster field-action list on member changes and rejects dead casters or empty action lists.
Pages through the resolved field actions, stores the selected action ID, checks caster status and executes after a network ownership request if needed.
Resolves the chosen Zoom destination, validates travel conditions, spends MP or consumes the travel item, and fills the pending field transition with destination coordinates.
Maps available miscellaneous commands to automatic healing, member options, skill points, shortcuts, sound, saving and party dialogue actions.
Snapshots HP, MP and poison status, ranks available healers and healing spells, checks MP costs and repeatedly applies healing or poison removal until finished.
Drives the member command grid, opens six-choice tactics and palette selectors, toggles a member display flag and refreshes the status palette.
Writes the confirmed one-of-six choice into the selected member linked-state tactics field at 0x94C and returns to the member command grid.
Previews a palette choice, stores it in member state 0x56A, refreshes equipment if needed and reloads party palettes with network synchronization.
Waits for the skill allocation panel, commits the member result, gathers newly unlocked skill entries, loads their messages and names and recalculates derived stats.
Resolves successive unlocked skill entries and builds the corresponding name, category and value arguments for a formatted acquisition message.
Reads title IDs from completed script execution, loads gender-dependent ttlname resources and constructs persistent 0x244-byte notification records from script entries and localized names.
Clears packed notification flags, both text buffers and auxiliary words, then points the text field at its embedded 512-byte body buffer.
Clears the 56-byte heading buffer and copies the supplied string using the literal %s format; called while building earned-title notification records.
Loads skilltable.bin, drives the skill allocation screen, displays unlock messages and title_skl script results, then tears down temporary screens and returns to member selection.
Tracks the skill-point member cursor, refreshes its details and enters the skill allocation state for the accepted member.
Loads seven saved shortcut assignments, selects a slot for editing and commits the assignments when the final row or cancellation returns to miscellaneous commands.
Pages through unlocked ordered action IDs, rejects unavailable choices, writes the selected shortcut slot and rebuilds the seven-slot assignment menu.
Handles touch or left/right input for music and effects volume, clamps values to one through five and applies changes through RefreshGlobalModesAndDispatchOnChange.
Rejects saving during a network session, loads pen_tm animation resources, advances a staged save write and fades audio and graphics before returning to the outer scene.
Drives formatted action results and multiplayer completion or timeout states, waits for messages or movement, then restores the inventory, spell or miscellaneous screen and selection.

Subtracts elapsed ticks from the shared action wait timer, clamps it to zero and reports whether time remains.

Remembers the source inventory slot, navigates or touches a destination across pages, draws the source marker and swaps item IDs and quantities on confirmation; cancel restores browsing state.

Clears the serialized pattern table, count and flags, then resolves fifteen fixed token strings into glyph indices. CharacterFilterTokens.cpp identifies punctuation used by the encoded pattern matcher.

Consumes completed background loads, skips inactive/completed or still-loading phases, resets window transfers, uploads dirty backgrounds, and invokes the description and entered-name text refresh routines.

When a replacement preview has finished loading, copies transforms and compatible animation name/time from the displayed object, swaps active and staging pointers, optionally reapplies body scale and clears pending-swap flags.
