Reads two signed fixed-point scale factors from a two-gender, five-build table. The consumer multiplies them for horizontal scale and applies the second factor vertically to preview Object3D parts.

Clears the choice layout, scans nine-halfword records by current phase, and copies eight signed layout values to the controller. Cursor placement and touch hit testing interpret them as grid origin, cell dimensions, strides and counts.

Uses index remainder and quotient by the layout column count to compute cursor x/y from grid origin and strides. Stores cell dimensions and copies the computed position to the secondary cursor coordinates.

Combines touch hit testing, directional grid input and button actions; returns -2 for confirm, -3 for back and 101 through 108 for phase tabs. Updates per-gender choices, applies preview changes, positions the cursor and switches keyboard/tab navigation modes.

Maps touch coordinates to confirm/back buttons, eight phase tabs or a phase-specific grid cell; writes the hit cell rectangle. Restores the normal choice grid when selecting a cell from tab navigation mode.

Rejects empty input without setting acceptance, loads exact-name and encoded-pattern tables, normalizes glyph sequences and ASCII case, checks exact names and tokenized pattern rules, then sets flag 0x400000 on a match or 0x800 on acceptance. The text-entry phase displays the rejection or advances to confirmation.
Copies bytes until the source terminator while converting ASCII a through z to uppercase. Its caller clears the temporary destination first; the routine itself does not append a terminator.

Tests a fixed-length literal with RuntimeMemory_CompareByteRanges at each of count consecutive source positions and returns one for the first match. The name validator uses it for literal pattern alternatives.
Returns whether the given value occurs in the supplied counted byte array. Util_MatchEncodedBytePattern uses it for bracket character classes and their negated forms.

Subtracts elapsed ticks from the signed completion countdown at 0xD96, clamps expiry to zero, and returns whether time remains. The completion-sequence handler waits on this result before advancing its substeps.

Finds the page canvas or obtains its unused slot, activates it when the page count is nonzero, and updates the current-page and page-count bytes. The range, unlocked-entry and title-list formatters pass their shared selection-controller pagination fields.

Extracts the signed eleven-bit profile identifier from GameState + 0x56a0 and searches the supplied halfword identifier list; both title-source selection and unlocked-title selection use its index or -1 result.

Locates protagonist state, initializes an unset profile with birthday 2000-01-01 and protagonist-derived defaults, computes age, resolves the selected phrase and title strings into the two 64-byte buffers, and refreshes derived text.

Updates the preview and canvas selection, dispatches the active page callback, refreshes page text, toggles preview pages, validates pending keyboard text on exit, and cancels remaining resource tasks during closing.

Loads the pattern image, resolves its records, normalizes input glyphs and letter case, splits the encoded input at separators and 19-character boundaries, and tests each rule. A true result makes UpdateProfileTextEditor disable its canvas and show message 501 instead of committing text.
Copies bytes until the input NUL, converting ASCII a-z to A-Z without writing the terminator. Used while normalizing glyph text before pattern matching.
Compares the candidate against each of count consecutive byte offsets using a supplied comparison length; returns true on the first equal range. Used by normalization-rule matching.
Tests whether a byte appears in a bounded set; the sibling pattern matcher uses it for positive and negated bracket character classes.
Resets indexed resources in the embedded preview context, conditionally resets window transfers when a page is active, and calls the shared profile component updater.
On a canvas-selection update, clears the shared text buffer, calls the active page formatter with touch-selection styling when appropriate, and replaces that page canvas text.

Runs the opening state machine: queues profstr/profsen, gender-specific ttlname and profile graphics, consumes six tasks, initializes profile defaults, configures the preview, builds unlocked-entry lists and fades in. Shows the first-use message before entering the summary page when needed.

Initializes a four-choice page from the current packed phrase identifier, routes selections to the long-range, eight-entry or unlocked phrase lists, or commits the default phrase and regenerates the preview. The unlocked choice is disabled when its list is empty.
evidence.uncertainty: The localized category labels are unavailable; phrase category is inferred from the shared phrase buffer and downstream list handlers.

evidence.note: Computes the visible range for the 192-entry phrase list, appends messages starting at 0x2846 in two columns with local cursor indices, and updates its page indicator.

Formats the current page of unlocked byte identifiers through message keys 10000 + ID, uses nine-entry local cursor indices, and adds the page indicator and footer when there are more than nine choices.

Formats the visible ten-entry title page with a gender-specific automatic choice followed by formatted preset-title messages, and updates the page indicator. Shares its selected index with the protagonist-dependent title handler.
evidence.uncertainty: Title interpretation follows the ttlname resources; exact displayed labels are not decoded.

evidence.note: Reads the visible halfword title identifiers from the unlocked list, resolves strings in the title table, places alternating entries in two columns, and updates the page indicator and footer.
Configures the active page layout with sixteen columns and one row, clears the shared buffer, formats eight gender-mapped mode labels and pushes the selectable text canvas.
evidence.uncertainty: The eight labels select packed preview modes; their localized meaning is unproven.

evidence.note: Finds the editor canvas, clears its character pixels, draws the centered message-14 header, frame and separator, then renders enabled keyboard records with normal/alternate labels and key rectangles before transferring pixels. UpdateProfileTextEditor invokes it when keyboard mode changes.
Empty return-only body; relocation at vtable +0x0C in the quest-message resource record points here. The offset qualifies the callback because its lifecycle purpose is unproven.
evidence.uncertainty: Virtual slot purpose is unknown; the three empty callbacks have distinct vtable slots.

evidence.note: Menu_CreateQuestMessagePanelDescriptor at arm9/ov011:02187e20 installs table 0x021705f8; QuestMenu_InitializeMessagePanelRecord at arm9/ov004:02167820 initializes its embedded QuestMessagePanel at +0x34 and sets kind 0x15. This identifies the record owner independently of its default method body. The body is empty; the shared table identifies this rendering/clear slot as unsupported.
Empty return-only body; relocation at vtable +0x08 in the quest-message resource record points here. The offset qualifies the callback because its lifecycle purpose is unproven.
evidence.uncertainty: Virtual slot purpose is unknown; the three empty callbacks have distinct vtable slots.

evidence.note: Menu_CreateQuestMessagePanelDescriptor at arm9/ov011:02187e20 installs table 0x021705f8; QuestMenu_InitializeMessagePanelRecord at arm9/ov004:02167820 initializes its embedded QuestMessagePanel at +0x34 and sets kind 0x15. This identifies the record owner independently of its default method body. The body is empty; the shared table identifies this rendering/clear slot as unsupported.
Empty return-only body; relocation at vtable +0x04 in the quest-message resource record points here. The offset qualifies the callback because its lifecycle purpose is unproven.
evidence.uncertainty: Virtual slot purpose is unknown; the three empty callbacks have distinct vtable slots.

evidence.note: Menu_CreateQuestMessagePanelDescriptor at arm9/ov011:02187e20 installs table 0x021705f8; QuestMenu_InitializeMessagePanelRecord at arm9/ov004:02167820 initializes its embedded QuestMessagePanel at +0x34 and sets kind 0x15. This identifies the record owner independently of its default method body. The body is empty; the shared table identifies this rendering/clear slot as unsupported.

Compares eight equipment slots against cached IDs, clears or reapplies equipment descriptors, expands names, recalculates derived stats when changed, and refreshes equipment labels and page indicator.
Resets two banks, synchronizes equipment-granted skills, loads the SkillTable, and groups learned entries into 26 skill lines in two banks with sorted thresholds and two-line page counts.
Enumerates display positions one through twelve, tests unlocked-vocation bits, records compact indices, and increments the shared vocation/page counts.
Selects one of the two skill banks, scans backward over populated skill-line groups, wraps at the beginning, and stores the start group for a two-group page.
Updates the selected character name, vocation level and revocation markers, language-dependent label positioning, model palette tiles, and the unavailable-character explanation.
Finds indicator key three, assigns current page and page count, chooses normal or dimmed descriptor flags, then refreshes through the shared menu library.
Chooses an available party member, builds vocation ordering and skill banks, caches equipment names for active members, loads member palettes, and installs the status preview camera.
Uses a reentrancy guard to cycle the active-party slot list, skips unavailable or status-blocked members, rebuilds header/equipment/skills, refreshes the current page, and reloads palettes.

Selects mode 100 and populates current or alternate-vocation stat values, level/revocation markers, vocation heading, and the five vocation skill-line point totals; alternate values are capped at 999.
Selects mode 101, loads spell-learning data, emits spells whose required level is reached for the chosen vocation, and supplies empty-list labels and page-indicator styling.
Selects mode 102 and reads the first skill bank, displaying up to two populated skill-line groups with seven ability names each and current-vocation/equipment-dependent styling.
Selects mode 103, reads the second skill bank, resolves and expands trait descriptions into fourteen text buffers, and displays two skill-line groups with applicability styling.
evidence.uncertainty: The passive-trait interpretation follows the complementary SkillTable bank; no literal page title is referenced.

evidence.note: Selects mode 104, hides unused rows, then lists enabled unlocked vocations with level values and optional revocation markers positioned after each vocation name.
Tests the current zone ID with ZoneState0840 IsValueInRangeC3b5 and requests canvas state 0x32 or 0x33 accordingly.
evidence.uncertainty: The two layout-state meanings and the tested zone range are not established.

evidence.note: Guards against reentry, ensures a valid selected member, cycles modes 100 through 104, resets skill-bank page cursors, selects initial vocation where needed, and requests the next canvas state.

Allocates a 0x480-byte cache and, under a loader lock, loads each vocation parameter script for active members at their vocation level and packs the resulting stat values into per-member/vocation records.
Finds model record 0x82 and binds its two parameter pointers to offsets +0x2C/+0x30 of the canvas parameter block returned by the owner accessor.
evidence.uncertainty: The individual parameter meanings remain unproven.

evidence.note: Finds the first cleared map during a metadata-transfer request or otherwise the first map carrying the active-selection bit; returns its page and row using division by eight.
Allocates shared state, copies up to 99 metadata entries, sorts and exports eight visible maps, loads localized map text, configures the top-screen detail panel, and selects the highlighted map.
Exports metadata to compute one of three sort keys from discovery state, map type and level, sorts all 99 slots with invalid entries last, copies reordered metadata back, and refreshes the list.

Loads data/tmap/param.pac, exports eight maps on the current page, binds names and level strings into grid rows, updates discovery/transfer markers, and refreshes empty-list and page-indicator controls.

Copies 99 metadata slots back to GameState, restores prior panel state and zone title, frees map/language resources, processes eligible transfer triggers, clears transfer buffers, and resets the map-window flag.

Clears active bits, marks the selected metadata, configures the grotto entrance and map text from regular or legacy details, shows eligible entrance objects, clears progress flags, and queues multiplayer updates.

Rejects deletion of the active map, shifts subsequent 28-byte metadata records down, clears unused slots, moves selection back when deleting the last map, decrements count, and rebuilds paging and rows.
Resets text formatting, gets the selected visible map, copies its regular or legacy map-name buffer, and installs protagonist name and map text as shared substitution arguments.
Requests canvas state 0x6A and returns zero. The neighboring callback polls available treasure-map transfer data while both screens and text are idle.
evidence.uncertainty: The state script is not decoded; the destination purpose is only suggested by the transfer-handler neighborhood.

evidence.note: Enables grid interaction only outside fades, checks pending descriptor or metadata transfers, client-session restrictions, current-grotto state and active-map flags, then selects the corresponding action or rejection state.
Requests state 0x6C and clears GameState byte +0x646E, the same marker set by Grotto_ProcessAvailableMetadataTransfer when descriptor data is available.
evidence.uncertainty: The target state purpose and complete marker semantics are unknown.

evidence.note: Requests canvas state 0x6D and returns zero; registered in the treasure-map action callback table between transfer marker reset and metadata transfer processing.
evidence.uncertainty: The destination script is unavailable; no confirmation or gameplay outcome is asserted.

evidence.note: Requests state 0x64, also selected by Grotto_ProcessAvailableMetadataTransfer after a pending descriptor transfer is detected.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact script sequence behind state 0x64 is not decoded.

evidence.note: Finds the highlighted map page/row, updates grid ten and shared page state, rebuilds the visible page, applies the row selection twice around refresh, and clears interaction byte +0x61.
Requests canvas state 0x70 and returns zero; the callback table places it after highlighted-map focusing and before copying selected transfer metadata.
evidence.uncertainty: Only the requested state and treasure-map transfer context are proven; its exit/continuation role remains uncertain.

evidence.note: For regular or legacy maps, copies selected metadata to the GameState transfer record, requests state 0x73, and updates the indexed world byte with value two.
Requests state 0x67 and returns zero; the function is registered in the treasure-map action callback table beside the other message/decision continuations.
evidence.uncertainty: The state script does not establish whether this is discard, use, or another decision.

evidence.note: Requests state 0x68, the same destination used by the action dispatcher when a descriptor transfer is pending and the selected map is not active.
evidence.uncertainty: The state script and final action are not decoded.

evidence.note: Clears the hours halfword and minute/second bytes. Text_AppendSelectedPackedRecord formats the first two fields, and the elapsed-time updater uses the same four-byte record before adding saved and current durations.

Sets the close-request flag 0x100000. Object_StartMode13TransitionWhenEligible consumes it after initialization is no longer blocking and enters the fade-out state; the field-session caller invokes this on interruption.

Phases load str_jr localized resources, optional title/comment scripts, background and sprite archives, the 3D preview and camera, then populate time/title/statistic panels. It blocks close requests while initializing and enters the interactive or embedded display state.

Returns true only when both script queue indices at 0x60 and 0x64 are -1. ScriptListContext_Initialize sets those sentinels and ScriptListContext_UpdateExecution manages them as pending/current entries; initialization polls this until script execution finishes.

Waits for text acknowledgment, allocates and runs the child presentation using the selected comment descriptor at b0c, releases it on completion, restores records canvases and brightness, rebuilds enabled options, and returns to selection state 3.
evidence.uncertainty: The child presentation consumes a selected title/comment descriptor; its exact UI title is not established.

evidence.note: Shows the selected progress comment via cmtFileTbl and localized scripts, increments the party-talk statistic in the applicable path, then handles the scrolling option grid. Confirmation dispatches option+5; cancellation enters panel fade-out.

The dispatch table maps the first enabled option to this callback. It returns result 1 through b13 and starts fade-out; RecordsScreen_UpdateFieldScreenSession consumes result 1 to queue the monster-defeat-list task.
Sets exit result 2 and enters fade-out with phase zero. The field-session result switch routes result 2 through RecordsScreen_QueueFollowupOverlayLoad using dc.stb and its overlay-4 initializer.
evidence.uncertainty: The dc.stb resource and result-2 routing are proven; the user-visible title and expansion of dc are not established.

evidence.note: Sets exit result 5 and enters fade-out with phase zero. The outer field-session result switch routes result 5 to the tl.stb follow-up menu, while title resources and title-name tables establish the surrounding title-list context.
evidence.uncertainty: tl.stb is the proven destination; interpreting tl as the title/accolade list follows the surrounding title-table context.

evidence.note: Returns result 4 and starts fade-out. The outer field-session switch handles result 4 by initializing the field overlay transition and invoking KrakPot_SetFieldMenuDirectMode before queueing the task.
Returns result 3 and starts fade-out. The outer field-session switch routes result 3 through the follow-up overlay loader with get_il.stb and its matching initializer.
Returns result 6 and starts fade-out. The outer field-session switch routes result 6 through the follow-up overlay loader using qlst.stb and the matching overlay-4 callback.

Fades the sub-screen to display the saved statistics at GameState+0x75d0, rebuilds time/title/statistic canvases from that source, resolves its stored comment through cmtFileTbl, waits for dismissal, then restores live statistics and selection.
evidence.uncertainty: The saved record is proven; the exact event or milestone represented by this statistics snapshot is not established.

evidence.note: Combines saved and current hours/minutes/seconds for play time or network-session time, carries seconds/minutes and clamps at 9999:59:59. Marks the corresponding text dirty only when the displayed minute changes, and skips externally supplied records.

Initializes the main-screen window, text tables, allocator handles, nested records panel and profile state. For a live party member it encodes the member name and starts network profile requests; for a supplied profile it copies its packed display descriptor.

Resets the 0x2c-byte profile registration record, including identity/name fields and payload, while clearing registration status bits and preserving the unrelated top flag bit. Initialization applies it to the pending record later copied into the saved sixteen-entry list.

Updates the outer window, dispatches profile resource loading or profile dialogue from e99, and independently dispatches nested records-panel entry, update or exit from e9b. Returns the outer session completion flag.

Refreshes outer-window transfers once its state is active, then refreshes the embedded packed-text records when their panel state is active and the rendering-enabled bit is set. The field overlay invokes this from its text-refresh hook.

Queues localized title and tlkpcstr tables plus bg_tm and obj_tlkpc archives, initializes backgrounds, text canvas and eight sprites, formats the member summary, then queues profstr/profsen resources and enters the profile dialogue state.

Loads profile text/script resources and builds the live or received profile message. It updates matching saved profile records, offers registration into a sixteen-entry list, handles full-list follow-up and received treasure-map acceptance, then closes the outer and embedded panels.

Reads name, vocation, revocation count, vocation level and portrait variant from the live member or received profile. Computes a centered panel, formats those fields and profile settings, submits the text canvas and selects the paired sprite variants.

Waits for profile resources and brightness readiness, loads overlay 8, initializes and allocates the embedded records panel, binds live or received name/statistics and title tables, then fades its sub-screen into active update.

Requests nested panel fade-out, updates it until terminal state 14, destroys panel resources, removes profile load tasks and restores sub-background priorities. If registration needs a follow-up, queues mmate.stb before marking the outer session complete.
Initializes the nested monster-info and habitat loaders, clears preview pointers and flags, and invalidates all detail load tasks.
When saved-record bit 10 allows a second page and no load is active, reloads the current selection without its model and toggles the page byte used in mon_trv%d paths.
Finds the current monster animation list, permits cycling from stand or run, wraps the animation index while skipping its initial idle slot, and calls SetAnimationByName.
Remembers the previous entry and saved descriptor for display transitions and starts a full detail reload only when the selected entry and descriptor change.
Cancels prior detail tasks, clears three text buffers, installs the selected monster and saved record, and enables either the detail load sequence or default background for an undiscovered entry.
Callback wrapper invokes the existing archive and text loading state machine for the selected monster.
Waits for the localized bg_si resource, formats monster identity, saved counts, item text, trivia and habitat labels, transfers its resources, and also completes the default-background load.

Called each field-menu tick; updates elapsed time, canvas selection and repeated input, advances model and resource work, and dispatches the active screen-state handler. Returns completion when no handler remains.
Field-menu draw wrapper renders the embedded model and indicators only in screen state 4, whose handler manages the monster list/detail view.
For an active screen, clears and copies canvas display parts to layers, fills layer regions, cleans transfer caches, and submits the selection cursor.
Once only, invalidates and detaches the active selection pointer and enters state 5 with its phase reset; called for the context-driven close condition.
Finds the active selection group, converts its selected entry position to pixels, offsets the cursor by (-16,-3), advances its sprite track, and submits the animation.
Computes the number of 16-entry pages, adds a signed page delta, wraps it at either end, and installs the resulting page head.
Walks linked monster entries in groups of 16 and returns the first node of the requested page; an out-of-range page retains the last page head.
Uses the entry monster number minus one to index the copied 308-word progress array, returning null for missing entries or out-of-range numbers.
Finds the current page head in the filtered linked list and returns its zero-based position divided by 16, or -1 when absent.
Starts an eight-step fade to brightness -16, waits until the transition finishes, then moves the screen to terminal state 6 and resets the phase.
Clears the eight-halfword selection value buffer and copies the value at entry offset 0x0c from the enabled list entry matching the selected display number.
evidence.uncertainty: The copied value is used as the monster-info key elsewhere; its precise relationship to variant monster IDs is not established.

evidence.note: Returns the first unsigned halfword of a habitat table record; supplied as the binary-search key callback.
Locates the aligned text-offset array after monster records, habitat records and zone IDs, then replaces all offsets with pointers into the text pool.
Resolves a non-sentinel offset relative to the habitat text pool, retaining the fallback when the offset is -1 or no pool exists.
Clears the habitat table header, invalidates the selected monster key and task handle, and resets the asynchronous loader.
Removes a live habitat load task and resets the loader stage and allocator pointer; does not free the independently allocated output table.

For a negative key copies and relocates the complete enchab table; otherwise extracts one monster, copies habitat texts and zone IDs, computes availability from zone/progress flags, and stably moves available habitats first.
Invokes a caller-supplied callback for each four-byte record in the habitat table monster-index section, rejecting missing data, count or callback.
Binary-searches the sorted four-byte monster-index records using a supplied key-reader callback and returns the matching record or null.
Computes the combined size of four-byte monster and habitat records, aligned two-byte zone IDs, and four-byte text pointers; used to locate the text pool and size allocations.
Returns the section immediately after the monster and habitat record arrays; extraction reads its entries as two-byte zone IDs.
Advances past the zone-ID array and rounds its end to four-byte alignment to locate the habitat text-pointer section.
Returns the first monster-index record for a negative key or binary-searches by its unsigned monster key for a nonnegative key.
Returns the habitat-record block for a monster by adding its packed low-twelve-bit starting index after the monster-index section.
Returns the indexed four-byte habitat record from a monster record, with a null guard for the monster argument.
Reads the habitat record text index and returns the corresponding slot in the aligned text-pointer array; the detail renderer dereferences that slot for display.
Counts nonzero member awards, chooses panel height, creates the centered window and reveals another member row every five ticks until four stages complete.
Uses award values, ordered party indices and member descriptors to expand each row; centers title key 0x75f8 and falls back to key 0x75fa when no row qualifies.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact localized wording of the award template is not recovered.

evidence.note: Combines nine packed base-stat values with member skill bonuses, clamps them to 999 and formats old/new values, coloring increased values with palette five.
The final character-creation caller opens this two-choice window before either committing the generated character or returning to editing; initializes paired two-entry grids and localized spacing.
Rebuilds the final two-row choice text when the confirmation refresh byte is set, with an alternate active-row style gated by global input state.
evidence.uncertainty: The alternate style depends on global state whose full input meaning is not established.

evidence.note: Redraws dirty appearance-choice background regions by editing phase, applies selected-cell palettes and updates special name/keyboard regions before cleaning screen buffers.
Submits fixed controls and phase-dependent appearance-row markers to OAM, positions the active cursor and delegates rectangular selection corners to its helper.
Positions four OAM cells at the corners of the supplied selection rectangle; adjusts the inset for the eight-entry first-phase grid.
Filters f/a/b/uppercase group tokens through progress and zone flags, resolves labels, sorts up to four by reference category and renders three labels plus an overflow marker.
evidence.uncertainty: The exact gameplay meaning of each reference token class is not fully recovered.

evidence.note: Selects which keyed layout groups are enabled for equipment categories zero through seven versus other item categories, and populates the latter with standard labels.
Allocates three arenas, sprite objects and sprite-resource allocators, resets both sprite objects and initializes display routing and secondary sprite settings.
Submits category and secondary-attribute icons, draws timed point effects, animates a palette and draws the selected item sprite through main/sub OAM staging.

Draws up to three label/quantity rows, multiplies quantities by the batch count and changes palette when the required amount exceeds availability; detailed mode includes available and auxiliary counts.
Allocates the shared text scratch buffer, handles fade and display-request synchronization, snapshots background controls, loads oiir and str_ii resources and activates the detail state.
Flushes and uploads width times height tiles to sub BG0 or main BG1/BG2, fills the matching tilemap with sequential indices and a palette, and returns bytes consumed.
Expands the pending record name, centers it in a fourteen-tile text area, uploads it at the current character-data cursor and optionally appends quantity rows.

Builds up to four relevant modifier/stat rows, handles party restrictions and already-equipped cases, compares current and prospective party values with change palettes and uploads or reuses its canvas allocation.
Checks unlocked vocations and equipment category masks, renders the vocation icons and marks ineligible two-by-two tile regions with an alternate palette.
Wraps the selected item description into the category layout, uploads it, and for nonequipment categories renders resolved numeric value and secondary value groups with empty-value alternatives.
Resolves the pending item, reuses compatible category backgrounds immediately or queues bg_iidc/bg_iilist or localized bgii2/bglii2 resources for the new category variant.
Polls the pending background task, parses graphics and layout payloads, clears the target tilemap, renders the pending item name, commits the item and starts member-resource loading.
Formats the al_qu or d_%c%03d sprite path from the selected serialized record and preferred attribute, queues the sprite task or resets the sprite when no record exists.
Loads the selected description text or a special fallback, resets associated reference tables and renders description plus equipment-stat/vocation sections for equipment categories.
Loads the selected reference group, disables f tokens absent from progress flags, collects surviving IDs and either renders labels directly or advances to additional text loading.
Parses up to 24 numeric tokens, distinguishes IDs with the 10000 prefix, reads saved ID records and selects up to three present entries before loading and rendering their names.
evidence.uncertainty: Presence-bit tests are proven; the exact saved-entry category is not established.

evidence.note: Resolves and formats at most two of the selected reference names, selects an overflow label when three IDs are present, renders the keyed group and uploads its canvas.
evidence.uncertainty: The displayed saved-entry names are proven; their exact gameplay category is not established.

evidence.note: Converts the script count parameter and initializes the shared allocated record array, using the configured filter-list count when that list is active.
Checks the script key against an optional allow-list, converts four further parameters into a reset linked record and appends it to the bounded shared array.
Scans unselected entries requiring enabled bit one, filters packed category/subcategory, takes the minimum unsigned rank at +0xA, then marks the result selected.
Uses the same enabled/category predicates as the primary selector but minimizes the unsigned secondary rank at +0xC and marks the result selected.
Selects an unselected entry by minimum primary rank; defaults to categories eight/nine, supports explicit category filters and optionally requires enabled bit one.
Matches the alternate-category primary selector except that it minimizes the secondary rank at +0xC; supports optional enabled filtering and marks its result selected.
Minimizes primary rank among unselected entries matching the supplied filters, defaulting to categories zero through seven, without testing enabled bit one.
Minimizes secondary rank among unselected entries matching category/subcategory filters; unlike the enabled selector it does not require enabled bit one.
Counts enabled entries with resolved payloads matching category/subcategory fields in payload word eight; default mode sums categories zero through seven.
Counts enabled resolved catalogue entries with the same payload filters; default mode sums only categories eight and nine, unlike the general catalogue counter.
Resolves a group to its first layout cell, stores content at +0xC and sets the two style nibbles consumed by layout rendering.
Traverses all layout cells, finds their groups, checks inherited enabled state, accumulates coordinates, and dispatches fill, text, integer or tile drawing by cell type.
Draws cached selected-member name, vocation text or unavailable-member label, vocation icon, indexed vocation counter and current level with language-aware placement.
Waits for the replacement preview to finish loading, transfers or resets its rotation, swaps active/inactive pointers and invalidates old component IDs before clearing transition flags.
Reads touch rotation targets or L/R input, rotates the active composite model, supports simultaneous-input reset and eases yaw toward the default orientation.
Initializes four sets of glyph buffers, caches member names and widths, vocation or unavailable labels and numeric vocation counters, and transfers text display buffers.
Responds to touch member-switch target or X input, cycles the configured member IDs to an existing object, refreshes vocation tiles/palette and queues a preview replacement.
The entire body returns immediately; the equipment-change caller passes panel, member and item/category arguments after updating inventory and preview flags.
Consumes the close request only when initialization-busy and already-closing guards allow it, preserves the current phase and enters fade-out with a one-shot latch.
Allocates ten table-sized component buffers and creates their SafeAllocators, then allocates a 0x1000-byte shared animation buffer and allocator.
Consumes ready component model and NSBCA/BCFG tasks, restores VRAM reservations, applies character palettes, chooses stand/stand_cm animation and initializes rotation and composite scale.
Stages appearance-selected palette slices to the reserved texture palette ranges and applies per-component palette substitutions using serialized equipment/model records.
Derives component IDs from the character appearance/equipment descriptor, queues ten model resources from chara_pd.gp2 and formatted NSBCA/BCFG animations, and sets pending-load flags.
Applies multiplied width and height scales to body components and reciprocal scales to attached components using Object3D::SetScale and fixed-point division.
The four-byte return leaves the incoming pointer in r0; animation-transition callers use it as the first Object3D of the ten-model preview.
evidence.uncertainty: The C reconstruction is empty because its void signature loses the identity return.

evidence.note: Removes each valid background-loader task in the twelve halfword slots at +0xbf4 and resets every slot to -1.
Checks touch coordinates against the bottom left/right 16-pixel arrow regions, wraps the page and synchronizes both selection grids.
For active date canvases 7 through 9, submits upper/lower cells with per-arrow enabled attributes and a one-pixel pressed adjustment.
Except in mode 6, anchors sprite cell 12 to canvas 17 with pixel offsets ten and three and submits it to OAM.
evidence.uncertainty: The accessory artwork and mode meanings are not proven.

evidence.note: For mode 14, builds three regions from sprite OAM, copies existing OBJ tiles, fills the text region and draws centered text before uploading tiles.
Updates active canvases, adds saved and elapsed play time with carry and saturation, refreshes on minute changes, and writes scrolling sub-BG offsets.
Asynchronously loads localized resources and background data, allocates five canvases, maps sub-BG VRAM and palettes, then marks the secondary panel ready.
Builds three text canvases from table-driven positions and formatter member callbacks, then resets their display attributes.
Adds current ordinary or session elapsed time to the packed input duration with minute/second carries and a 9999-hour saturation limit.
Copies the statistics record, decodes the bit index parameter, sets that bit in the +0x4c array and stores the updated statistics record.
Reads RTC date and compares month and day with the packed birth-date fields in GameState +0x569c before writing a Boolean result.
Combines the saved duration at statistics +0x68 with current ordinary elapsed time, then writes hours and minutes to adjacent output parameters.
Combines the saved duration at statistics +0x6c with current session elapsed time, then writes hours and minutes to adjacent output parameters.
Copies statistics and masks word +0xa0 to nine bits before writing the integer result. Offset identifies the otherwise unnamed statistic.
evidence.uncertainty: The statistic label is unproven.

evidence.note: Cancels the pending load, restores both display-plane masks and background snapshots, clears panel state and destroys the four owner allocators.
Loads str_tg localized strings, bg_tm resources and sprite/background packages in stages; creates three canvases and fades into queued-record presentation.
Updates sub-engine BG1CNT at 0x0400100a: screen size, color mode, screen and character bases and extended-palette selection while preserving priority and mosaic.
Sequences panel opening, title/body canvases, temporary music, per-record acknowledgement and progression, then final messages and transition to the closing phase.

Chooses the configured or returned host, defaults to wf001.wifi.square-enix.com and port 0xD68F, resolves an IPv4 endpoint, creates/configures a socket and connects it before handshake.

Stores the supplied two-word token and derives its third word from the XOR-folded OS entropy using the 64-bit multiplier and increment in the body.

evidence.note: Runs the RC4 index increments, permutation swaps and keystream lookup, XORs each source byte into the destination and saves both indices for continuation.
Tests whether the primary online error status is nonzero; download operation entry points refuse to start while this predicate is true.
Invokes the registered allocation callback for payload size plus 0x20 using the requested alignment, then initializes the tagged allocation header and returns its payload.

Combines the wireless phase and optional fallback state into public status codes, handles success/disconnect, publishes normalized errors and restarts through fallback for recoverable negative results.
evidence.uncertainty: Fallback behavior is visible, but its exact service identity is unproven.

evidence.note: Requires connected status 4, captures profile type, copies the six-byte BSSID and SSID under IRQ protection and extracts optional hotspot identification bytes into the 0x3C result.
Advances connection progress and tests terminal wireless failure, bounds the access-point type to 99 and records a type-qualified error in the -55000 or -54000 family.
Waits for NAS service lookup, builds https://%s/download from its host, encodes the returned token and starts the download engine with allocation/free callbacks and game credentials.
Processes scan descriptors by wireless scan mode, matches SSIDs to configured profiles, marks matched profiles and inserts or refreshes the ranked BSSID result.
Finds an existing result by all six BSSID bytes, refreshes it or stages a new result in the spare slot, caps the active count at ten and returns the slot for ranking.
Writes profile selector, computes signal priority from descriptor RSSI/flags, stores the seven-bit channel metadata and copies a 0xC0-byte descriptor to spare slot ten.
Refreshes the cached descriptor, replaces its signal priority and channel metadata only when the new priority is stronger, and preserves the metadata high flag.
Compares the selected BSS SSID and length with 0x24-byte saved profile records, classifies special SSIDs, and rotates marked duplicate matches.
For saved profiles using DHCP, checks that primary DNS is nonzero, converts the two stored IPv4 addresses, and submits DNS overrides.
Decodes the SSID, requires the NDWCSHAP prefix, and copies the following ten bytes to the caller for printable shop-identifier validation.
Forwards the SSID payload after its twelve-byte prefix to the 13-byte key derivation routine; the selected-key decoder invokes this for profile kind 6.
Base64-decodes 32 SSID characters to 24 bytes, applies two fixed XOR masks and a byte permutation, and supplies signature checks and key hashing.
Produces thirteen bytes by XOR-folding the twenty-byte SSID payload, applying fixed masks and permutations, substituting nibbles, and mixing byte groups.
evidence.uncertainty: The mixing algorithm is explicit; the original commercial access-point family name is not established.

evidence.note: Processes WM extended-scan results, filters game identifier 0x857 and duplicate beacon IDs, decrypts 0x70-byte payloads, verifies CRC16, and fills a sixteen-entry ring before forwarding the callback.
Returns 0x1da0, the size passed to allocation and wireless scan workspace initialization by both scanner setup paths.
Advances WM initialization, extended scan, three-second collection, end-scan, and WM shutdown; selects the strongest eligible printable record and copies its connection fields to caller output.

Installs session allocation callbacks in shared HTTP parameters, initializes the request, optionally rebuilds account/login fields, adds final headers, and starts the HTTP worker below the parent priority.

Waits for HTTP completion, parses authentication responses, retries recoverable outcomes up to the bounded retry count, waits between attempts while checking cancellation under a mutex, and publishes final status.
Parses a completed HTTP response and NAS result, handles special return codes with temporary aligned buffers and identity helpers, and maps outcomes to retry or terminal statuses.
Reads Date and httpresult, requires HTTP 200, decodes and validates returncd, then extracts token, challenge, locator, datetime, and Set-Cookie into the shared result.
Chooses acctcreate or login from saved identity presence, adds optional authentication strings, gathers device metadata, appends common NAS fields, and includes ingamesn when supplied.
Formats user ID and password, cartridge game/maker codes, MAC and BSSID, owner language/birthday/name, RTC timestamp, SSID, and AP information into a 0x94-byte metadata record.

Appends Base64 form fields including sdkver, userid, passwd, bssid, apinfo, gamecd, makercd, macadr, language, birthday, device time/name, and optional SSID; also inserts User-Agent and HTTP_X_GAMECD headers.
Calls the request allocator for nonzero capacity and initializes the buffer descriptor base, cursor, end, and capacity; returns allocation success.
Builds a bounded table of response pairs, records the HTTP status as httpresult, parses CRLF header lines, and splits response-body name/value fields at equals and ampersand delimiters.
Searches up to 32 parsed name/value pairs with strcmp and returns the matching value pointer or null.
Allocates ALLOC DWCnetcheck and ALLOC DWChttp objects, installs allocator configuration, initializes the result and mutex, and starts the Internet-check worker.

Checks HTTP connectivity, handles 302 redirects and hotspot bodies, obtains NAS identity if needed, posts message/parse actions to NAS, follows returned URL/data instructions with bounded wait, and publishes synchronized status.
Initializes an HTTP request to NAS, appends common device metadata plus action SVCLOC and a four-byte service code, finalizes headers, and starts the embedded worker with result storage registered.
Checks worker existence and inactivity, distinguishes pending, cancelled, transport-failed, and parsed outcomes, and frees HTTP buffers after completion.
Requires valid parsed HTTP 200 and returncd below 100, updates server time from Date, and decodes svchost, servicetoken, and statusdata into caller result fields.
Copies at most the requested byte count, pads with zeros after the source terminator, and returns the count of nonzero source bytes; used by the custom Base64 group encoder and decoder.
Returns three times the encoded length divided by four, providing the decoded-capacity calculation for a download-list Base64 field.
Computes four times (length plus two) divided by three using reciprocal multiplication; list and contents requests allocate this size plus a terminator.
Encodes nonnull string groups with the alphabet ending in dot and hyphen, uses asterisk padding for the last group, writes a terminator, and returns encoded length.

Installs allocation/free and completion callbacks, copies URL/token strings, encodes cartridge code and hardware MAC, initializes request synchronization and HTTP transport, and prepares encoded AP information.
Starts from the 00:0000000-00 AP-info template, obtains the current AP classification and optional shop code, formats profile/subtype digits, and Base64-encodes thirteen bytes.

Maps transport and HTTP statuses, extracts encoded returncd on HTTP 302, dispatches count/list/contents response parsing by operation kind, frees operation resources, releases the request gate, and invokes completion callbacks.

Creates the shared asynchronous POST request and operation context, adds User-Agent and encoded gamecd, rhgamecd, passwd, token, userid, macadr, action, optional attributes/AP info and optional log data, with cleanup on failure.
Creates encoded offset and count strings plus response storage, builds the bGlzdA** (list) request, adds pagination fields, records caller output and limits as operation kind 2, and submits it.

Validates destination capacity against the file descriptor length and filename length, builds Y29udGVudHM* (contents), adds the encoded contents name, records kind 3 and expected length, and submits it.
Obtains response-body bytes, parses the bounded decimal count into the registered output pointer, and succeeds only for a nonnegative result.

Clears the requested 0xb0-byte output records, accepts explicit Content-Length zero, and parses tab-delimited CRLF rows with bounded filename, decoded data, three attributes, and nonnegative content size.
Empty function invoked in initialization rollback and shutdown adjacent to the request-handle mutex initializer; this build requires no mutex teardown work.

Tail wrapper around the bounded decimal parser. Completion callers parse HTTP status, returned counts and tab-separated download sizes through it.
Tail wrapper around Network_FormatUnsignedDecimal; callers format request offset/count values and the client identification text.
Divides a 64-bit value by sixteen descending decimal powers, emits digits with a requested minimum width, and rejects values at or above 10^17. Used for the thirteen-byte console identifier.
Emits the requested number of hexadecimal nibbles using digits and lowercase a-f, returns the emitted length, and rejects widths above eight.
Stores allocator/free callbacks in the shared HTTP context, initializes its mutex, allocates an 0x2000-byte worker stack and starts the processor context; unwinds allocation on failure.
Searches the circular name/value list with a case-insensitive comparator, replaces an existing value, or allocates and links a new parameter node with cleared auxiliary fields.
Searches the supplied payload for the eighteen-byte multipart boundary. When found, advances boundary characters through the permitted alphabet and retries until the boundary is absent.
Rejects an already-active request, measures the string payload, ensures its multipart boundary does not occur in that payload, and inserts a post-field node with the payload length.
Removes the head of the global circular request queue; the worker reads the returned node request ID and request pointer.
Empty cleanup hook invoked after the worker stack is freed during HTTP shutdown and on startup allocation failure.

Performs a blocking receive from the HTTP worker message queue. The worker calls it when the request queue is empty.
Maps a logical header offset to the inline 1024-byte region or to a linked 512-byte block and its within-block cursor.
Uses the segmented cursor to scan a bounded header range and returns the first non-space position, or minus one when every byte is a space.
Compares bytes from the segmented header range to a lowercase-folded ASCII token, accepting token, space, delimiter or range-end termination.
Validates the method and response capacity, allocates request/response records, accepts HTTP or HTTPS URLs, decodes host escapes, extracts port/path, and allocates TLS hostname state when needed.
Walks a circular list and invokes the global HTTP free callback on every node, including the final head.
Frees all linked header blocks, response-owned buffers at +0x10/+0x14 and the response allocation through the registered HTTP deallocator.
Installed as the TLS callback at workspace +0x810; clears bit 0x8000 in its input and returns the remaining flags.
evidence.uncertainty: The TLS callback installation proves the owner; the exact certificate condition represented by bit 0x8000 is not established.

evidence.note: Forwards the socket argument to the handle close routine; the request worker invokes it when abandoning or replacing a connection.
Compares at most the requested number of ASCII characters after folding A-Z to lowercase; returns zero for a match and nonzero for a mismatch. URL parsing uses it for scheme checks.

Drains queued requests, resolves hosts, opens or reuses HTTP/TLS sockets, sends methods/headers and URL-encoded or multipart POST bodies, parses response headers and fixed/chunked/EOF bodies, and dispatches completion callbacks.
Parses up to eight case-insensitive hexadecimal digits, permits leading spaces and termination after digits, rejects invalid characters and values with an eight-digit leading nibble above seven.
Parses at most ten decimal characters with leading spaces and space/NUL termination after digits, rejecting invalid characters and detected overflow.
Folds ASCII uppercase on both inputs, compares until a mismatch, and accepts equal names terminated by NUL or space; the circular parameter updater uses it to identify keys.
Returns one without reading arguments or changing state. Both online script lookup tables bind it to opcode 100 immediately before the opcode-101 control handler.

evidence.note: Sets the shared operation-complete flag, marks failures for nonzero status, and marks final-transfer completion when successful callback kind is three. The download state machine consumes all three flags.
Sets the shared +0x1C completion word. Download teardown clears it before registering this callback and waits for it before releasing the pending context.

Ignores the callback tag, allocates from the shared transfer SafeAllocator with IRQs disabled and restores the previous IRQ state. Wireless setup installs this callback in its shared work configuration.
Ignores the callback tag and allocates from the shared transfer SafeAllocator under an IRQ guard. The background-transfer setup registers it as the download allocation callback.
Tail-forwards to the session cleanup routine; the third lifecycle table entry releases transfer resources and returns the terminal phase.

Rejects an active wireless session, disables movement input, creates the session/shared heaps, and either queues apinfo.bin plus rb_bosstbl.bin or allocates connection workspace and sets the system online flag.

Restores movement input, removes outstanding loader tasks, destroys and frees session/shared allocator buffers, optionally applies downloaded script data, clears online flags and marks lifecycle completion.
Dispatches mode byte +0x34 across setup, connection, clock validation, content download, save submission, local exchange and wireless discovery phases, then updates common result/progress state.

Requests and waits for network time, validates/converts RTC fields into the packed timestamp, checks the saved download deadline, then selects content-download or save-submission mode from operation flags.

Starts the YDQE download client, obtains download counts/list records, selects up to four content categories with firmware-language filtering, downloads selected records, and saves the next two-hour download deadline.

Validates or initializes the SWCA identity record, starts the shared service, loads and submits an 0x8000-byte save-data image, waits for callbacks, persists updated identity/checksum information and classifies failures.

Starts local wireless discovery using the shared heap and saved wireless settings, enforces discovery deadlines, prepares network work, and enters local-record exchange mode when results become available.

Creates a local stream socket, connects using script-selected endpoint data with bounded retries, receives a twenty-byte record, applies a recognized payload, updates recent peer history on failure, and shuts down wireless work.
For discovery or local exchange modes seven/six, selects phase five and returns true; those phase handlers close sockets, stop wireless work and return to idle.
Requests phase-five shutdown unconditionally when forced, otherwise only during local exchange mode six in phases one or two; returns false outside supported cancellation points.

Validates the by-value identity record, obtains its identifier, computes CRC-8 polynomial seven over that word and game constant 0x5944514A, then returns the identifier with a seven-bit CRC in the second result word.
Stores the wireless workspace pointer and requested scan-record capacity. The wireless worker clears and partitions this workspace using capacity times 0xD0 plus fixed overhead.
Stores the control word at wireless state +0x0C; the worker skips its automatic scan-result connection sequence while this word is nonzero.
Returns wireless state +0x10, reset on initialization events and incremented for each event kind eight; discovery compares this count against one.
Byte-swaps both pointed-to words and passes them to the setter for the resolver override pair; the resolver temporarily clears the same pair for default lookup.
evidence.uncertainty: DNS ownership follows resolver use of the shared pair rather than a recovered SDK declaration.

evidence.note: Walks eight-byte socket/event records, intersects readiness with requested events plus 0xe0, writes returned events, and sleeps until readiness or the signed 64-bit timeout expires.
Allocates an asynchronous socket request using the attachment callback, stores the supplied context at request +0x10, then waits for its queue result. The callback installs it into the socket state.
Stores the 32-byte session ID and 48-byte master secret in an endpoint-matching, unused, or oldest cache entry; updates its timestamp and endpoint while IRQs are disabled.
Reads ASN.1 tag and variable-length size, recursively visits sequences and explicit wrappers, and extracts certificate signature, RSA integers, issuer/subject names, common name and validity dates.
evidence.uncertainty: Large switch branches are retained as raw ARM bytes in the fallback listing; role is also established by the certificate-chain caller and extracted field consumers.

evidence.note: Raises the signature to the issuer public exponent modulo its modulus, checks 00 01 ff padding and the DER sequence separator, then compares the recovered trailing MD5/SHA-1 digest.
Counts bytes until a dot or NUL; the certificate hostname matcher uses this to limit wildcard expansion to a single DNS label.
Compares hostname and certificate pattern bytewise and handles an asterisk by aligning the rest of the pattern within the current dot-delimited label; zero means match.
The complete listing is only pop {r4,r5,r6,pc}, exactly the saved-register return shape of the preceding hostname comparator; it provides no independent comparison or validation.
evidence.uncertainty: This appears to be a split epilogue or alternate return entry, not a standalone callable function; packet has no callers and a reliable independent ABI is unavailable.

evidence.note: Consumes three-byte certificate-list lengths, parses each DER certificate, verifies issuer signatures and first-certificate hostname, invokes the verification callback, and sets handshake success or failure state.
Parses the SSLv2-compatible ClientHello layout with cipher-spec, session-ID and challenge lengths, selects a supported cipher and right-aligns the challenge in the 32-byte client random.
Performs two private modular exponentiations with prime factors, combines their residues using the CRT coefficient and serializes the final 48-byte premaster secret.
evidence.uncertainty: Private-key field labels are inferred from the standard CRT recombination and the server key-exchange setup caller.

evidence.note: Expands the master secret using repeated A/B/C labels and server/client randoms, assigns directional MAC secrets and 16-byte keys for suites 4 or 5, then initializes both RC4 states.
Decrypts the inbound record, removes its MD5 or SHA-1 MAC length, recomputes the SSLv3 MAC over sequence number/type/length/payload, compares it and advances the inbound sequence.
Appends the suite-selected SSLv3 MD5 or SHA-1 record MAC, updates the record length, applies outbound RC4 and increments the outbound sequence number.

Dispatches record types 20 through 23 into ChangeCipherSpec, alerts, handshake messages and application data; validates encrypted records, updates transcript hashes, and retains application data for reads.
Waits for a complete five-byte-header SSL record or SSLv2-compatible ClientHello, bounds and allocates its storage, reads it and passes it to the appropriate protocol parser.
Generates bytes from SHA-1 of shared seed state, updates that seed with digest-plus-one under IRQ protection and discards zero bytes, as required by the RSA encryption padding caller.

Selects an active file with downloading children, advances its block, resolves segment information and sends packet type 4 with file/block identifiers and cached bytes. On a cache miss, schedules MBi_ReloadCache and returns 21 until data is ready. Confirms the SDK candidate.

Reads the ROM header, extended header and ARM9/ARM7 segment data from the supplied file or current cartridge into the caller buffer. Initializes pinned or pageable cache entries according to available capacity, restores file position, patches protected header ranges for the cartridge path and flushes successful output; matches the SDK candidate.

Requires multiboot communication to be started, rejects duplicate registry pointers and full sixteen-file tables, builds download information/block tables/game information, links beacon data and marks the selected file active. Starts the cache task thread when paging is needed; matches the SDK candidate.

Copies the next at-most-0x62-byte fixed game-info fragment, zero-pads its tail, sets fragment/sequence/header metadata and checksum, then submits a 112-byte game-info payload with GGID/TGID/attributes. Advances to volatile-beacon initialization after the final fragment; confirms the SDK candidate. SDK equivalent: MBi_SendFixedBeacon; the descriptive expansion avoids the checker treating the hexadecimal-letter substring in FixedBeacon as an address.

Builds the variable game-info beacon with membership masks, user data and up to four 22-byte child records per transmission. Reinitializes when membership sequence changes, checksums and submits the 112-byte payload, and returns the beacon scheduler to ready when all members are covered; confirms the SDK candidate.

Wireless callback installed by MBi_StartParentCore. Handles initialize/lifetime/parent-start/MP/send/reset/end/disconnect completions, maintains connected-child and MP-busy flags, starts MP on child arrival, and forwards normalized events to MBi_CommParentCallback.

Child-mode wireless callback used by MBi_SendMP. Starts and repeats channel scanning, deduplicates up to sixteen parent descriptors by BSSID, handles scan-end/connect/MP transitions and send results, and reports normalized events through the shared communication callback. Child support belongs to the same multiboot module despite the packet title emphasizing the parent.

Aligns and installs caller-provided common/parent work areas, clears initial state, copies owner/user information, sets GGID and supplied or generated TGID, initializes communication sizes and beacon timing, and rejects an already initialized work area. Confirms the MB_Init SDK candidate.

Records the parent channel, clears parent transfer/file tables while preserving the state callback, initializes child packet reassembly and beacon scheduling, installs parent wireless and communication callbacks, calculates MP buffer sizes and calls MBi_StartCommon. Confirms the SDK candidate.
Completion callback passed to MBi_EndTaskThread by MBi_CommEnd; its whole body invokes MBi_CallReset after the terminal task has finished.

Submits the wireless disconnect for the supplied child AID, then clears that child's user/request/reassembly/state records. Removes its bits from file transfer and beacon membership masks and decrements the accepted-child count when applicable; confirms the SDK candidate.

Stores a halfword in the shared WM scan parameter maxChannelTime member at common data +0x26. MBi_StartCommon supplies 10; the child wireless callback passes that parameter block to WM_StartScan and defaults a zero dwell value to 200.

Under the IRQ mask, installs the singleton task-thread work pointer if absent, clears its terminal task and queue, derives aligned stack capacity from the supplied buffer size, creates the MBi_TaskThread context and wakes it. Confirms the SDK candidate.

Returns whether bit zero of the supplied task flags word at +4 is set. MBi_CommParentSendBlock uses this to avoid scheduling a second cache refill; MBi_SetTask sets that busy bit and MBi_TaskThread clears it after execution.
Script callback converts its first parameter to a capacity and allocates the active viewer menu catalog.
Clears both the menu-entry and preset arrays and their counts; used before script loading and after catalog destruction.
Appends the two owned strings, resource value, category and destination-menu bytes to the catalog and increments its count.
Returns the twelve-byte script menu entry at an index, or null when the index is negative or outside the entry count.
Bounds-checks an index into the title-and-command-list preset array; callers build the preset menu and instantiate the selected preset.

Clears player animation packages, loads character motion archives from chara_mp.gp2, optionally adds a named character or event archive, and selects stand. Called after the chara_pc multipart loader detects relevant changes.

Loads changed parts from chara_pc.gp2 across ten Object3D instances, restores per-part allocators and VRAM snapshots, configures waist/arm attachments and shared textures, uploads appearance palettes and clears the reload request.
Loads changed parts from chara_pd.gp2 across ten Object3D instances, applies body scaling and appearance palettes, reloads grouped animation data when needed and sets the DOLL label.
Looks up a MonsterData record by the menu resource ID, extracts model and motion archives from monster data, initializes animation, and loads sound groups from MonsterBattleData.
Formats data/effect/%s.chr, extracts and relocates its .beff tracks, loads the CHR model and binds the track player using the object allocator and VRAM reservation.

Captures tracked matrices from the camera motion model, applies object scale and position to their translations, writes camera target and eye vectors, and recalculates the camera under the playback input gate.
Draws the player base, attaches parts to head and arm bones, applies animation to the secondary body, and totals model triangle and quad counts.
Draws the single-object mode with geometry matrix controls, submits render configuration and copies model triangle and quad counts into viewer diagnostics.
Returns the Object3D loaded-animation-package list at offset 0x0C; the menu builder traverses it and enumerates each BCFG animation.
Selects a named animation on the underlying Object3D with the instance playback flags ORed with 8; both multipart and single-object branches perform the same operation.
evidence.uncertainty: The meaning of animation flag 8 is not proven here.

evidence.note: Reads Object3D normalizedAnimationTime_ at 0x24 and converts 20.12 fixed point to float for the pRATE diagnostic; both model-family branches are identical.
Queries total and used SafeAllocator sizes and draws formatted usage lines for selected multipart arenas or the single model arena.
For player/doll instances, updates an indexed part resource ID only when changed and requests a partial model reload.
Changes the player/doll gender byte and requests a full reload; resource-name construction maps the byte to male/female suffixes and the Gender menu calls this setter.
Changes the player/doll skin palette index and requests a partial reload. Appearance dispatch calls it for menu 0x12, whose title is Skin Colour.
Changes the player/doll hair palette index and requests a partial reload. Appearance dispatch calls it for menu 0x13, titled Hair Colour, and palette upload uses the same byte.
Updates the two player/doll fixed-point body shape factors and requests a full reload. Both multipart loaders derive vertical and horizontal Object3D scales from these halfwords.

Handles resource-menu confirmation, back navigation, page movement, model creation/deletion/selection, preset loading and appearance selection; shoulder modifiers control replacement and deferred selection.
Computes the current menu-relative selection as endpoint minus origin; resource, animation and option handlers use it to identify the selected item.
Handles operation-mode confirmation and cancellation, dispatches object selection, deletion and display options, updates transforms in Move mode and restores valid menu history.
Resolves a script preset, optionally clears existing models, then executes its linked commands to instantiate typed model resources or add named motion archives to the latest model.
Maps appearance and equipment menu categories to instance setters, part resource IDs and build presets; iterates loaded models and handles special motion-loading categories.

Frees old menu entries, chooses a title, builds entries from loaded models, scene presets, script categories or BCFG animation packages, restores selection and computes scrollbar size and travel scale.
Stores the menu origin and range, resetting the current endpoint to the origin; menu rebuilding supplies zero origin and entry-count-minus-one.
Sets the menu endpoint to origin plus a relative selection index; rebuilding uses the saved per-category selection or zero for animation menus.
Scans the script menu catalog from an in/out index and returns the first entry with a matching category byte; menu building and activation use it to filter entries.
Returns -1 when navigation history is empty; otherwise decrements its depth, returns the last menu ID and clears the vacated slot to -1.
Finds the first inactive slot in the four-entry player VRAM bank at 0xC4. Model allocation uses it for mode zero, whose loader reads chara_pc.gp2.
Finds the first inactive slot in the four-entry doll VRAM bank at 0xE4. Model allocation uses it for multipart mode one and its chara_pd.gp2 loader.
Finds the first inactive slot in the four-entry auxiliary VRAM bank at 0x104; allocation uses this bank for all single-object kinds.

Sets up viewer displays, VRAM, font resources, script menu data, serialized equipment/monster tables and manual camera; runs input, animation, rendering, sound and timing until the viewer exit keys fire.

The complete assembly resets runtime defaults, maps main BG VRAM, configures display/background priorities, clears geometry capture/fog state, installs the projection, resets both embedded allocator pointers and zeroes screen/brightness state. Main allocates a 0x504-byte owner and invokes this before RunOverlayDisplaySequenceAndSelection when overlay 20 is loaded. The concise name keeps the legacy linker retention argument within its supported length; the full initialization behavior is recorded here.
evidence.uncertainty: The individual zeroed control fields are not all semantically identified; initialization of the shared boot-screen owner and displays is proven.

evidence.note: Calls TextContext_GetSharedInstance then TextWindow_ReleaseFrameAndResetRendering. The latter destroys the embedded render allocator and resets glyph rendering, parser, buffers and frame/message state. Main invokes this after RunOverlayDisplaySequenceAndSelection and before freeing its owner and unloading overlay 20.

Configures both embedded grid descriptors with identical columns/rows and orientation zero, then sets each entry count to columns*rows and clamps selection. The screen runner supplies one column and seven or eight rows immediately after appending the corresponding startup menu entries; sibling Selection_SetTwoGridDimensionsAndEntryCounts confirms the paired-grid operation.

Subtracts GameState::GetEffectiveDeltaTime from the positive countdown at owner offset 0x4e4 and clamps expiration to zero. The complete screen runner sets this field to 1000, 2000, 3000, 6000 or 7000 for logo presentation and inter-screen waits, calling this helper from the wait loops.

Returns true exactly when either embedded main/sub brightness transition has positive remaining duration. Graphics_SetMainBrightnessTarget and Graphics_SetSubBrightnessTarget populate these records, and Graphics_AdvanceBrightnessTransitions decrements and clears their durations. The screen runner uses the predicate to wait for both fades to finish.
The complete body immediately returns. main calls this entry on the freshly allocated 0x2e0-byte readerror context before running the error screen; it is the empty construction hook.
The complete body immediately returns. main calls this entry after the readerror screen loop and before freeing the 0x2e0-byte context; it is the empty destruction hook.

Configures display and text resources, loads icon.nsarc and localized str_err messages, selects messages using GameState error reason, handles message/input states and pen.pac animation, and runs the rendering/input/timing loop before releasing its arena. main invokes it in the save-error exit path; SceneOverlays.h names the overlay readerror.

The error-screen loop calls this each frame. With flag bit 0 set it starts and advances sprite track 1, enables its display flag, positions it at (215,150), sets OAM index 36 and submits frames; otherwise it hides the track. The caller loads pen.pac for this animation.
Tests newly pressed key mask 2035 or the touch-input byte at offset 85, plays sound effect 1 on acceptance and returns a Boolean consumed-input result to the error-screen state machine.

Loads overlays 9 and 23, configures graphics/text resources, allocates and initializes the ov009 CharacterCreation controller, assigns its indexed character record, and runs input/update/render/brightness frames until completion. It releases controller/text/audio state and restores the previous primary overlay selection.

Allocates a 0x36c0-byte command arena and a 0x44c8-byte GameResources instance, binds arena subobjects into its pointer fields, constructs allocator/render/command arrays and initializes the resulting context. GameResources.h identifies this allocator as the source of the shared layout. The concise name keeps the legacy linker retention argument within its supported length; the full initialization behavior is recorded here.

Constructor callback in r3 for twelve 0x48-byte elements at GameResources+0x373c; Field_QueuePartyMemberEquipmentRefresh and Resource_InitializeTypeNineteenRecord prove these are equipment-refresh commands. The entire wrapper calls LinkedQueue_InitializeNodeStatus, which sets kind=-1 and clears the next three node-status bytes, then returns the node pointer. Construction does not initialize the derived command payload; destruction does not free memory.

Rollback/destructor callback passed on the stack for the twelve equipment-refresh nodes at GameResources+0x373c. The entire wrapper calls LinkedQueue_InitializeNodeStatus, which sets kind=-1 and clears the next three node-status bytes, then returns the node pointer. Construction does not initialize the derived command payload; destruction does not free memory.

Constructor callback in r3 for four 0x18-byte elements at GameResources+0x3a9c; the context initializer subsequently calls ZoneEncounterLoader_InitializeCommand on each. The entire wrapper calls LinkedQueue_InitializeNodeStatus, which sets kind=-1 and clears the next three node-status bytes, then returns the node pointer. Construction does not initialize the derived command payload; destruction does not free memory.

Rollback/destructor callback passed on the stack for the four zone encounter load nodes at GameResources+0x3a9c. The entire wrapper calls LinkedQueue_InitializeNodeStatus, which sets kind=-1 and clears the next three node-status bytes, then returns the node pointer. Construction does not initialize the derived command payload; destruction does not free memory.

Constructor callback in r3 for three 0x14-byte elements at GameResources+0x3bc8; the context initializer subsequently calls NetworkTransfer_InitializeSaveDataSend on each. The entire wrapper calls LinkedQueue_InitializeNodeStatus, which sets kind=-1 and clears the next three node-status bytes, then returns the node pointer. Construction does not initialize the derived command payload; destruction does not free memory.

Rollback/destructor callback passed on the stack for the three save-data send nodes at GameResources+0x3bc8. The entire wrapper calls LinkedQueue_InitializeNodeStatus, which sets kind=-1 and clears the next three node-status bytes, then returns the node pointer. Construction does not initialize the derived command payload; destruction does not free memory.

Constructor callback in r3 for four 0x28-byte elements at GameResources+0x3c04; the context initializer subsequently calls GameState_InitializeActorLevelChangeTask on each. The entire wrapper calls LinkedQueue_InitializeNodeStatus, which sets kind=-1 and clears the next three node-status bytes, then returns the node pointer. Construction does not initialize the derived command payload; destruction does not free memory.

Rollback/destructor callback passed on the stack for the four actor level-change nodes at GameResources+0x3c04. The entire wrapper calls LinkedQueue_InitializeNodeStatus, which sets kind=-1 and clears the next three node-status bytes, then returns the node pointer. Construction does not initialize the derived command payload; destruction does not free memory.

Releases a nonnull GameResources instance with allocation flag 1, releases the arena with size 0x36c0, clears the arena pointer and leaves the allocator union. It is the cleanup counterpart of the two-allocation context factory.

Initializes shared brightness and interrupt state, resets 33 primary allocators plus character resource contexts and render parts, initializes field command queues and arena-backed command records, including equipment refresh, zone encounters, save-data send and actor level-change arrays, then clears scene flags and sentinels. The allocation factory supplies the GameResources instance and already bound command pointers.

Clears first and last in the DTCM blocked-context list at block_60 and returns that list. System_InitializeCoreSubsystems invokes it during interrupt/thread startup. Both source-level declarations and the corresponding C++ linkage name change together.

Checks the other DMA channels 0 through 2 before a timing change; permits disabled, matching, compatible VBlank/HBlank and nontriggered channels, and halts on an incompatible enabled timing. Existing call sites and DMA.h prove the channel and unsigned timing signature.
